title: # Akamai Bot Manager blocks CloakBrowser even with navigator.webdriver correctly hidden, humanize/geoip/fingerprint flags set, and Pro binary
body:
## Summary

On a page protected by Akamai Bot Manager, CloakBrowser gets blocked ~100% of the time on the Free tier and ~75% of the time on Pro, while a plain, unpatched Playwright-launched Chromium with only `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` gets through ~50% of the time — under identical proxy/IP conditions. Since CloakBrowser already reports `navigator.webdriver === false` correctly on both tiers, the gap isn't explained by that specific signal, and points to some other detectable characteristic of the CloakBrowser binary/session itself.

## Environment

- `cloakbrowser` npm package: 0.5.1 (also reproduced after upgrading to Pro, Chromium 151.0.7922.108.3)
- Free tier binary: Chromium 146.0.7680.177.5 (58 patches)
- Pro tier binary: Chromium 151.0.7922.108.3 (73 patches)
- OS: Windows 11 x64
- Proxy: residential rotating proxy (Decodo), sticky session per attempt, fresh IP each attempt
- Target: a page behind Akamai Bot Manager (`server: AkamaiGHost`, `bm_so`/`bm_lso`/`ak_bmsc`/`bm_s` cookies present on the response — confirmed Bot Manager, not a generic WAF rule)

## What we tested

All attempts used a fresh residential proxy IP (different country/ASN each time — confirmed via `ipinfo.io`, saw genuine major ISPs: Comcast, Cox, Verizon, TDS Telecom, EPB Fiber, etc., not datacenter ranges), same target URL, same `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` navigation.

**Config A — CloakBrowser Free:**
```js
await launch({
  headless: false,
  humanize: true,
  proxy, geoip: true,
  args: ['--fingerprint-noise=false', '--fingerprint-windows-font-metrics'],
})
```
Result: **0/13+ succeeded** (100% blocked, `403` from `AkamaiGHost`, "Page Unavailable" custom error page).

**Config B — CloakBrowser Pro** (same config as A, after setting `CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY`):
Result: **2/8 succeeded** (~25%).

**Config C — CloakBrowser Pro + `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` + `ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--enable-automation']`:**
Result: **1/8 succeeded** (~12%, i.e. no improvement over B, possibly slightly worse — within noise for this sample size).

**Config D — plain Playwright, real Chrome binary (not CloakBrowser), same proxy pattern, `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` + `ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--enable-automation']`:**
```js
await chromium.launch({
  executablePath: '<real Chrome / Playwright-managed Chromium>',
  headless: false,
  proxy,
  args: ['--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled'],
  ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--enable-automation'],
})
```
Result: **3/6 succeeded (50%)**, confirmed via `navigator.webdriver === false` on every successful attempt.

**Controlled A/B (same bare proxy username in both arms, only automation-hiding flag toggled):**
| Group | webdriver | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A — no automation-hiding flag | `true` | 0/6 |
| B — with automation-hiding flag | `false` | 3/6 |

This confirms hiding the automation signal matters a lot in general — but CloakBrowser (which already hides it) still underperforms plain Chrome with the same signal hidden.

## Verified: CloakBrowser already hides the obvious automation tells

```js
const browser = await launch({ headless: false, humanize: true })
const page = await browser.newPage()
await page.goto('https://example.com')
console.log(await page.evaluate(() => navigator.webdriver))                 // false
console.log(await page.evaluate(() => !!window.chrome?.runtime))            // false
console.log(await page.evaluate(() => Object.keys(window).filter(k => k.startsWith('cdc_')).length)) // 0
```
All clean on both Free and Pro. So whatever Akamai is keying on here isn't `navigator.webdriver`, `window.chrome.runtime`, or the classic `$cdc_` markers.

## Question / askF

Given `navigator.webdriver` is already hidden correctly, what else might differ between CloakBrowser's launched Chromium and a plain Playwright-launched Chromium that a sophisticated, well-resourced detector (Akamai Bot Manager) could be keying on? Possibilities we haven't been able to test ourselves:
- A consistent low-level trace from the C++ patch injection itself (timing, a specific JS engine snapshot artifact, etc.)
- TLS/JA3/JA4 fingerprint differences between the CloakBrowser binary and stock Chrome-for-Testing
- Something detectable in the binary's version/build metadata exposed at the network or Client Hints level

Would appreciate any insight into whether this is a known limitation, or something worth investigating further — happy to share more detail (redacted proxy credentials, full request/response headers, HAR files) if useful.

title: macOS v148+ OfflineAudioContext output remains identical across --fingerprint seeds
body:
Description:

This appears to be related to #181. The maintainer response on #181 explained
that the v145 macOS binary predates the seed-based audio noise system. Issue
#318 later stated that macOS binaries shipped again starting with v148, but
the current macOS builds still produce identical `OfflineAudioContext` output
for different fingerprint seeds.

With fingerprint noise enabled, the macOS build does not vary the rendered
`OfflineAudioContext` samples when the fingerprint seed changes. Canvas,
WebGL, screen, and hardware values do vary as expected, so the fingerprint
seed is reaching the browser and other noise paths are active.

Expected: the same seed should produce a stable audio fingerprint, while
different seeds should produce different rendered audio values on supported
macOS builds. If audio noise is not yet supported on macOS, the release notes
should state that explicitly and identify the first supported build.

CloakBrowser version: `0.5.9` (Python wrapper); tested macOS Pro Chromium builds:
`148.0.7778.215.5`, `150.0.7871.114.3`, and `151.0.7922.108.3`

Wrapper: Python

Environment: macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple M4, arm64, not using Docker

Launch options:

The only values changed between runs were the fingerprint seed and, in one
control, the platform value. Noise was enabled and `--fingerprint-noise=false`
was not passed.

```text
--fingerprint=31415
--fingerprint-platform=macos
--fingerprint-noise=true
```

```text
--fingerprint=27182
--fingerprint-platform=macos
--fingerprint-noise=true
```

The same behavior was observed with `--fingerprint-platform=windows` on the
same macOS host.

Tested with a different IP or proxy? No (not applicable; this is a local
OfflineAudioContext rendering result)

Works outside Docker / on host machine? Not using Docker

Steps to reproduce:

1. Launch CloakBrowser on macOS with the first argument set above.
2. Evaluate the following script and record the returned `sha256` and
   `absoluteSum`.
3. Close the browser, launch again with the second seed, and evaluate the same
   script.

```javascript
async () => {
  const digest = async (value) => {
    const bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(String(value));
    const hash = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', bytes);
    return Array.from(new Uint8Array(hash), b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
  };

  const context = new OfflineAudioContext(1, 5000, 44100);
  const oscillator = context.createOscillator();
  oscillator.type = 'triangle';
  oscillator.frequency.value = 10000;
  const compressor = context.createDynamicsCompressor();
  compressor.threshold.value = -50;
  compressor.knee.value = 40;
  compressor.ratio.value = 12;
  compressor.attack.value = 0;
  compressor.release.value = 0.25;
  oscillator.connect(compressor);
  compressor.connect(context.destination);
  oscillator.start(0);

  const rendered = await context.startRendering();
  const samples = Array.from(rendered.getChannelData(0)).slice(4500);
  return {
    sha256: await digest(samples.join(',')),
    absoluteSum: samples.reduce((total, value) => total + Math.abs(value), 0),
  };
}
```

Error output / screenshots:

No browser error is reported. The output is identical for both seeds:

```text
seed=31415  sha256=c9b528371839b0cbd8d8aeac448f000535b14af6e3f492aa3f4764156753963b
             absoluteSum=124.04347624466754
seed=27182  sha256=c9b528371839b0cbd8d8aeac448f000535b14af6e3f492aa3f4764156753963b
             absoluteSum=124.04347624466754
```

Dockerfile (if applicable):

N/A

Additional notes:

- This is reproducible on the v148, v150, and v151 macOS builds listed above,
  not only the v145 build discussed in #181.
- The result is unchanged with noise enabled, with noise omitted (default), or
  with `--fingerprint-platform=windows` on macOS.
- As a control, canvas and WebGL values changed between the same seeds,
  showing that the fingerprint seed and renderer noise paths are active.
- Passing `--fingerprint-noise=false` also returns the native audio, which is
  expected according to the documentation.
- Docker/Linux is reported to include audio noise support, but this report is
  specifically about the native macOS builds.
- Could you confirm whether the seed-based offline-audio patch is included in
  the v148+ macOS binaries? If it is not, please document the limitation or
  provide a macOS build with the patch. If it is intended to be included,
  please investigate why `AudioBuffer.getChannelData()` remains identical
  across seeds.

body:
Description: <!-- What happened? What did you expect? -->

The latest stable CloakBrowser Pro binaries on macOS and Linux do not pass a clean IPHey Browser fingerprint check.

Expected:

- Identity verdict: `Trustworthy`
- MX score: `100`
- Browser diagnostic signals: none

Actual:

### macOS V150

- MX score: `90`
- Browser diagnostic:
  - `Detected an inconsistent browser fingerprint (meteor)`

### Linux V151

- Identity verdict: `Unreliable`
- MX score: `70`
- Browser diagnostics:
  - `Detected an inconsistent browser fingerprint (meteor)`
  - `Detected an inconsistent browser fingerprint (butterfly)`

The Linux result reproduced across three fresh profiles with different fingerprint seeds.

A stock Chrome control on the same macOS host and network returned `Trustworthy`, MX score `100`, and no Browser signals in three fresh-profile runs.

CloakBrowser version: <!-- pip show cloakbrowser / npm list cloakbrowser -->

### macOS

- Binary: `150.0.7871.114.3` Pro

Tested with a different IP or proxy? <!-- Yes (same result) / Yes (works with different IP) / No -->

The Linux build failed IPHey using both direct egress and a configured proxy. No IP addresses, proxy endpoints, or credentials are included in this report.

The direct Linux run passed the separate IP, VPN, WebRTC, OS, and architecture-coherence checks. The named IPHey failures were specifically reported under Browser diagnostics.

Works outside Docker / on host machine? <!-- Yes / No / Not using Docker -->

### macOS

Not using Docker. The failure occurs on a native macOS host.

### Linux

Not yet tested as an uncontainerized Linux process.

The Docker host uses native x86_64 execution without QEMU, Rosetta, TCG, or other CPU emulation. Browser and network architecture checks agreed on x86/amd64.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Install the applicable CloakBrowser npm wrapper.
2. Configure a valid Pro license.
3. Pin the exact binary:
   - macOS: `150.0.7871.114.3`
   - Linux: `151.0.7922.108.2`
4. Create a completely fresh browser profile.
5. Generate a fresh fingerprint seed.
6. Launch a headed persistent context.
7. On Linux, use native x86_64 execution, Xvfb, real Windows fonts, and the Windows persona.

- Native `linux/amd64` execution
- Real Windows fonts available through fontconfig

The complete application Dockerfile is not required to reproduce the issue. A minimal reproduction can launch the pinned binary under Xvfb using the options above.

Additional notes:

- Fingerprint seed

title: humanScrollIntoView never scrolls the x axis: clicks on horizontally-overflowing pages always fail with "covered by <none>"
body:
### Summary `humanScrollIntoView` only ever moves the **y** axis, so a humanized click on an element that sits off the right edge of a horizontally-overflowing page can never succeed. It fails with a message that points at the wrong cause, and it fails on every attempt rather than intermittently. ### What happens `click_target` aims at a point inside the element's box; `check_pointer_events` hit-tests that point with `document.elementFromPoint`. A point outside the viewport returns `null`, and `build_pointer_js` maps that to `covering: 'none'`: ``` ElementNotReceivingEventsError: Element '#btnEntrar' failed pointer_events check: element is covered by ``` Two things make it hard to diagnose: 1. **"covered by ``" reads like an overlay, and there isn't one.** Nothing is on top of the element — the point is simply not on screen. I went looking for a z-index culprit that did not exist. 2. **It is deterministic.** The coordinate never becomes reachable, so the retry loop re-tests the same dead point until the click timeout and then throws. Every attempt fails identically, each burning the full 30 s. ### Why the x axis is never touched - `_is_in_viewport` compares only `bounds["y"]` and `bounds["height"]` - `_smooth_wheel` sends `raw.wheel(0, delta)` - all eleven `scroll_*` knobs in `HumanConfig` are y-axis knobs (`scroll_target_zone` is a fraction of viewport *height*) - `Locator.scroll_into_view_if_needed()` is patched to the same routine so there is no call and no setting that moves x. (`ElementHandle.scroll_into_view_if_needed` is *not* patched and does fix both axes — but using it means the engine's own scroll then sees the element inside `scroll_target_zone` and skips, which removes the humanized pointer travel from before the click.) Interestingly the Puppeteer port already has the primitive: `smoothWheel(raw, delta, cfg, axis: 'x' | 'y')`, used by the `page.mouse.wheel` wrapper. The scroll-into-view path just never calls it with `'x'`. ### Reproduction ```html
left
``` With a viewport narrower than ~1600 px, `page.click('#target')` throws `ElementNotReceivingEventsError ... covered by ` after the full timeout. Real-world instance, on a government portal whose auth page lays two panels in a row that does not wrap (document held at ~1615 CSS px, fingerprinted viewport 945 px): ``` check_pointer_events selector=#btnEntrar x=1257 y=630 viewport={"w": 945, "h": 1000, "sx": 0, "sy": 518} -> ElementNotReceivingEventsError: ... covered by ``` `sy: 518` shows the vertical scroll worked perfectly — the page is at its bottom and y=630 is comfortably inside the window. `sx: 0` is the bug. 15 of 15 runs failed this way. ### Version cloakbrowser 0.5.8 (Python, sync API), Chromium headless. The same gap is present in `scroll_async.py`, `js/src/human/scroll.ts`, `js/src/human-puppeteer/scroll.ts` and `dotnet/src/CloakBrowser/Human/HumanScroll.cs`. ### Suggested fix After the existing vertical pass, if the box is still outside the viewport horizontally, centre it with a horizontal wheel burst and re-read the box — leaving the vertical logic, the target zone and the `did_scroll` semantics untouched. Containment rather than a zone on the x axis (the target zone is a vertical, reading-position idea), and bail when the page is already pinned at its horizontal boundary, in the spirit of 5494ac1. I have this implemented and tested across Python (sync + async), both JS ports and .NET, and I'm happy to open a PR. Two design questions I'd rather you decided first: 1. Do you want a separate `scroll_target_zone_x` knob, or is plain containment right? 2. The fix needs `scrollX` / `maxX`, which widens the .NET `IHumanScrollPage.GetScrollStateAsync` tuple to `(double Y, double MaxY, double X, double MaxX)?`. Happy to do that differently if you'd rather not change that interface. ### Note for anyone measuring this `mouse.wheel` returns before the compositor applies the scroll, so `window.scrollX` read straight afterwards is still the old value. Measured that way, `wheel(dx, 0)` looks like it does nothing and `Shift`+`wheel(0, dy)` looks like the only thing that moves x. Both readings are wrong. Polling until the position stops changing: | gesture | both axes overflow | x-only overflow | |---|---|---| | `wheel(300, 0)` | sx 300 | sx 300 | | `wheel(0, 300)` | sy 300 | nothing | | `Shift` + `wheel(0, 300)` | sx 300 | sx 300 |

title: [Bug][Windows] Fingerprint anti_detect_browser persists on Chromium 151 with documented flags
body:
Description: Fingerprint Pro Playground reports `anti_detect_browser=true` on native Windows with latest free-key binary `151.0.7922.108.2`, official `cloakbrowser` 0.5.8, and documented flags. Expected current 148+ binary with `noise=false` and Windows font metrics to clear Browser Tampering, as described in README and prior maintainer comments. Actual result keeps `anomaly_score=0` while independent antidetect ML remains positive at 0.9096–0.9938.

CloakBrowser version: `cloakbrowser@0.5.8`; binary `151.0.7922.108.2`

Wrapper: JavaScript, Node.js 20.19.6

Environment: Windows 11 x64 native; headed; direct residential ISP connection without proxy/VPN; runtime timezone `Asia/Saigon`; tested at https://demo.fingerprint.com/playground on 2026-08-24. `mmdb-lib` installed and GeoIP resolved successfully. Playground returned `proxy=false`, `vpn=false`, `bot=not_detected`, `developer_tools=false`, and `virtual_machine=false`.

Launch options:

```js
const browser = await launch({
  headless: false,
  geoip: true,
  args: ["--fingerprint-noise=false", "--fingerprint-windows-font-metrics"],
});
```

Tested with a different IP or proxy? No; tested on direct residential ISP connection without proxy/VPN.

Works outside Docker / on host machine? Not using Docker; native Windows host.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Install `cloakbrowser@0.5.8` and `mmdb-lib` on native Windows 11 x64 with Node.js 20.19.6.
2. Launch headed browser using options above.
3. Open https://demo.fingerprint.com/playground.
4. Observe Browser Tampering result.

Error output / screenshots:

Official `launch()` result:

```json
{
  "suspect_score": 12,
  "tampering": true,
  "tampering_confidence": "medium",
  "tampering_ml_score": 0.9938,
  "tampering_details": { "anomaly_score": 0, "anti_detect_browser": true },
  "bot": "not_detected",
  "developer_tools": false,
  "virtual_machine": false
}
```

Browser was recognized as Chrome `151.0.0`; `navigator.webdriver=false`.

Same binary launched directly with persistent Test Profile, fixed seed, `noise=false`, and `--fingerprint-windows-font-metrics`:

```json
{
  "suspect_score": 8,
  "tampering": true,
  "tampering_confidence": "medium",
  "tampering_ml_score": 0.9096,
  "tampering_details": { "anomaly_score": 0, "anti_detect_browser": true }
}
```

Dockerfile (if applicable): N/A

Additional notes:

Removing only `--fingerprint-windows-font-metrics` produced the same ML score (0.9096) and same `font_hash`, suggesting this flag does not affect this native-Windows signal.

Controlled observations:

- Chromium `146.0.7680.177.5`, fixed seed, `noise=false`: ML 0.9806, `anomaly_score=0`, `anti_detect_browser=true`.
- Official wrapper with same v146: ML 0.9991.
- Historical Python `cloakbrowser` 0.3.4 + Windows Chromium `145.0.7632.109.2` + `launch(args=["--fingerprint=12345"])`: ML 0.9971.
- One run passed no fingerprint flags, but canvas/GPU values changed across relaunch and second run crossed threshold at ML 0.8064, so this was not stable.

Related: #193, #320, #395, #398.

Questions:

- Is `anti_detect_browser` independent of font/anomaly fixes and expected to pass on native Windows Chromium 151?
- Is another flag or release channel required?

title: [Bug] Incompatibility with Shifter.io Residential Proxies (WebRTC/Gateway Leak & Mislocation)
body:
Issue Description:
I am currently using a CloakBrowser Pro Plan. However, when using Shifter.io Residential Proxies, the browser fails to fully mask the proxy's underlying entry gateway, resulting in fingerprint inconsistency, location spoofing failure, and account bans on Google services.

In contrast, Webshare Proxies (Direct Exit / 1-1) work flawlessly under the exact same browser configuration and profile settings.

Steps to Reproduce:
Configure Profile A with a Shifter.io Residential Proxy targeted to South Korea (e.g., p.shifter.io:443).
Configure Profile B with a Webshare Proxy (e.g., p.webshare.io:80).
Launch both profiles and test against [Google Maps](https://maps.google.com/) and [Pixelscan](https://pixelscan.net/).

Expected Behavior:
Both proxy providers should route traffic cleanly to South Korea.
WebRTC, DNS, GeoIP, and TCP sockets should be fully synchronized.
Pixelscan should mark the fingerprint as consistent and legitimate.

Actual Behavior:
With Webshare Proxy:
Google Maps: Accurately detects location in South Korea.
Pixelscan: Passes all checks smoothly with 0 leaks.
Network Layer: Socket IP matches the exit IP directly (1-1 Direct Exit).

With Shifter.io Proxy:
Google Maps: Misidentifies location based on the entry gateway instead of the exit IP.
Pixelscan: Flags the environment and exposes an active intermediary gateway in Singapore (143.198.216.110).
Result: Accounts get flagged/banned due to network-layer mismatch.

Root Cause Analysis (Technical Log):
Inspecting the network layer via curl -v reveals that Shifter uses a multi-hop HTTP CONNECT tunnel carrying an extra transit header (X-Proxy-Exit-Ip):
Plaintext
* Trying 143.198.216.110:443... (DigitalOcean Singapore Gateway)
* CONNECT tunnel: HTTP/1.1 negotiated
< X-Proxy-Exit-Ip: 218.235.86.9 (South Korea Exit IP)
...
{
  "origin": "218.235.86.9"
}
Webshare connects directly to the destination socket, whereas Shifter routes through a Singapore entry gateway first. The browser core currently fails to pre-resolve and synchronize the C++ network stack before rendering, leaving the Singapore entry gateway exposed to target sites.

Environment:
OS: Windows 11 / macOS
Proxy Providers Tested: Shifter.io (Fails) vs Webshare.io (Passes)
Target Country: South Korea (KR)

title: Fix humanize=True false-negative visible check for display:contents elements
body:
## Bug

Reported: `humanize=True` `page.click()` (and other actions) fail with `ElementNotVisibleError` on an element that is demonstrably visible and rendered on screen — specifically reproduced on a Bootstrap-style toggled dropdown-menu `<li>` option. Regression from 0.5.6, when the isolated-world (CDP) actionability re-implementation replaced the previous real-Playwright `is_visible()`/`bounding_box()` calls.

## Root cause

The isolated-world visibility/geometry reads (`_ACTIONABLE_OP`/`_BOX_OP` in `stealth_dom.py`, mirrored in the JS and .NET ports) computed visibility and geometry from an element's own `getComputedStyle()` + `getBoundingClientRect()` only.

An element with `display: contents` (e.g. a reset `<li>` used by some custom dropdown/menu widgets to strip default list box styling while keeping DOM semantics) is *never itself boxed* — `getBoundingClientRect()` on it is always `{0,0,0,0}` — even though its children/text render normally. This exactly matches Playwright's own actionability engine (`packages/injected/src/domUtils.ts::computeBox`), which special-cases `display: contents` by recursing into children/text nodes instead of trusting the element's own empty rect. CloakBrowser's isolated-world reimplementation never added this special case, so it reported `visible: false` / no box indefinitely for such elements — a real, static CSS property, not a transient race — explaining why the retry loop never recovered.

## Fix

- Add a shared `__visBox()` helper to the isolated-world resolver JS (identical across Python, JS, and .NET) that recurses into child elements/text nodes for `display: contents`, unioning their rects. Used by both the box read and the actionable (visible/enabled/editable) read.
- `_ACTIONABLE_OP` now also returns the box alongside `visible`/`enabled`/`editable`.
- As defense-in-depth, `ensure_actionable`/`stealthActionable`/`EnsureActionableAsync` cross-check a `visible: false` in-world verdict against Playwright's own `is_visible()` before failing, whenever a non-empty box is present — matching the "only trust `not visible` when geometry is also absent/zero" pattern.

## Tests

- Python: new real-browser regression test (`TestDisplayContentsActionability` in `tests/test_humanize_unit.py`) reproducing a toggled `display:contents` dropdown; confirmed it fails with the pre-fix code (via git stash) and passes with the fix.
- JS: new `display:contents` behavioral tests in `js/tests/stealthDom.test.ts` executing the actual shipped resolver JS against a DOM stub, plus cross-check tests for `ensureActionable`.
- .NET: new Node-executed resolver test in `dotnet/tests/CloakBrowser.Tests/Human/StealthDomTests.cs` mirroring the JS test.

All existing unit tests pass unmodified (verified for Python and JS; .NET mirrored byte-for-byte from the tested JS/Python logic — could not compile locally, no dotnet SDK available in this environment).

## Changelog

Added an `[Unreleased]` entry in `CHANGELOG.md`.

title: Akamai SBSD returns 403
body:
Two related problems on **CloakBrowser Pro** (`scale` license), wrapper **0.5.8**, Chromium **151.0.7922.108.3** (pro), Linux x64, Playwright, headed Windows persona (Win fonts 8/8, Office fonts 10/10).

1. On **https://www.voeazul.com.br/br/pt/home** (Akamai Bot Manager with **SBSD**), a **Windows** persona consistently gets **HTTP 403**. The same automation with a **macOS or Linux** persona clears SBSD and yields a healthy session (valid cookies / successful page load). We cannot run those non-Windows personas in production: at high volume they get blocked. Traffic goes through a **high-quality residential proxy with Brazilian IPs**. Without SBSD on this URL, even Windows succeeds.
2. During an SBSD run the Playwright page dies mid-session with `Page.reload: Not attached to an active page`. This looks like the **Pro binary killing the browser after the CDP handshake** (session cap / license deny), but `cloakbrowser info` reports **`Sessions: unavailable`** and never shows the **plan limit** (used vs allowed).

### 1. Akamai SBSD → 403 (works without SBSD)

**Expected:** CloakBrowser 151 Pro should present a coherent browser to Akamai Bot Manager, including SBSD.

**Target URL:** https://www.voeazul.com.br/br/pt/home

**Actual:** With SBSD active and a **Windows** persona, the first document response is **403**.

The same flow on this URL, still through the **Brazilian residential proxy**, behaves differently by OS persona:

- **macOS** and **Linux** personas: SBSD is solved and we get good cookies / a normal page.
- **Windows** persona: HTTP 403.
- **Without SBSD:** Windows also succeeds.

We **cannot** switch production traffic to macOS/Linux: at high volume those personas are blocked, so we need Windows to work under SBSD.

Fingerprint basics on the Windows persona look consistent (Win32 UA, fonts 8/8, GPU, `outer >= inner` after launching without a Playwright viewport override). The 403 correlates with **SBSD + Windows**, not with proxy quality or a missing Windows font set.

### 2. Page detach mid-session (likely seat / license) + `info` does not show quota

While handling the SBSD challenge we call Playwright `page.reload({ waitUntil: 'commit' })` and get:

```text
Protocol error (Page.reload): Not attached to an active page
Call log:
  - waiting for navigation until "commit"
```

Immediately around that, launches also fail with:

```text
CloakBrowser Pro: couldn't verify your license (license server unreachable or a connection problem).
```

That maps to Pro exit code **78**. Exit code **76** is documented as *session limit reached*. Your wrapper also notes that a **post-handshake seat denial** can kill the browser **after** Playwright already has a live CDP connection, so the caller sees a generic “target closed / not attached” instead of a clear session-limit error.

**Expected:**

- If the plan is over capacity, fail at launch (or on the next API call) with the **session limit** message, not a Playwright protocol error on `reload`.
- `cloakbrowser info` should show **used / limit**, e.g. `Sessions: 8/20 in use`, not only `N seats in use` when the count API works.

**Actual `cloakbrowser info`:**

```text
CloakBrowser diagnostics
Wrapper:   0.5.8
Node:      v24.19.0
OS:        Linux x64
Platform:  linux-x64
Channel:   Stable
Version:   151.0.7922.108.3 (pro)
Binary:    /opt/cloakbrowser/chromium-151.0.7922.108.3-pro/chrome
Installed: true
Cache:     /opt/cloakbrowser/chromium-151.0.7922.108.3-pro
Launch:    ✓ CloakBrowser 151.0.7922.108.3
Win fonts: ok (8/8)
Office fonts: ok (10/10)
License:   scale
Sessions:  unavailable
GeoIP DB:  not downloaded (optional)  (pass --proxy <url> to resolve exit IP + timezone/locale)
Modules:
  playwright-core: ok
  puppeteer-core: missing
  mmdb-lib: missing
```

`Sessions: unavailable` does not tell us:

- how many seats are in use;
- what the **scale** plan limit is;
- whether we are over cap, the session-count API failed, or the license server was unreachable.

Without used/limit it is hard to tell a real SBSD 403 from the browser being killed because we hit the concurrent-session ceiling.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package | `cloakbrowser` 0.5.8 (npm) |
| Binary | 151.0.7922.108.3 pro |
| License | `scale` (`CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY`) |
| Runtime | Linux x64, Node v24.19.0, Playwright |
| Display | headed (Xvfb) |
| Fonts | Win 8/8, Office 10/10 |
| Proxy | High-quality **residential**, **Brazilian IPs** |
| Persona that 403s | Windows (required at high volume) |
| Personas that pass SBSD | macOS / Linux (blocked at high volume, not usable in production) |
| Target | https://www.voeazul.com.br/br/pt/home |

### Ask

1. Guidance or a fix for **Akamai SBSD 403** on 151 Pro with a **Windows** persona (macOS/Linux already pass SBSD on this URL, but we cannot use them at high volume).
2. Surface **session used / limit** in `cloakbrowser info` (and `--json`), and do not print `unavailable` without a reason.
3. When a post-handshake seat/license deny kills Chromium, propagate **exit 76/78** to the Playwright caller instead of `Protocol error (Page.reload): Not attached to an active page`.

title: CloakBrowser 0.5.8 — False-negative visible actionability check on dropdown menu items
body:
# Bug Report: CloakBrowser 0.5.8 — False-negative `visible` actionability check on dropdown menu items --- ## Environment | | | |---|---| | `cloakbrowser` (wrapper) | **0.5.8** (regression) — confirmed working on **0.4.11** | | Browser binary | v146 (free tier) | | Playwright | 1.61.0 | | Python | 3.12.13 | | OS | Linux 6.8.0-137-generic x86_64 (Docker container, glibc 2.41) | | Launch mode | `launch_persistent_context(..., headless=False, humanize=True, viewport={"width": 1920, "height": 1080})` | ## Summary After upgrading only the `cloakbrowser` wrapper from `0.4.11` → `0.5.8` (base image + pip package, no other code changes), a previously-reliable `page.click("text=Hoy")` call started failing **100% of the time** with `ElementNotVisibleError`, even though the target element is demonstrably visible and rendered on screen at the exact moment of the check. ## Steps to reproduce (site-specific, described since it's on a private/authenticated site) Open an open, absolutely-positioned dropdown menu (`.daterangepicker.dropdown-menu, display: block`) containing a list of `
  • ` options, e.g.: ```
    • Hoy
    • Últimos 7 Días
    • Mes Actual
      • ...
    ...
    ``` Call page.click("text=Hoy", timeout=10000) (via the humanized wrapper, humanize=True). 3. Observe `ElementNotVisibleError: Element 'text=Hoy' failed visible check: element is not visible` after the full timeout elapses. 4. Retry with `force=True` → this skips `ensure_actionable()` entirely but still calls `scroll_to_element()`, which now raises `RuntimeError: Element not found while scrolling into view` because `get_box()` returns `None`. ## Expected behavior The click should succeed (as it reliably did on `0.4.11`), since the element: - Is attached to the DOM - Has non-zero size (visually rendered, orange-highlighted `active` state) - Is within the viewport - Is not covered by any other element ## Actual behavior `_stealth_actionable()` in `cloakbrowser/human/actionability.py` reports `visible: false` for the entire 10-second retry window (backoff loop `[100, 250, 500, 1000]ms`), even though: - A debug screenshot taken by our own error handler **at the exact moment of the `ElementNotVisibleError`** shows the "Hoy" `
  • ` fully rendered, highlighted, and in the same visual state as a manual browser inspection of the identical dropdown (screenshots available, see "Attachments" below). - The manual (non-automated) inspection of the same page/dropdown, in a separate browser session, shows the element in an ordinary, clearly visible state (`class="active"`, orange background) — no unusual CSS (`opacity`, `transform`, `visibility: hidden`, `display: none`) is present. This strongly suggests a false negative in the in-world visibility computation added/changed in 0.5.x, rather than a real rendering issue. ## Comparison across versions (from our production logs) - **Last run on `0.4.11`:** `Clicking filter option 'Hoy'...` → succeeded in **< 1 second**. - **First run on `0.5.8`** (same code path, no other changes deployed yet): `Clicking filter option 'Hoy'...` → failed after **~30s** (default click timeout) with the identical `ElementNotVisibleError`. - Reproduced identically across 4 separate runs on `0.5.8` (different sessions, different persistent profile states), always at the same step. - Reverting the wrapper + base image back to `0.4.11` (no other code changes) immediately restored the previous reliable behavior. ## Suspected root cause / area to investigate - `cloakbrowser/human/actionability.py::_stealth_actionable()` — the in-world (`page._stealth_world`) evaluation of `build_actionable_js(selector)` for the `"visible"` check. - Possibly related to the 0.5.x changelog items "safer humanized pre-click checks" (0.5.7) and "safer humanized behavior after in-page navigation ... scroll refinements" (0.5.8) — a change here may have altered how visibility/geometry is computed for elements inside dropdowns that are: - Absolutely/fixed-positioned relative to a trigger element rather than in normal document flow, - Rendered via a toggled `display: block` (Bootstrap-style `dropdown-menu`) rather than being always in the DOM, - Possibly cached/stale in the isolated-world context (`page._stealth_world`) across an earlier navigation or DOM mutation in the same page session (we also removed an unrelated banner via `page.evaluate()` shortly before this click, in case that's a relevant trigger for isolated-world staleness — see `stealth.invalidate()` calls tied to `framenavigated` in `__init__.py`, which wouldn't fire here since there's no navigation, only a DOM mutation). ## Suggested fix / workaround for the CloakBrowser team 1. Add a regression test with a Bootstrap-style toggled `dropdown-menu` (`display: none` ↔ `display: block`, no navigation involved) to the actionability test suite, asserting the in-world `visible` check agrees with Playwright's own `locator.is_visible()`/`bounding_box()` for such elements. 2. Consider falling back to Playwright's own `is_visible()`/`bounding_box()` as a cross-check when the in-world read reports `not visible` but the element has a non-null, non-zero bounding box — i.e., only trust "not visible" from the isolated world when geometry is also absent/zero, to avoid false negatives like this one. 3. If the isolated world (`page._stealth_world`) can go stale after in-page DOM mutations that aren't full navigations (e.g. `page.evaluate()` removing an unrelated banner elsewhere on the page), consider invalidating/re-syncing it on such mutations too, not just on `framenavigated`. ## Suggested workaround for our own use (already applied) Pinned back to `cloakbrowser==0.4.11` / `cloakhq/cloakbrowser:0.4.11` until this is fixed upstream. ### Attachments ``` CloakBrowser 0.5.8 — false-negative 'visible' actionability check ==================================================================== Environment ----------- cloakbrowser (wrapper): 0.5.8 (regression) Known-good version: 0.4.11 (confirmed working, same code, same site) Browser binary: v146 (free tier) Playwright: 1.61.0 Python: 3.12.13 OS: Linux 6.8.0-137-generic x86_64 (Docker, glibc 2.41) Launch options: launch_persistent_context( PROFILE_DIR, headless=False, humanize=True, viewport={"width": 1920, "height": 1080}, accept_downloads=True, args=['--start-maximized'], ) Failing call ------------ page.click("text=Hoy", timeout=10000) ... where "Hoy" is a
  • Hoy

title: feat(browser): add launch_chrome_direct() for TCP CDP server mode
body:
## Problem

Server-style runtimes that want to hand a CDP endpoint to another process (e.g. an MCP browser server) currently route through `launch_persistent_context(user_data_dir, args=["--remote-debugging-port=9222"])`. Playwright's `launch_persistent_context` injects `--remote-debugging-pipe` and owns the connection over that pipe; the TCP `--remote-debugging-port` argument never becomes a usable endpoint for external CDP clients. External tools that `connect_over_cdp` to the advertised port hang or fail, and the orphaned instance wedges the shared profile so every later launch exits immediately with code 0.

## Fix

Adds `launch_chrome_direct()` — a subprocess-based launch that:
- builds the same stealth args via `build_args()` (fingerprints, extensions, locale/timezone),
- launches the patched Chromium directly with `--remote-debugging-address` / `--remote-debugging-port` (TCP, no pipe),
- waits for the CDP listener, then hands back the `Popen` handle for the caller to own,
- **Windows only**: appends `--disable-features=AutoDeElevate`. Since Chrome 131, AutoDeElevate relaunches the browser de-elevated; inside the patched build the re-exec fails and the parent exits 0 instantly — killing the launch. Playwright's default args mask this, which is why it only bites direct launches.

## Verification

- `tests/test_launch.py::test_launch_chrome_direct_exposes_tcp_cdp` — real binary: `/json/version` answers over TCP, no `--remote-debugging-pipe` in argv.
- `tests/test_launch.py::test_launch_chrome_direct_auto_delevate_always_on_windows` — flag always present on Windows, merged (not duplicated) into caller-supplied `--disable-features`, absent on non-Windows.
- End-to-end: Playwright `connect_over_cdp` + `page.goto("https://www.google.com")` works against the direct-launched endpoint.

title: humanize fill() fails with ElementNotAttachedError: isolated world stays bound to bfcached old document after click/form-triggered navigation (regression in 0.5.6)
body:
# Bug: humanize `locator.fill()` fails with `ElementNotAttachedError` when the isolated world stays bound to a bfcached old document after click/form-triggered navigations (introduced in 0.5.6)

## Summary

Since **0.5.6** (commit `9fa24723`, "route pre-click element reads through a shared DOM helper"), actionability checks (attached/visible/enabled/editable) are performed through the CDP isolated world (`page._stealth_world`) instead of plain Playwright reads. When a page navigates via a click or form submission (not `page.goto`), the world is never invalidated (`stealth.invalidate()` is only wired into `_human_goto`). If the previous document is kept alive in the back/forward cache, its isolated-world execution context stays valid, so `Runtime.evaluate` keeps succeeding **against the stale document** instead of erroring and triggering the "auto-recreate on next call" path. The result: `fill()` on an element that is present and visible in the current document consistently raises

```
Element 'input[name="code"] >> nth=0' failed attached check: element not found in DOM
```

for the full `timeout`, retrying ~3s per call and never recovering (observed for 36+ seconds / 9 attempts).

## Steps to reproduce

This reproduces with a multi-hop signup flow where navigation happens via clicks/forms, e.g.:

```python
import time
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
from cloakbrowser import launch_context

with sync_playwright() as p:
    context = launch_context(headless=True, humanize=True)
    page = context.new_page()

    # 1) Initial goto -> world created on document A
    page.goto("https://chatgpt.com/", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
    # 2) click-driven navigation (document B)
    page.locator('button[data-testid="signup-button"]').click()
    # ... form submit -> authorize page (document C), possibly a Cloudflare
    # challenge reload (document D), then the OTP page (document E) ...
    # 3) Fill an input on the final document (E)
    page.locator('input[name="code"]').first.fill("123456", timeout=3000)
```

Actual (humanize=True):

```
cloakbrowser.human.actionability.ElementNotAttachedError: Element 'input[name="code"] >> nth=0' failed attached check: element not found in DOM
```

- The element **is** in the DOM of the current document: `page.locator(...).is_visible()` returns `True` right before the fill, and `page.content()` shows it.
- Only the isolated world's `document.querySelectorAll(...)` returns nothing, i.e. the world is bound to a stale document (previous page kept alive in bfcache after a click/form-driven navigation).

Expected (humanize=False works fine): the fill succeeds on the first attempt.

## Root cause analysis

1. `_SyncIsolatedWorld.evaluate()` (and the async variant) only recreates the world when `Runtime.evaluate` raises. When the old document survives in the bfcache, its isolated-world `executionContextId` is never destroyed, so `Runtime.evaluate` returns a successful result — against the wrong document. The "auto-recreate on navigation" promise in the class docstring is therefore silently broken for click/form-triggered navigations.
2. `stealth.invalidate()` is only called from `_human_goto` / `_frame_aware_goto`. Any navigation initiated by clicking a button, submitting a form, `history.pushState`, or a Cloudflare challenge reload never invalidates the world.
3. Since 0.5.6, `ensure_actionable()` runs the "attached" check through the isolated world (`_stealth_actionable` → `build_actionable_js`), and a `NOT_FOUND` from a stale world becomes a hard `ElementNotAttachedError` that is retried until the action timeout. Before 0.5.6 the checks used plain Playwright reads, so the stale world was harmless for fills.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Named world (recommended, minimal)**: create the isolated world with a non-empty `worldName` in `Page.createIsolatedWorld`. Named worlds are recreated by Chromium on navigation with a fresh context for the new document, so `evaluate` always runs against the current document:
   ```python
   result = cdp.send("Page.createIsolatedWorld", {
       "frameId": frame_id,
       "worldName": "cloakbrowser-stealth",   # non-empty
       "grantUniveralAccess": True,
   })
   ```
2. **Invalidate on every navigation**: also call `stealth.invalidate()` from the frame/navigation event hooks (or from `wait_for_load_state` / after click) so the world re-binds on the next evaluate.
3. **Verify document identity per evaluate**: track the current `executionContextId` (or frame's document id) and recreate the world when it changes, instead of relying on `Runtime.evaluate` erroring on stale contexts.

## Environment

- cloakbrowser 0.5.7 (Python, sync and async APIs both affected; `actionability.py` / `stealth_dom.py` identical between 0.5.6 and 0.5.7)
- Playwright-driven multi-page auth flow with click/form-triggered navigations
- Regression introduced by commit `9fa24723` (2026-08-07), first released in 0.5.6

title: Google passkey creation rejects the gstatic appidExclude before WebAuthn proxy
body:
CloakBrowser chromium-v146.0.7680.177.5 rejects a Google passkey creation request before an attached chrome.webAuthenticationProxy extension receives onCreateRequest.

Minimal comparison from an https://accounts.google.com page:

1. A creation request for rp.id google.com with extensions.googleLegacyAppidSupport=true reaches onCreateRequest.
2. The same request with extensions.appidExclude=https://www.gstatic.com/securitykey/origins.json and googleLegacyAppidSupport=false immediately rejects with SecurityError: This is an invalid domain. No onCreateRequest event fires.

The current Google Account settings enrollment flow uses the second shape. The older post-sign-in passkey enrollment flow used the first shape, which explains why the old flow worked while the current one fails.

The v146.0.7680.177.5 Linux binary contains domain-substituted values for the two Chromium Google AppID compatibility constants instead of the upstream gstatic URLs. Chromium ValidateAppIdExtension compares the caller value against those constants before dispatching to webAuthenticationProxy, so the upstream Google special case cannot match.

Expected: Google subdomains may use the two upstream Chromium gstatic AppID constants and the request reaches the attached WebAuthn proxy.

Could you confirm whether the current v150 Stable binary restores these constants? If not, please preserve the upstream kGstaticAppId and kGstaticCorpAppId values in the next build. A regression test should cover explicit appidExclude from accounts.google.com with an attached webAuthenticationProxy extension.

title: Best Buy product document resets HTTP/2 stream; forcing QUIC succeeds
body:
## Description

CloakBrowser 0.5.7 with Chromium 151.0.7922.108.2 on Linux x64, running in Docker via `cloakserve`, consistently fails when opening this public Best Buy product URL as a top-level document:

https://www.bestbuy.com/site/case-logic-laptop-sleeve-for-17-3-laptop-black-laps15/4126483.p

The failure is:

`net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR`

The same browser identity can:

- open `https://www.bestbuy.com/` with HTTP 200 over h2;
- fetch the product URL in-page with HTTP 200 and a complete HTML body over h3;
- open the product URL successfully as a top-level document when Cloakserve is started with `--origin-to-force-quic-on=www.bestbuy.com:443`, returning HTTP 200 over h3 and rendering the expected product heading.

Without the flag, direct navigation and a user-style clicked link both fail. Fresh fingerprints and fresh sessions reproduce the result.

## Environment

- CloakBrowser wrapper: 0.5.7
- Chromium: 151.0.7922.108.2 (Preview)
- Platform: Linux x86_64 Docker
- Integration: Playwright over Cloakserve CDP
- Target: Best Buy product document

## Minimal reproduction

Start Cloakserve normally, connect with Playwright over CDP using a fresh fingerprint, and run:

```js
await page.goto("https://www.bestbuy.com");
await page.goto("https://www.bestbuy.com/site/case-logic-laptop-sleeve-for-17-3-laptop-black-laps15/4126483.p", {
  waitUntil: "domcontentloaded",
  timeout: 30000
});
```

Observed: `net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR`.

Then start Cloakserve with:

```text
--origin-to-force-quic-on=www.bestbuy.com:443
```

The same top-level navigation returns HTTP 200 over h3 and renders the product heading.

No credentials, cookies, authorization headers, raw response data, network topology, or screenshots are included.

**Description:**
Currently, when running the CloakBrowser Pro binary (which is based on Chromium 150), if we try to downgrade the browser identity to an older version (e.g., Chrome 148) by setting:
1. `LaunchContextOptions.UserAgent` to a Chrome 148 UA string.
2. `--fingerprint-brand-version=148.0.7778.215` (to match the exact version).

The UA strings and Client Hints are patched. However, advanced kernel checks (like BrowserScan's Bot Detection) can still easily detect the mismatch through JavaScript/DOM feature detection. 

BrowserScan flags it as:
- "The browser claims that Chrome 148"
- "Detect version Chrome 150"

**Expected Behavior / Feature Request:**
Since the underlying V8/Chromium engine is v150, the feature-detection scripts find APIs that shouldn't exist in v148, which causes the mismatch.

Is there any future plan or roadmap for CloakBrowser to implement dynamic DOM/JS feature masking? For example, hiding or spoofing newer JS APIs / CSS properties introduced in v150, so that the kernel perfectly emulates a v148 environment and passes strict feature-detection checks?

title: fix(humanize): preserve timeout: 0 semantics
body:
## Summary

- Fixes: Ready Page and ElementHandle actions fail before their first actionability check when callers pass Playwright's timeout: 0 option, even though zero is documented to disable the timeout.
- Root cause: Each action converted the raw numeric timeout directly into Date.now() + timeout. That collapsed raw zero into an already-expired deadline, while forwarding numeric remaining values also made it impossible to distinguish a genuinely exhausted finite budget from Playwright's special zero value.

## Regression evidence

- Before: `cd js && npx --yes node@20 node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/humanize.test.ts -t 'keeps a ready humanized page action timeout-free'` exited `1`

- After: `cd js && npx --yes node@20 node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/humanize.test.ts -t 'keeps a ready humanized page action timeout-free'` exited `0`

## Verification

- `cd js && npx --yes node@20 node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/humanize.test.ts`
- `cd js && npx --yes node@20 node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run`

title: [Bug] hasInconsistentTimingResolution triggered by CloakBrowser itself — confirmed via A/B test on identical VM (plain Playwright is clean)
body:
Summary
deviceandbrowserinfo.com/are_you_a_bot's hasInconsistentTimingResolution signal fires true when using CloakBrowser, but false on the exact same machine with plain, unpatched Playwright Chromium. This isolates the cause to CloakBrowser's own source-level patches, not the OS, not virtualization, and not the detector being a false positive on cloud/VM environments in general.

Environment
CloakBrowser: 0.5.6 (Python wrapper), binary 150.0.7871.114.3 (free tier, license key configured, 1 concurrent session)
Platform: genuine AWS EC2 Windows Server instance (m7i-flex.large), no OS spoofing involved — CloakBrowser was running as native Windows-on-Windows
Python 3.12.7, cloakbrowser.launch(headless=False), no extra args
Detector: https://deviceandbrowserinfo.com/are_you_a_bot
Steps to reproduce
On a real Windows machine (tested: AWS EC2 Windows Server, m7i-flex.large), install CloakBrowser and configure a free license key.
Run:
import cloakbrowser
browser = cloakbrowser.launch(headless=False)
page = browser.new_page()
page.goto("https://deviceandbrowserinfo.com/are_you_a_bot", wait_until="load")
page.wait_for_timeout(4000)
print(page.inner_text("body"))
Compare against plain Playwright on the same machine:
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=False)
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto("https://deviceandbrowserinfo.com/are_you_a_bot", wait_until="load")
    page.wait_for_timeout(4000)
    print(page.inner_text("body"))
Results (same VM, same session, only variable is CloakBrowser vs plain Playwright)
CloakBrowser:

{
  "isBot": true,
  "details": {
    "hasBotUserAgent": false,
    "hasWebdriverTrue": false,
    "hasWebdriverInFrameTrue": false,
    "isPlaywright": false,
    "hasInconsistentChromeObject": false,
    "isPhantom": false,
    "isNightmare": false,
    "isSequentum": false,
    "isSeleniumChromeDefault": false,
    "isHeadlessChrome": false,
    "isWebGLInconsistent": false,
    "hasInconsistentWebGLShaderLang": false,
    "hasInconsistentTimingResolution": true,
    "isAutomatedWithCDP": false,
    "isAutomatedWithCDPInWebWorker": false,
    "hasInconsistentClientHints": false,
    "hasInconsistentGPUFeatures": false,
    "isIframeOverridden": false,
    "hasInconsistentWorkerValues": false,
    "hasHighHardwareConcurrency": false,
    "hasHeadlessChromeDefaultScreenResolution": false,
    "hasSuspiciousWeakSignals": false
  }
}
Every other signal is clean — hasInconsistentTimingResolution is the sole reason isBot resolves true.

Plain Playwright (same VM):

{
  "isBot": true,
  "details": {
    "hasBotUserAgent": false,
    "hasWebdriverTrue": true,
    "hasWebdriverInFrameTrue": true,
    "isPlaywright": false,
    "hasInconsistentChromeObject": false,
    "isPhantom": false,
    "isNightmare": false,
    "isSequentum": false,
    "isSeleniumChromeDefault": false,
    "isHeadlessChrome": false,
    "isWebGLInconsistent": false,
    "hasInconsistentWebGLShaderLang": false,
    "hasInconsistentTimingResolution": false,
    "isAutomatedWithCDP": true,
    "isAutomatedWithCDPInWebWorker": true,
    "hasInconsistentClientHints": false,
    "hasInconsistentGPUFeatures": false,
    "isIframeOverridden": false,
    "hasInconsistentWorkerValues": false,
    "hasHighHardwareConcurrency": false,
    "hasHeadlessChromeDefaultScreenResolution": false,
    "hasSuspiciousWeakSignals": true
  }
}
Flags true for the expected unpatched-automation signals (hasWebdriverTrue, isAutomatedWithCDP, etc. — as expected for vanilla Playwright), but hasInconsistentTimingResolution is false.

Additional context
This same hasInconsistentTimingResolution: true result was also reproduced with CloakBrowser (not plain Playwright) across three other environments before this test: Docker (cloakhq/cloakbrowser official image), native WSL2 Ubuntu, and a separate AWS Linux VPS — all spoofing a Windows platform. Initially we suspected this was a Linux-hosting-Windows-spoof side effect, or a general cloud/hypervisor clock-granularity artifact. This Windows-native + plain-Playwright A/B test rules out both of those: the same cloud hypervisor, running plain Playwright, does not trigger the signal. The variable that flips it is specifically CloakBrowser's own binary/patches.

Expected behavior
hasInconsistentTimingResolution should be false when CloakBrowser is patching a real Windows-on-Windows launch with no spoofing involved, matching plain Chromium's behavior on identical hardware.

Ask
Given this is a clean, reproducible before/after isolation on identical hardware, is this a known limitation in one of CloakBrowser's timing-related patches (e.g. the performance.now()/high-resolution-timer countermeasure), and is there a workaround or planned fix?

title: fix(cloakserve): evict poll()-alive but CDP-dead browsers instead of serving 502s
body:
## Problem

`ChromePool.get_or_launch` decides whether to reuse a pooled Chrome for a seed with a single liveness check — `proc.process.poll() is None`. But `poll()` only reports whether the OS process has been reaped, which lags CDP availability in two common ways:

- **Graceful-shutdown window.** Chrome tears down its DevTools/CDP listening socket seconds before the process actually exits. A client that closes a browser and immediately requests the same fingerprint seed is handed the still-"alive" process whose CDP port already refuses connections.
- **Wedged browser.** A hung/unresponsive Chrome can keep its process alive indefinitely while its CDP port no longer answers.

In both cases the dead process is returned, and `handle_json_version` / `handle_json_list` then fail to reach `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/version` and return `502 {"error": "CDP endpoint unreachable"}`. Crucially, the 502 path **does not evict the dead pool entry**, so every retry for that seed hits the same corpse — the failure is **not self-healing** until the OS finally reaps the process (or the idle timeout fires).

This is easy to trigger under any workflow that reuses seeds across browser restarts, or when a browser crashes/OOMs and lingers mid-shutdown. Under load it presents as a burst of dead-port 502s against a seed whose process still `poll()`s as alive.

## Fix

1. `get_or_launch` reuses a `poll()`-alive process **only if its CDP port actually accepts a TCP connection** (`_cdp_port_alive`, a sub-millisecond local connect). `poll()` short-circuits the check, so an already-exited process skips the probe and takes the existing cleanup+relaunch path. A poll-alive-but-dead-port corpse now falls through to `_cleanup_process` + a fresh launch, under the existing per-seed lock.
2. `handle_json_version` and `handle_json_list` wrap the fetch in a 2-attempt loop: on the first connection failure they evict the stale entry and retry once, so a browser that dies in the narrow window between the probe and the fetch becomes a single cold relaunch instead of a persistent 502. Eviction matches the pooled process **by object identity**, never by recomputing the seed key, so a concurrent relaunch on the same seed is never killed.

The reuse fast-path stays fast (one cheap local connect) and behavior is unchanged for a genuinely-live browser.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_cloakserve.py`:

- `TestCdpPortAlive` — the probe returns True for a listening port, False for a closed one.
- `TestPoolKeyForIdentity` — identity match; returns None when a concurrent relaunch has replaced the entry.
- `TestGetOrLaunchReuseGuard` — poll-alive-but-dead-port is evicted and relaunched; poll-alive-and-port-alive is reused after exactly one probe (no relaunch).
- `TestHandlerCorpseRecovery` — `json/version` and `json/list` recover without a 502 by evicting once and retrying; they return 502 only after both attempts fail; identity-based eviction spares a concurrently-relaunched process.

Two existing tests were adjusted for the new reuse probe. `pytest tests/test_cloakserve.py` → **113 passed**.

title: Requesting v148.0.7778.215.5 downloads Chromium v150.0.7871.114.3 instead
body:
## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x64
- Python: 3.14
- CloakBrowser: Latest PyPI package
- License: Pro Trial

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from cloakbrowser import launch

browser = launch(
    license_key="cb_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    browser_version="148.0.7778.215.5"
)
```

## Expected behavior

The API should download the requested browser version (`148.0.7778.215.5`) or the correct rollback binary associated with that version.

## Actual behavior

The download request is redirected to a different Chromium version:

**Request URL**

```
https://cloakbrowser.dev/api/download/148.0.7778.215.5
```

**Final URL**

```
https://.../cloakbrowser/chromium-v150.0.7871.114.3/cloakbrowser-windows-x64.zip
```

Since the downloaded binary is Chromium v150 while the expected checksum corresponds to the requested rollback version, SHA256 verification fails.

```
Checksum verification failed!

Expected:
d86afa5eab7383b0b135f1a89057bd697d1db5dc8385b872f14b8e3124c0cf48

Got:
a905bfdaa79c2ac2db2119ac4b153da8c1aebde9732da617de71722176b05084
```

The wrapper correctly rejects the downloaded binary because it does not match the expected SHA256.

## Additional information

I added some debug logging to `download.py` and confirmed that:

```
REQUEST URL:
https://cloakbrowser.dev/api/download/148.0.7778.215.5

FINAL URL:
https://.../cloakbrowser/chromium-v150.0.7871.114.3/cloakbrowser-windows-x64.zip
```

It appears that the download endpoint redirects to the latest Chromium binary instead of the requested rollback version.

Could you please verify whether this is an issue with the download API or the rollback mapping?

Thank you!

title: [Bug] 0.5.4: every humanized page call raises TypeError on Python 3.14 — license guard's functools.partial is now a method descriptor
body:
## Summary

On Python 3.14, **every humanized page call fails** in 0.5.4 (0.5.3 is fine):

```
TypeError: Page.goto() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 positional arguments
           (and 2 keyword-only arguments) were given
```

`_install_license_guard` (new in 0.5.4) replaces each public page method with a
`functools.partial`, documented as safe because "a partial ... is NOT a
descriptor". **Python 3.14 made `functools.partial` a method descriptor.**
`humanize` stores the guarded methods on a holder *instance* and reads them back
off it, so the partial binds the holder and prepends it as a positional
argument.

## Environment

- cloakbrowser 0.5.4 (Pro), `humanize=True`, sync API — the async path composes
  identically
- Python 3.14.6, Linux (also reproduces on 3.14.0/macOS)
- 0.5.3 unaffected — the guard is new in 0.5.4

## Reproduction

No browser and no licence needed; the two wrappers are enough. Python 3.14,
`pip install cloakbrowser==0.5.4`:

```python
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from cloakbrowser.browser import _install_license_guard
from cloakbrowser.human import _CursorState, patch_page
from cloakbrowser.human.config import resolve_config


class FakePage:
    """`goto` carries Playwright's real signature; `mouse`/`keyboard` are
    properties, as on the real Page — the guard skips properties by name."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._mouse, self._keyboard = MagicMock(), MagicMock()

    @property
    def mouse(self): return self._mouse

    @property
    def keyboard(self): return self._keyboard

    def goto(self, url, *, timeout=None, wait_until=None, referer=None):
        return ("navigated", url, timeout, wait_until)

    def click(self, *a, **k): ...
    def type(self, *a, **k): ...
    def fill(self, *a, **k): ...
    def hover(self, *a, **k): ...
    def dblclick(self, *a, **k): ...
    def select_option(self, *a, **k): ...

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        return self.__dict__.setdefault("_extras", {}).setdefault(name, MagicMock())


cfg = resolve_config("default", None)

page = FakePage()
_install_license_guard(page, "/nonexistent/denial")   # the order launch() uses
patch_page(page, cfg, _CursorState())
page.goto("https://example.com", wait_until="load", timeout=60000)
```

```
guard-then-humanize: TypeError: goto() takes 2 positional arguments but 3
                     positional arguments (and 2 keyword-only arguments) were given
humanize-then-guard: OK          # reversing the order hides it
```

Traceback, entirely inside the package:

```
human/__init__.py:1042  _human_goto → response = originals.goto(url, **kwargs)
browser.py:123          guarded     → result = original(*args, **kwargs)
TypeError: goto() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 positional arguments
           (and 2 keyword-only arguments) were given
```

## Mechanism

1. `launch()` installs the guard first ("Installed before the wraps below so it
   sits closest to the real call"), so `browser.new_page` is guarded and, being
   a `_GUARD_FACTORY_METHODS` entry, deep-guards the page it returns. Every
   public page method becomes `functools.partial(guarded)`.

2. `patch_browser` → `patch_page` snapshots those methods into a holder — note
   the trailing `()`, which makes it an **instance**, not the class
   (`human/__init__.py:983-1001`):

   ```python
   originals = type("Originals", (), {"goto": page.goto, "click": page.click, ...})()
   ```

3. `_human_goto` calls `originals.goto(url, **kwargs)` — instance attribute
   access. Through Python 3.13 that returned the partial unchanged. On 3.14 a
   partial is a method descriptor, so the access binds the holder:

   ```
   holder.goto  ->  <bound method ? of <cloakbrowser.human.Originals object>>
   ```

   `guarded` therefore receives `(originals, url)` instead of `(url,)`, and
   since `original` is the real bound method, Playwright's `goto` sees three
   positionals.

The comment at `browser.py:141-146` states the assumption that no longer holds:

> Wrap in a partial so the guard is NOT a descriptor. Playwright's real methods
> are bound methods; humanize copies them into a class attribute
> (`type("Originals", ...)`) and reads them back off an instance. A plain
> function there would re-bind and inject a spurious `self` arg — a partial
> (like a bound method) does not. Keeps composition with humanize.

The holder *is* read off an instance, and on 3.14 a partial re-binds there
exactly as a plain function would.

`hasattr(functools.partial, "__get__")` is **not** a usable probe — it is `True`
on 3.13 as well. Only the behaviour differs:

| Python | `Holder().goto("URL")` where `Holder.goto` is a `partial` |
|---|---|
| 3.12.13 | works — partial is not a descriptor |
| 3.13.x | works, with `FutureWarning: functools.partial will be a method descriptor in future Python versions` |
| 3.14.6 | **`TypeError`** — binds the instance and prepends it |

The 3.13 `FutureWarning` names both the change and a fix (`staticmethod()`).

## Scope

Not specific to `goto` — it hits everything `patch_page` copies into the holder:
`click`, `type`, `fill`, `hover`, `dblclick`, `select_option`, `goto`,
`mouse_move`, `mouse_click`, `mouse_wheel`, `mouse_down`, `mouse_up`. `goto` is
simply the first call most flows make. `_install_license_guard_async` composes
with `patch_page_async` the same way, and the same
`type("_R", (), {"move": self.page._original.mouse_move})()` pattern appears at
`human/__init__.py:504, 521, 818, 839`.

There is no workaround at the call site: the argument is injected below the
public API, and passing `url=` as a keyword fails identically.

## Suggested fix

Make the guard a non-descriptor again — a small callable object works on every
version, with no `functools` behaviour to track:

```python
class _Guarded:                     # no __get__, so holder storage stays inert
    def __init__(self, fn): self._fn = fn
    def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs): return self._fn(*args, **kwargs)
```

`staticmethod(...)`, what the 3.13 `FutureWarning` recommends, also restores the
old behaviour where the value reaches a class body.

A regression test that composes `_install_license_guard` with `patch_page` and
calls one wrapped method would catch this — the two wrappers are only exercised
together at runtime today.

## Impact

Deploying 0.5.4 took down our scraping fleet: 100% of runs failed ~0.8 s after
launch, at the first `goto`. We have reverted to 0.5.3 and are holding there.

Updates `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` from 1.14.1 to 1.14.2
Release notes

Sourced from pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish's releases.

v1.14.2

🛠️ Urgh… Another release!? Again? Explain yourself!

Looking at the diff, you'll only witness updates across the dependency tree. That's it! It's not a security fix or anything like that even, no. But you'll want this update.

[!tip] So what most people will find useful is @​takluyver💰's update of Twine to v7 that we use internally (#416). This version will let them upload their sdists and wheels containing core packaging metadata v2.5 to (Test)PyPI.

🧐 Tell me why..

TL;DR non-pure-python projects with C-extensions tend to have dozens (sometimes hundreds) wheels to upload to PyPI per release. They are often quite big and take time to transfer over the network. People started noticing problems and coming up with DIY sharding workarounds like aio-libs/aiohttp#13226 around July 23. On this date, projects with a good amount of bytes to publish would start getting timeouts 5 minutes after the PyPI publishing job begun. The same job that worked just fine before.

I had to start pinging upstream library and ecosystem people, on GitHub and privately, to start making sense of what was happening. Eventually, we collectively concluded that GitHub must've shortened the lifetime of their OIDC identity — it seems to have used to be 10 minutes long (at some point in the past) and is now 5 minutes, apparently. It's not documented clearly, and we have not been able to get any clarity by attempting to contact GitHub through private channels, using personal connections.

Over the course of investigation, @​facutuesca💰 found and fixed a related underlying cache invalidation bug in sigstore/sigstore-python#1838, which he then coordinated propagation through the dependency chain updates in sigstore-python, pypi-attestations, gh-action-pypi-publish and gh-action-sigstore-python.

Mike's also discovered that Sigstore's Rekor slowdown seems to have become the main contributing cause of the last week's incident. He's collected some data to support this claim: https://publishing-five-minute-timeout.tiiny.site.

🫶 New Contributors

  • @​davidbrochart made their first contribution in #415
  • @​takluyver made their first contribution in #416

🪞 Full Diff: https://github.com/pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish/compare/v1.14.1...v1.14.2

🧔‍♂️ Release Manager: @​webknjaz 🇺🇦

🙏 Special Thanks to @​davidbrochart💰 and @​Dreamsorcerer💰 for turning my attention (in #415 and in private) to the newly surfaced corner case in GitHub's behavior that only affected a narrow category of projects while many others remained blissfully unaware. @​bdraco💰 came up with a DIY sharding workaround for aiohttp that served as a demo for other projects. @​miketheman💰 confirmed the Warehouse-side details. Also, @​jku💰 and @​woodruffw💰 helped work through, review and release the Sigstore ecosystem upstream libs.

Updates `playwright-core` from 1.61.1 to 1.62.1
Release notes

Sourced from playwright-core's releases.

v1.62.1

Bug Fixes

  • #41989 [Regression]: tsconfig "extends" bare specifier isn't resolved via node_modules walk-up like tsc (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41998 [Regression]: directory-form tsconfig project references ("path": "../pkg") fail to resolve (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41985 Accessibility snapshot drops button name when text is nested inside spans with aria-hidden SVG
  • #42000 [Regression]: page.evaluate() arg of a branded primitive type (string & { brand }) no longer type-checks since 1.62
  • #42013 [BUG]Image-type actionable elements are not presented in the snapshot.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });
await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.
await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

title: [Bug][Windows][Pro 150] Browser exits after ~10 seconds with exitCode=78 despite a valid license
Free-tier session never releases after abrupt process exit — every subsequent launch fails silently with "Target page, context or browser has been closed" (any site, headless or headed)
body:
Description:
After one abrupt/non-clean shutdown (browser killed mid-run, script crashed, terminal
closed while a script was paused at input()) instead of a clean browser.close(), my
free-tier license got permanently stuck showing "1 seat in use" via `cloakbrowser info`
— even though zero CloakBrowser processes are running anywhere on the machine.

From that point on, every single launch() call fails identically: the browser opens
(is_connected() == True for ~1-2s), then the very first page.goto() throws
"Target page, context or browser has been closed". This happens on ANY url, including
https://example.com — not specific to any target site. No error text is printed
anywhere (stdout/stderr/Windows Event Log) explaining why — it's a completely silent
failure, consistent with the documented behavior in license.py that license-denial
exit codes intentionally print no diagnostic string.

Expected: either the session should self-release faster, or launch() should raise a
clear CloakBrowserLicenseError (like it does for other license failures at launch-time)
instead of returning a Browser object that dies on first use with a generic Playwright
error.

CloakBrowser version: 0.5.3 (wrapper), Chromium 150.0.7871.114.3 (pro binary, free tier)

Wrapper: Python 3.13.5

Environment: Windows 11 Home (10.0.26200), x86_64, not Docker. Binary at
C:\Users\<user>\.cloakbrowser\chromium-150.0.7871.114.3-pro\chrome.exe

Launch options:
launch(headless=False, humanize=True, human_preset="careful", license_key=<redacted>,
stealth_args=True)
— also independently tested and failed identically with: headless=True,
stealth_args=False, humanize=False, no extra args, and with license_key omitted
entirely (falls back to same cached binary). Also reproduced launching the raw
chrome.exe binary directly (bypassing Playwright/the Python wrapper entirely) with
--remote-debugging-port — DevTools opens ("DevTools listening on ws://...") and the
process still exits within ~5s with no further output besides one harmless
`net\cert\ev_root_ca_metadata.cc` warning.

Tested with a different IP or proxy? No — this reproduces on the plain host network,
and the failure isn't network/site-specific (fails on example.com too), so this wasn't
pursued further.

Works outside Docker / on host machine? Not using Docker — this is on host machine only.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Have a valid free-tier license key with 1 concurrent session allowed.
2. Run several launch() calls in succession during normal dev/testing iteration,
   at least one of which is interrupted abruptly (Ctrl+C, crashed script, closed
   terminal) rather than reaching browser.close().
3. Run `python -m cloakbrowser info` — note "Sessions: 1 seat in use" despite no
   local process running.
4. Any subsequent launch() + goto() now fails with TargetClosedError, indefinitely,
   until the session times out or is cleared server-side.

Error output:
Launched OK. is_connected: True
Context created.
Page created. is_closed: False
Navigating...
playwright._impl._errors.TargetClosedError: Page.goto: Target page, context or browser has been closed
Call log:
  - navigating to "https://example.com/", waiting until "load"

Dockerfile (if applicable): N/A, not using Docker.

Additional notes:
Before concluding this was a stuck session, I ruled out every other explanation I
could check on this machine:
- Windows Defender: no threat detections near the crash times
- Defender Attack Surface Reduction rules: not even enabled on this machine
- AppLocker: nothing relevant logged
- SmartScreen: empty operational log
- Application crash events / crash dump files: none — it's exiting clean, not crashing
- validate_license(key) returns valid=True, plan='free'
- ~/.cloakbrowser config dir: writable, confirmed
- Network reachability to https://cloakbrowser.dev/api/license/validate: reachable (405
  on GET, as expected for a POST-only endpoint)
- A completely separate SeleniumBase/undetected_chromedriver Chrome instance launches
  and navigates fine on this same machine at the same time, so it's not a
  system-wide/Chrome-wide problem.

The only client-facing function related to sessions in the installed package is the
read-only `get_active_session_count(key)` in cloakbrowser.license — there's no
release_session()/end_session() exposed anywhere to clear this from the client side.

Would appreciate either: (a) a documented way to force-release a stuck session
client-side, (b) a shorter server-side timeout for abandoned sessions, or (c) launch()
raising CloakBrowserLicenseError immediately in this case instead of a silent
downstream Playwright error.

title: feat(docker): opt-in GPU acceleration via CLOAKBROWSER_GPU_ACCEL
body:
Supersedes #230 by @mvanhorn — keeps that PR's flag/env/JS/test scaffolding and docker-compose example, rebased onto current `main` (resolves its conflict). Closes #189.

#230 stalled on the one thing it couldn't test: a real GPU. I ran it end-to-end on an **NVIDIA RTX 3080 Ti** (host + inside the built image); it doesn't work as written, so this fixes two defects:

**1 — wrong Chrome flag.** `--use-gl=egl` was removed from modern Chromium (the shipped binaries are 146/150); it silently **disables WebGL** instead of enabling the GPU. Correct: `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl` (ANGLE over native EGL).

**2 — image missing the GLVND loader.** Even with the right flag, ANGLE fails with `Could not dlopen native EGL: libEGL.so.1`. The Dockerfile now installs `libglvnd0 libegl1 libgles2 libglx0 libopengl0`.

### Testing — NVIDIA RTX 3080 Ti (CDP `SystemInfo.getInfo` == `chrome://gpu`; util from `nvidia-smi`)

`launch(gpu_accel=True, headless=True)` / `CLOAKBROWSER_GPU_ACCEL=1`:

| Scenario | WebGL | Real backend | GPU util |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (flag off) | software | SwiftShader | 0% |
| **#230** `--use-gl=egl` | ❌ disabled | none | 0% |
| **this PR** `--use-angle=gl-egl` (host) | ✅ hardware | NVIDIA RTX 3080 Ti (OpenGL ES) | **91%** |
| **this PR, inside the built image** | ✅ hardware | NVIDIA RTX 3080 Ti | **90–93%** |
| flag on, no GPU | ❌ disabled | none | 0% — starts, no crash |

- `nvidia-smi` during a WebGL load shows the Chrome GPU process at ~90% util (149 W).
- **Scope, tested honestly:** acceleration engages on the **headless** `launch()` path (surfaceless EGL). Headed sessions rendered on the container's Xvfb stay on the software driver — Xvfb exposes no GPU display — so this is documented as headless-only rather than over-claimed for the CDP/session path.
- On a **no-GPU** container the flag doesn't crash but WebGL goes dark (no SwiftShader fallback) — worth knowing before enabling it without a GPU.
- The stealth WebGL-renderer spoof still holds with the GPU on (JS sees a Windows `D3D11` string; real backend is Linux `OpenGL ES`), so it doesn't leak the real renderer.
- Unit tests green: `pytest` (build_args flag matrix + `gpu_accel` forwarding, sync/async), `vitest` config matrix; `tsc` build clean.
