Updates `playwright-core` from 1.61.1 to 1.62.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright-core's releases.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });

await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.

await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

page.screenshot() and [locator.screenshot() (https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-screenshot) also accept webp as a type, where quality 100 (the default) is lossless and lower values use lossy compression.

🧩 Custom test filtering with Reporter.preprocess()

New reporter.preprocess() hook runs after the configuration is resolved and before reporter.onBegin(), letting a reporter mark individual tests as skipped, excluded, fixed, or failing through a TestRun object:

title: fix: preserve HTTP proxy credentials during GeoIP resolution
body:
## Summary

- Preserve HTTP proxy credentials during GeoIP and WebRTC exit-IP resolution.
- Reuse existing credential-aware proxy URL reconstruction in the JavaScript, Python, and .NET SDKs.
- Keep unauthenticated HTTP proxy behavior unchanged.
- Add regression tests, including a JavaScript CONNECT proxy authentication test.

## Testing

- JavaScript: `npm test -- tests/geoip.test.ts` — 17 passed
- JavaScript: `npm run typecheck` — passed
- Python: `uv run --extra dev --extra geoip pytest -q tests/test_proxy.py::TestMaybeResolveGeoip tests/test_geoip.py` — 40 passed
- .NET: `dotnet test dotnet/tests/CloakBrowser.Tests/CloakBrowser.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~ProxyResolverTests` — 12 passed

Closes #469

title: Preserve HTTP proxy credentials during GeoIP resolution
body:
When `geoip` is enabled and an authenticated HTTP proxy is provided with separate `username` and `password` fields, `extractProxyUrl()` returns only `proxy.server`. Unlike SOCKS proxies, the HTTP proxy URL is not reconstructed with its credentials.

`maybeResolveGeoip()` then uses this unauthenticated URL for GeoIP resolution. Because `Proxy-Authorization` is only added when credentials are present in the URL, the proxy rejects the CONNECT request with `407 Proxy Authentication Required`.

```javascript
{
  geoip: true,
  proxy: {
    server: "http://<proxy-host>:<proxy-port>",
    username: "<username>",
    password: "<password>"
  }
}
```

Relevant code:

- [`extractProxyUrl()` only reconstructs credentials for SOCKS proxies](https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/blob/093a6646016f7068ff1bcf92a7ec4fd226f694b0/js/src/geoip.ts#L414-L422)
- [`maybeResolveGeoip()` passes the extracted URL to GeoIP resolution](https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/blob/093a6646016f7068ff1bcf92a7ec4fd226f694b0/js/src/geoip.ts#L464)
- [`Proxy-Authorization` requires credentials in the proxy URL](https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/blob/093a6646016f7068ff1bcf92a7ec4fd226f694b0/js/src/geoip.ts#L262-L275)

Expected behavior: authenticated HTTP proxy objects should be reconstructed with their credentials before GeoIP resolution, just like authenticated SOCKS proxy objects.

> CloakBrowser version: `150.0.7871.114.3`  
> Wrapper: JavaScript (`cloakbrowser@0.4.11`)

title: fix(humanize): re-scroll after the settle wait so clicks land (#329)
body:
Fixes the real cause behind #329.

## Symptom

`humanize=True` silently misses clicks on pages that are still loading. No exception, the call returns as if it worked, and the click simply never happened.

## Root cause

The click pipeline scrolls the element into view, then waits for its position to settle if the page is reflowing. **It never scrolls again.** On a page that keeps reflowing, the element is pushed back off screen during that wait, so the coordinates we compute are outside the viewport and the click lands on nothing.

Instrumented run, `settle_ms=15000`, viewport 1920x959, on current `main`:

```
t= 4.65s  scroll_to_element EXIT   box y=607, did_scroll=True
t= 4.65s  ensure_stable ENTER
t=16.05s  ensure_stable EXIT ok             <- waited out the reflow, correctly
t=16.05s  check_pointer_events at (58,1238) <- y=1238, viewport is 959 tall
t=30.18s  check_pointer_events EXIT ok      <- 14s of retries, then failed open
t=31.50s  human_move EXIT
t=31.67s  mousedown y=1238 -> hit <HTML>
          err=NONE  clicked=False
```

The element was at y=607 when we scrolled. Eleven seconds later, when it finally stopped moving, it was at y=1219 — below the fold. We clicked at 1238.

A second defect made it silent rather than loud. `check_pointer_events` **correctly detected** there was no element at those coordinates and retried for 14 seconds. But its `bounding_box` timeout is computed as `max(1, min(deadline - now, 1000))`, so as the deadline approaches it clamps to ~1ms and always throws. The `except` treats a throw as indeterminate and fails open. A miss the check had already proven became "unknown", and the click was allowed through.

## What we tried first, and why it did not work

The obvious readings of #329 are all wrong, and each was tested before being discarded.

**Is the stability check too strict?** `_boxes_differ` has a 1px tolerance and retries with backoff, so it only fires on real movement. But it samples 100ms apart, where Playwright compares two consecutive animation frames (`rafCountForStablePosition()` returns 1 on Chromium). Rewrote it to match Playwright's definition using an in-page rAF comparison. Result: the check passed, and the click then **silently missed**. Loosening the check does not produce a landed click, it produces a click on whatever moved into that spot.

**Is the element moving during the mouse travel?** Added a re-aim step after `human_move`, re-reading the box and correcting. **Missed by 5px.** Changed it to re-aim at the element centre with an edge inset. **Missed by 12px, landed on `<HTML>`.**

At that point the numbers stopped making sense — the corrections were not converging on the element at all — which is what prompted instrumenting the pipeline stage by stage. That trace is above, and it showed the element was never on screen to begin with.

**Is our own scroll animation the cause?** Ruled out by measurement: a fully static page passes 20/20.

**Does #355's approach work?** Tested it directly. Swallowing `ElementNotStableError` lets `ensure_stable` consume the whole budget, so the next line's `bounding_box` gets `max(1, ~0)` and the user receives `Timeout 1ms exceeded` instead of a message describing the problem. Still fails, with a worse error. Declined in #355 with these results.

## The fix

**1. Re-scroll after the settle wait.** The existing `bounding_box()` re-read refreshed the coordinates but never checked they were still on screen. Replaced with the same `scroll_to_element` call already used before the wait. It returns `did_scroll=False` when the element is already visible, so it is a no-op on pages that never moved — which is why the static-page result is unchanged.

**2. Do not launder a confirmed miss.** `check_pointer_events` now remembers a *determined* miss. A later attempt that merely errored can no longer turn it into a pass at the deadline. Genuinely indeterminate results still fail open, exactly as before, since failing closed would block legitimate clicks.

## Results

Test page: button below the fold, content growing above it every 50ms, stopping after `settle_ms`. Real Chromium in Docker, default 30s click timeout.

| page reflows for | before | after (Python) | after (JS) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–5s | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| 10s | **silent miss, 32.5s** | PASS, 16.4s | PASS, 14.3s |
| 15s | **silent miss, 32.0s** | PASS, 19.9s | PASS, 19.9s |
| 20s | **silent miss, 32.6s** | PASS, 25.9s | PASS, 26.2s |
| 25s | **silent miss, 32.4s** | PASS, 30.7s | — |
| 30s+ | `ElementNotStableError` | `ElementNotStableError` | `ElementNotStableError` |
| static page ×20 | 20/20 | 20/20 | — |

Pages that reflow longer than the call's own timeout still raise, which is correct — the page never held still long enough to click.

## Scope

Python (sync + async), JavaScript, .NET. Click, dblclick, hover.

## Verification

- Python: 94 passed. The one failure is environmental, Playwright's own `chrome-headless-shell` is not installed on the dev machine.
- JavaScript: 512 passed across 16 files. Includes the existing `checkPointerEventsHandle still throws when genuinely covered` test, so the fail-open change did not open the closed path.
- .NET: builds clean. **Not runtime-verified**, `dotnet test` could not run locally. CI should exercise it.
- Browser sweep above run for both Python and JavaScript. JS matched Python at every row.

## Asking for a review and a test run

@evelaa123 you wrote most of this layer — could you review this and run it against your own setup?

1. **Test it on real pages you use humanize on.** This changes the click path for every `click`, `dblclick` and `hover` under `humanize=True`, so it touches everything. We verified on a synthetic reflowing page and a static one, not against real sites. If you have flows that were intermittently missing clicks, this is the change most likely to move them, in either direction.
2. **Does the second scroll read as natural?** It emits real wheel input where previously there was only a box read. It fires only when the element is genuinely off screen, and scrolling again is what a person would do, but you have the better instinct for this.
3. **Is the fail-open line drawn in the right place?** The comment at the original `except` says failing closed would block legitimate clicks, and I did not want to undo that reasoning — only to stop a *proven* miss being reclassified.

The repro is one HTML file plus a script. Say the word and I will attach both so you can reproduce before and after directly.

@eofreternal this touches the pointer-events check from #303 — the iframe offset logic is untouched, only the fail-open branch. A look at that part would be appreciated.

## Not included

No regression test in the suites. The mocked unit tests cannot catch this — they do not observe whether the click landed, which is why this survived. It needs a real-browser test asserting a click handler fired. Happy to add one here rather than as a follow-up.

Updates `playwright-core` from 1.61.1 to 1.62.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright-core's releases.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });

await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.

await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

page.screenshot() and [locator.screenshot() (https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-screenshot) also accept webp as a type, where quality 100 (the default) is lossless and lower values use lossy compression.

🧩 Custom test filtering with Reporter.preprocess()

New reporter.preprocess() hook runs after the configuration is resolved and before reporter.onBegin(), letting a reporter mark individual tests as skipped, excluded, fixed, or failing through a TestRun object:

title: CreepJS detects 3 lies: Canvas, DOMRect, Audio cross-scope inconsistencies
body:
## Description

When running CloakBrowser v146.0.7680.177.5 (linux-x64, free tier) in a Docker container under Xvfb, CreepJS consistently reports 3 spoofing inconsistencies (lies) for Canvas 2d, DOMRect, and Audio. All other detection sites (deviceandbrowserinfo, sannysoft, browserleaks, pixelscan, nowsecure, incolumitas) pass cleanly — `isBot: false`, `webdriver: false`, WebGL renderer spoofed correctly.

## CreepJS finding detail

```
3 spoofing inconsistency(ies):
  - 1053.00ms Canvas 2d<hash> data: <hash>
  - 15.20ms DOMRect<hash> elems A: 0.24583
  - 993.70ms Audio<hash> sum: 124.04346828
```

Verdict is WARN (not FAIL), severity is manageable, but worth investigating.

## Analysis

Tested the specific APIs across main thread and Worker scopes:

| API | Main Thread | Worker |
|-----|------------|--------|
| OfflineAudioContext | Present (patched value: 124.043472...) | **Not defined** |
| AudioContext | Present | **Not defined** |
| OffscreenCanvas | Present | Present |
| Canvas 2d output | 3078 bytes (patched) | 2219 bytes (unpatched) |
| DOMRect | Present (patched) | Present |

Key observations:

1. **AudioContext/OfflineAudioContext removed from Workers** — in normal Chrome 150 (system Chromium, same container), these are also absent from Workers, so this isn't CloakBrowser-specific. However, the main thread's audio fingerprint sum (124.043472...) is a patched value that CreepJS likely cross-references against known hardware profiles.

2. **Canvas output differs** — main thread Canvas (via `document.createElement("canvas")`) produces 3078-byte output vs Worker OffscreenCanvas producing 2219-byte output. System Chromium produces 2970 bytes in the main thread. The CloakBrowser patched output (3078 bytes) doesn't match the expected rendering for the spoofed GPU (e.g. NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060).

3. **The lies likely come from the patched fingerprint values not being internally consistent** with the claimed GPU profile. CloakBrowser's `--fingerprint=<seed>` randomizes Canvas, Audio, DOMRect values, but the combination doesn't match any known real hardware fingerprint that CreepJS has in its database.

## Environment

- CloakBrowser: v146.0.7680.177.5 (linux-x64, free tier)
- Container: Docker linux/amd64
- Display: Xvfb :99 (1920x1080x24)
- Launch args: `--no-sandbox --fingerprint=<random> --fingerprint-platform=windows --ignore-gpu-blocklist --disable-dev-shm-usage`
- Mode: headful (not headless)

## Questions

1. Is this a known limitation of the seed-based fingerprint randomization approach?
2. Is there a way to generate fingerprints that are internally consistent with a claimed GPU's expected rendering behavior?
3. Would using `stealth_args=False` and providing custom `--fingerprint-*` flags from a curated real-device profile database reduce the lies?

## Impact

Low-medium. Most anti-bot systems don't use CreepJS-level cross-reference analysis. All major detection sites (deviceandbrowserinfo, sannysoft, pixelscan, nowsecure) report `isBot: false`. The WARN verdict is acceptable for most production use cases.

title: GeoIP cache refresh fails on Windows, causing repeated 70 MB downloads on every launch
body:
## Summary

After the cached GeoIP database becomes older than 30 days, every GeoIP-enabled browser launch downloads the approximately 70 MB database again.

The download does not successfully replace the existing database on Windows, so the cache remains stale and the same download is triggered indefinitely.

Launching many profiles can therefore cause many repeated or concurrent downloads of the same shared file.

## Root cause

The issue is caused by the combination of two problems in `geoip.py`.

### 1. The existing database cannot be replaced on Windows

When the database is older than `GEOIP_UPDATE_INTERVAL`, `_maybe_trigger_update()` starts a background download:

```python
_download_geoip_db(db_path)
```

After downloading, `_download_geoip_db()` attempts to update the existing database with:

```python
tmp_path.rename(dest)
```

On Windows, `Path.rename()` cannot overwrite an existing destination file. It raises `FileExistsError`/`WinError 183` when `GeoLite2-City.mmdb` already exists.

The background thread catches this exception and logs it only at debug level:

```python
except Exception:
    logger.debug("Background GeoIP update failed", exc_info=True)
```

As a result:

1. The full database is downloaded.
2. Replacing the existing database fails.
3. The temporary download is deleted.
4. The old database modification time remains unchanged.
5. The database is still considered older than 30 days.
6. The next browser launch starts another full download.

This creates an endless download loop after the cache first expires.

### 2. There is no update-in-progress guard

Every call to `_maybe_trigger_update()` creates a new thread when the database is stale:

```python
threading.Thread(target=_bg, daemon=True).start()
```

There is no lock or shared "update in progress" state.

If many profiles are launched while the cache is stale, every launch can start another approximately 70 MB download.

The initial download has a similar race: multiple callers can all see that the database does not exist and begin downloading it simultaneously.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- CloakBrowser tested: `0.3.31`
- The same affected logic appears to still be present in `0.4.12`
- Cache file: `~/.cloakbrowser/geoip/GeoLite2-City.mmdb`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable `geoip=True` and configure a proxy.
2. Ensure `GeoLite2-City.mmdb` exists and is older than 30 days.
3. Launch a browser profile.
4. Observe the GeoIP database download.
5. After the download finishes, check the database modification time.
6. Launch the profile again.

The database modification time remains unchanged and the complete download starts again.

Example logs:

```text
cloakbrowser INFO GeoIP download: 79 %
cloakbrowser INFO GeoIP download: 89 %
cloakbrowser INFO GeoIP download: 99 %
```

When multiple profiles are launched, multiple copies of these download sequences can appear.

## Expected behavior

- Only one refresh should run when the database becomes stale.
- Other launches should continue using the existing database.
- The downloaded database should atomically replace the existing file on Windows.
- Concurrent launches should not start duplicate downloads.

## Suggested fix

Use `os.replace()` or `Path.replace()` instead of `Path.rename()`:

```python
tmp_path.replace(dest)
```

Also add a process-wide lock or update state so only one initial download or background refresh can run at a time.

For stale databases, the existing database should remain usable while one background refresh is running. If the refresh fails, the existing database should be retained and retries should be rate-limited.

title: fix(cli): run main() when invoked via a symlinked bin (npx) (#427)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #427 — `npx cloakbrowser info` (and every subcommand) produced no output and exited 0. The CLI entry guard compared `import.meta.url` against `pathToFileURL(invokedPath)` but only realpathed the invoked side; under npx/pnpm-exec the bin is a symlink (`node_modules/.bin/cloakbrowser` -> `dist/cli.js`) and the two realpaths did not match, so `main()` never ran.

## Fix
- js/src/cli.ts: extract `isCliEntry(invokedPath, metaUrl)` which realpaths **both** sides before comparing and returns `false` (never auto-running `main()`) on any resolution error. The module-level guard now uses it.
- js/tests/cli.test.ts: unit tests for `isCliEntry` — symlink resolution, missing path, unrelated file, and undefined `argv[1]`.

## Validation
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/cli.test.ts` -> 6 passed.
- End-to-end: a symlinked bin shim invoking `dist/cli.js` now prints `CloakBrowser diagnostics` (exit 0) instead of silently exiting. Importing `cli.js` in tests does NOT auto-run `main()` (the import-by-test case stays safe).
- `tsc` build clean.

Closes #427.

title: Feature Request: `pxBypass=True` — Automatic PerimeterX Challenge Detection & Bypass
body:
### Feature Request: `pxBypass=True` — Automatic PerimeterX Challenge Detection & Bypass

**Problem**

PerimeterX (PX) is one of the most aggressive anti-bot vendors in production use today. It deploys:

- Cookie-challenge walls (JS challenge + fingerprint collection)
- CAPTCHA-style confirmation popups
- Behavioral scoring that varies per session

Even with CloakBrowser's source-level C++ patches + `humanize=True`, PerimeterX often:
1. Serves a challenge page that requires clicking a "Confirm" / "I am human" button
2. Scores the session based on challenge-solving behavior
3. Drops sessions that fail to interact with the challenge naturally

Issue #100 and #419 already confirm this as a known pain point.

**Proposed API**

```python
browser = launch(
    proxy="http://user:***@residential-proxy:port",
    geoip=True,
    headless=False,
    humanize=True,
    pxBypass=True,  # <-- new flag
)

title: navigator.connection returns unrealistic values (downlink=10, rtt=0) when launched with HTTP proxy
body:
```markdown
## Description

`navigator.connection.downlink` and `navigator.connection.rtt` return unrealistic values when CloakBrowser is launched with a browser-level HTTP proxy.

With the same Docker container, same Xvfb environment, same proxy, and same test page:

- Stock Chromium reports normal values, e.g. `downlink ~= 1.7`, `rtt ~= 300`
- CloakBrowser reports `downlink = 10`, `rtt = 0`

This makes CloakBrowser distinguishable from stock Chromium on sites that collect Network Information API signals.

## Environment

- CloakBrowser version: `0.4.10`
- Cloak Chromium version: `146.0.7680.177.5`
- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)
- Runtime: Docker + Xvfb
- Browser mode: headed
- Proxy type: browser-level HTTP proxy
- Proxy example: `--proxy-server=http://host.docker.internal:18081`

## Reproduction

### 1. CloakBrowser with proxy

```python
import asyncio
import tempfile
from cloakbrowser import launch_persistent_context_async

async def main():
    context = await launch_persistent_context_async(
        user_data_dir=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="cloak-nqe-"),
        headless=False,
        proxy="http://host.docker.internal:18081",
        args=[
            "--no-sandbox",
            "--fingerprint=123456",
            "--fingerprint-platform=windows",
        ],
    )

    page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()
    await page.goto("https://browserleaks.com/javascript", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
    await page.wait_for_timeout(3000)

    result = await page.evaluate("""
        () => ({
            userAgent: navigator.userAgent,
            webdriver: navigator.webdriver,
            connection: navigator.connection ? {
                effectiveType: navigator.connection.effectiveType,
                downlink: navigator.connection.downlink,
                rtt: navigator.connection.rtt,
                saveData: navigator.connection.saveData,
                type: navigator.connection.type || null,
            } : null,
        })
    """)

    print(result)
    await context.close()

asyncio.run(main())
```

Observed result:

```json
{
  "webdriver": false,
  "connection": {
    "effectiveType": "3g",
    "downlink": 10,
    "rtt": 0,
    "saveData": false,
    "type": null
  }
}
```

### 2. Stock Chromium with the same proxy

In the same Docker container, using Debian Chromium:

```bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends chromium
```

Then launch stock Chromium with the same proxy:

```python
import asyncio
import json
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile
import urllib.request
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async def wait_http(port):
    for _ in range(150):
        try:
            return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/json/version", timeout=1))
        except Exception:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
    raise RuntimeError("CDP not ready")

async def main():
    port = 9662
    user_data = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="raw-chromium-")
    args = [
        "/usr/bin/chromium",
        f"--remote-debugging-port={port}",
        "--remote-allow-origins=*",
        f"--user-data-dir={user_data}",
        "--no-first-run",
        "--no-default-browser-check",
        "--no-sandbox",
        "--proxy-server=http://host.docker.internal:18081",
        "data:text/html,<html>probe</html>",
    ]

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["DISPLAY"] = os.environ.get("DISPLAY", ":99")

    proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, env=env)

    try:
        await wait_http(port)

        async with async_playwright() as pw:
            browser = await pw.chromium.connect_over_cdp(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}")
            context = browser.contexts[0]
            page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else await context.new_page()

            await page.goto("https://browserleaks.com/javascript", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
            await page.wait_for_timeout(3000)

            result = await page.evaluate("""
                () => ({
                    userAgent: navigator.userAgent,
                    webdriver: navigator.webdriver,
                    connection: navigator.connection ? {
                        effectiveType: navigator.connection.effectiveType,
                        downlink: navigator.connection.downlink,
                        rtt: navigator.connection.rtt,
                    } : null,
                })
            """)

            print(result)
            await browser.close()
    finally:
        proc.terminate()

asyncio.run(main())
```

Observed stock Chromium result:

```json
{
  "webdriver": false,
  "connection": {
    "effectiveType": "3g",
    "downlink": 1.7,
    "rtt": 300
  }
}
```

## Additional Notes

I also captured Chrome NetLog from CloakBrowser.

The underlying Network Quality Estimator appears to have reasonable values, for example:

```json
{
  "name": "NETWORK_QUALITY_CHANGED",
  "params": {
    "downstream_throughput_kbps": 1400,
    "effective_connection_type": "3G",
    "http_rtt_ms": 308,
    "transport_rtt_ms": 125
  }
}
```

But the JavaScript-exposed Network Information API still returns:

```json
{
  "downlink": 10,
  "rtt": 0
}
```

So the issue seems to be in the JS-exposed `navigator.connection` layer, not the underlying network measurement.

## Expected Behavior

CloakBrowser should expose Network Information API values that are consistent with stock Chromium under the same proxy/environment, or provide explicit fingerprint flags to control these values.

For example:

```json
{
  "effectiveType": "3g",
  "downlink": 1.5,
  "rtt": 250
}
```

instead of:

```json
{
  "effectiveType": "3g",
  "downlink": 10,
  "rtt": 0
}
```
```

title: fix: allow shared playwright instance across launch calls
body:
each launch_context_async() call spawns its own node.js driver process. calling it multiple times creates multiple processes — more memory, more cpu, more overhead. this is an api misuse that the current api silently enables.

adds optional playwright= parameter to launch(), launch_async(), launch_context(), and launch_context_async(). when provided, reuses the existing driver process instead of spawning a new one. caller owns the lifecycle — closing a context with a shared instance does not stop the playwright driver.

before:
`
ctx1 = await launch_context_async()
ctx2 = await launch_context_async()  # second node.js process
`

after:
`
async with async_playwright() as p:
    ctx1 = await launch_context_async(playwright=p)
    ctx2 = await launch_context_async(playwright=p)  # shared driver
`

title: Performance issues when creating multiple async_playwright() instances
body:
When creating multiple instances of async_playwright() in a single application, there are significant performance and resource consumption issues. Each instance spawns a separate Node.js driver process, leading to excessive memory usage and CPU overhead.

```
import asyncio
from cloakbrowser import launch_context_async


async def main():
    ctx1 = await launch_context_async()
    ctx2 = await launch_context_async()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

Expected Behavior:
The documentation should clearly warn against creating multiple async_playwright() instances and provide guidance on the recommended pattern: using a single instance with multiple browsers/contexts.

Actual Behavior:
Each async_playwright() instance creates a separate Node.js driver process
Memory consumption increases linearly with each instance
Initialization overhead for each instance (several hundred milliseconds)
Risk of hitting OS limits (file descriptors, ports) with many instances

The recommended approach is:
```
import asyncio
from cloakbrowser import launch_context_async
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright


async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        ctx1 = await launch_context_async(playwright=p)
        ctx2 = await launch_context_async(playwright=p)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

title: Add community Rust client (rust/)
body:
## Community Rust client

Adds a **Rust** wrapper under `rust/`, following the same monorepo conventions as the first-party `.NET` client (`dotnet/`, PR #385): self-contained crate + CLI + examples + unit tests, built on [`playwright-rs`](https://crates.io/crates/playwright-rs).

This is a faithful port of the open-source wrapper surface (not the Chromium binary). Behavior targets parity with Python / JS / .NET for launch flags, download verification, Pro routing, proxy/GeoIP/WebRTC, and humanized input.

### Conventions followed

- **Layout:** `rust/` at the repo root, alongside `cloakbrowser/` (Python), `js/`, and `dotnet/`. Workspace with `cloakbrowser` (lib) + `cloakbrowser-cli` (bin) + examples.
- **Versioning:** wrapper version `0.4.10`, matching the current monorepo release.
- **Docs:** `rust/README.md` is the client guide (feature matrix, API, env vars, Python→Rust mapping). Root README gets a short Install blurb + Latest bullet; `CHANGELOG.md` has an **[Unreleased]** entry.
- **CI:** new `rust` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo test -p cloakbrowser --lib` (browser-free unit tests).

### What's ported

| Area | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Binary lifecycle | Download / cache / auto-update; pinned **Ed25519** on `SHA256SUMS.sig` + SHA-256; version binding (anti-downgrade); zip-slip guard |
| Launch | Stealth args, ignore automation defaults, proxy HTTP/HTTPS + SOCKS5 (inline creds gated by binary version), GeoIP timezone/locale, WebRTC `=auto`, extensions, license env injection |
| Pro | `license_key` / `CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY` / `~/.cloakbrowser/license.key`; 24h cache; Pro path never silently falls back to free on verification failure |
| Persistent context | `launch_persistent_context` + viewport auto/`Size`/`NoViewport`; Linux **Widevine** hint seeding |
| Humanize | Explicit `HumanPage` (Bezier mouse, typing + CDP shift symbols, scroll bursts). Rust cannot monkey-patch Playwright's sealed `Page` — same design pressure as .NET's decorator layer |
| CLI | `install` / `info` / `update` / `clear-cache` |

### Not in this PR (intentionally)

- Transparent Playwright interface wrapping for *every* `Page` method (would be a large generator like the .NET Roslyn source generator). Callers use `new_human_page()` / `HumanPage` for humanized actions and `page()` for the raw Playwright surface.
- crates.io publish / release automation (happy for maintainers to own packaging).
- Full actionability matrix / iframe humanize parity with the latest Python frame-routing work.

### Tests

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p cloakbrowser --lib   # 34 passed
cargo clippy -p cloakbrowser --lib -- -D warnings
```

Coverage includes version pins, checksum/manifest parsing, zip-slip, stealth arg composition, proxy SOCKS/HTTP resolution, viewport defaults, Bézier math, keyboard nearby-key map, Widevine no-ops, and license env injection.

### Build & try locally

```bash
cd rust
cargo run -p cloakbrowser-cli -- install
cargo run -p cloakbrowser-cli -- info --quick
cargo run --example basic -p cloakbrowser
cargo run --example humanize -p cloakbrowser
cargo run --example persistent_context -p cloakbrowser
```

Happy to adjust naming, CI pins, docs wording, or drop root-README/CHANGELOG touches if you'd rather land those in a follow-up (the .NET PR originally left those to maintainers).

title: [Bug] Fails BrowserScan authenticity test with 70% score (WebGL & Audio exceptions)
body: ### Description When running CloakBrowser and testing it on `https://www.browserscan.net/`, the browser fails to achieve a high authenticity score, resulting in only a **70% fingerprint authenticity score**. BrowserScan flags multiple fingerprinting and configuration issues that are supposed to be masked by CloakBrowser: 1. **Different time zones (-10%):** There is a mismatch between the IP-based timezone (`Asia/Almaty`) and the JavaScript-reported timezone (`Asia/Qyzylorda`). Even though both are technically UTC+5 now, the string identifiers do not match, causing a penalty. 2. **WebGL exception (-5%):** The spoofed GPU (`ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU...)`) triggers a WebGL exception, indicating the WebGL context is corrupted or throwing errors during fingerprinting. 3. **Audio exception (-5%):** BrowserScan detects that the audio parameters are not functioning properly and have been manually modified ("Your Audio is not functioning properly. Your Audio appears to have been modified manually."). 4. **Incognito mode detection (-10%):** The browser is successfully detected as running in Incognito mode. --- ### CloakBrowser version 1.4.6 [Free build] python module 0.4.10 --- ### Wrapper Python (Playwright) --- ### Environment - **OS:** Windows 11 - **Docker:** No - **Architecture:** x86_64 --- ### Launch options ```python # Insert your exact launch code here, for example: browser = launch(headless=False, humanize=True) # or if you used proxy/geoip: # browser = launch(headless=False, humanize=True, geoip=True) ``` --- ### Tested with a different IP or proxy? Yes (same result) --- ### Works outside Docker / on host machine? Yes (not using Docker) --- ### Steps to reproduce 1. Initialize `cloakbrowser` with headed mode. 2. Navigate to `https://www.browserscan.net/`. 3. Wait for the browser fingerprint authenticity scan to complete. 4. Expand the details to see the penalties: - Different time zones (-10%) - WebGL exception (-5%) - Audio exception (-5%) - Incognito mode (-10%) --- ### Error output / screenshots Please find the attached screenshots showing the specific test failures: - **Overall Score (70%):** - **Detected Penalties (Timezone, WebGL, Audio, Incognito):** - **Timezone Mismatch Detail (Asia/Almaty vs Asia/Qyzylorda):** - **WebGL & Audio Exception Details:** - **Incognito Mode Detail:** --- ### Additional notes The timezone mismatch is particularly tricky since Kazakhstan standardized all its regions to UTC+5 in 2024. However, BrowserScan still flags a mismatch if the exact timezone strings (`Asia/Almaty` and `Asia/Qyzylorda`) do not align. The WebGL and Audio exceptions indicate that the underlying Chromium source-level patches might be throwing API errors when queried by advanced fingerprinting scripts.

> "Oops! You've landed here by mistake."



(or occasionally fails to establish a trusted session.)



However, if we take the **same residential proxy** and configure it using the **Bright Data Chrome Extension** in a regular Chrome browser, the exact same URL opens successfully without showing the "Oops" page.



## What we've verified



- Same residential proxy provider (Bright Data)

- Same country (Japan)

- Same target URL

- Same machine

- Same network

- Chromium 146 (CloakBrowser)



The main difference appears to be:



**Native Chrome + Bright Data Extension**

- Page opens normally



**CloakBrowser**

- Frequently reaches the Jetstar "Oops! You've landed here by mistake." page



## Leak audit observations



While investigating, we noticed a few potential differences:



- Host OpenGL reports `llvmpipe`, while JavaScript WebGL reports an Apple GPU profile.

- BrowserScan reports an Incognito flag.

- BrowserScan reports a WebGL exception.

- WebRTC correctly matches the proxy IP.

- `navigator.webdriver` is false.

- No Playwright or `cdc_` markers were detected.

- Timezone and locale match the proxy.



We're not claiming these are the cause, but they seemed worth mentioning.



## Question



Have you seen similar behavior where:



- Native Chrome succeeds

- CloakBrowser behaves differently under the same residential proxy



Is there any recommended configuration that we should try?



For example:



- `fingerprint-noise`

- `humanize`

- `geoip`

- GPU/WebGL configuration

- launch flags

- persistent context options

- anything else specific to CloakBrowser



If this is something you'd like us to test, we're happy to run experiments and provide logs.



Thanks!

title: Feature Request: Add connect() API with humanize support for remote CDP browser control
body:
## Feature Request: Remote CDP connection with humanize support

### Problem

Currently `cloakbrowser` only exports `launch*` functions (`launch()`, `launch_async()`, `launch_persistent_context()`, etc.) that start a **local** browser instance. There is no way to connect to an **already running** CloakBrowser instance (e.g., one started via `cloakserve` in Docker) and still have `humanize` behavior work.

The Docker Hub docs show this pattern for remote CDP:

```python
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
pw = sync_playwright().start()
browser = pw.chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://localhost:9222")
```

But this uses **stock Playwright** directly -- no `humanize` support, no stealth args, no convenience.

### Architecture Analysis

Looking at the source code in `browser.py`, the `humanize` behavior is applied via `patch_browser()` from `cloakbrowser.human`, and it operates on a standard Playwright `Browser` object. Since `connect_over_cdp()` also returns a standard Playwright `Browser` object, the `patch_browser()` function would work on remote connections too -- the browser origin (local vs remote CDP) does not matter.

The C++ fingerprint patches are in the binary (persist regardless of connection method), and the humanize behavior simulation is in the SDK wrapper -- so combining them across a remote CDP connection is perfectly feasible.

### Proposed API

A simple `connect()` function (and its async variant) that mirrors `launch()` but connects to an existing CDP endpoint:

```python
from cloakbrowser import connect

# Connect to a CloakBrowser instance running in Docker
browser = connect(
    cdp_url="http://localhost:9222",
    humanize=True,
    human_preset="careful",
)
page = browser.new_page()
page.goto("https://example.com")
page.click("#btn")  # humanize works via patch_browser()
browser.close()
```

The implementation would be straightforward -- essentially the same as `launch()` but using `pw.chromium.connect_over_cdp(cdp_url)` instead of `pw.chromium.launch(executable_path=...)`:

```python
def connect(
    cdp_url: str,
    humanize: bool = False,
    human_preset: HumanPreset = "default",
    human_config: HumanConfigOverrides | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> Any:
    from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
    pw = sync_playwright().start()
    browser = pw.chromium.connect_over_cdp(cdp_url, **kwargs)

    if humanize:
        from .human import patch_browser
        from .human.config import resolve_config
        cfg = resolve_config(human_preset, human_config)
        patch_browser(browser, cfg)

    return browser
```

### Use Cases

1. **Docker deployment**: Run the CloakBrowser binary in a Docker container (`cloakserve`), connect from the host or another container with full humanize support
2. **Multi-language**: Connect from Python/JS to a CloakBrowser instance running on another machine
3. **Orchestration**: Manage a pool of CloakBrowser instances centrally, workers connect remotely
4. **CloakBrowser-Manager integration**: Connect to browsers launched via the Manager web UI with humanize enabled

### Why not just use `patch_browser` manually?

Users can already do this manually by importing from `cloakbrowser.human`, but it requires knowing the internal module structure. A first-class `connect()` function would:
- Provide a discoverable, documented API
- Handle Playwright instance lifecycle (start/stop) automatically like `launch()` does
- Maintain API consistency with the existing `launch()` interface

Would love to hear the maintainers' thoughts on this. Happy to submit a PR if the approach sounds good.

body:
## Environment

python3 -m cloakbrowser info

```
Version:   145.0.7632.109.2 (free)

License:   Free
```

## Proxy

Authenticated HTTP proxy.

Format:

```
proxy.soax.com:1337:USERNAME:PASSWORD
```

Converted to:

```python
proxy = {
    "server": "http://proxy.soax.com:1337",
    "username": "...",
    "password": "...",
}
```

---

## Expected behavior

According to the README:

> launch_persistent_context() supports all the same options as launch_context(), including proxy.

I expect both APIs to behave the same.

---

## Actual behavior

### launch_context()

Works correctly.

```python
from cloakbrowser import launch_context

ctx = launch_context(
    headless=False,
    proxy=proxy,
)

page = ctx.new_page()
page.goto("https://api.ipify.org")
print(page.text_content("body"))
```

Result:

```
<public ip>
```

---

### launch_persistent_context()

Fails immediately.

```python
from cloakbrowser import launch_persistent_context

ctx = launch_persistent_context(
    "./profile_test",
    headless=False,
    proxy=proxy,
)

page = ctx.new_page()
page.goto("https://api.ipify.org")
```

Result:

```
playwright._impl._errors.Error:

Page.goto:
net::ERR_PROXY_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED
```

Full message:

```
Page.goto: net::ERR_PROXY_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED at https://api.ipify.org/
```

---

## Additional information

The exact same proxy works with:

- launch() ✅
- launch_context() ✅

Only launch_persistent_context() fails.

The failure occurs before any website loads, so it does not appear to be website-specific.

I can reproduce this consistently with a fresh profile directory.

title: How to set the default search engine (omnibox search) for a launched profile?
body:
Hi, thanks for CloakBrowser (using 0.4.8, .NET, Chromium 146, via LaunchPersistentContextAsync).

**Problem**
In a launched profile, the default search engine is a built-in entry named **"No Search"** whose search URL is literally `http://{searchTerms}`. So when a user types a non-URL query in the omnibox, the browser navigates to `http://<query>` (e.g. a number becomes an IP like `0.0.48.25`) instead of doing a web search.

The prepopulated engine list contains Yahoo / Bing / Baidu / CocCoc but **no normal Google**, and Google-related domains in other entries appear obfuscated (e.g. `9oo91e.qjz9zk`). I assume this is intentional anti-fingerprint behavior.

**What I tried (all reverted / not viable)**
- Writing `default_search_provider_data` into `Default/Preferences` → reverted on next launch (tracked-preference MAC protection resets it).
- Editing the `keywords` table in `Web Data` → overwritten from the prepopulated data on startup.
- Chrome enterprise policy (`DefaultSearchProviderSearchURL`) → needs admin / registry.
- Driving `chrome://settings/searchEngines` via the WebUI → works but is fragile (per-profile UI language differs, validation edge cases).

**Question**
Is there a supported/intended way to set the default search engine (e.g. Google) for a launched profile — via `LaunchContextOptions`, a Chromium flag in `Args`, an `initial_preferences` mechanism, or a `search_provider_overrides` hook?

If not, would you consider adding an option such as `DefaultSearchEngine` / `SearchProviderOverrides` / `Homepage`, or documenting a recommended approach? Many users expect normal omnibox search.

Thanks!

title: fix: humanize=True resolves iframe locators in the owning frame (#428)
body:
Fixes #428.

## Problem

With `humanize=True`, any `Locator` action on an element **inside an iframe** (`frame.locator("#btn").click()`, `fill()`, `hover()`, …) failed with `cloakbrowser.human.actionability.ElementNotAttachedError: element not found in DOM`. Native Playwright (`humanize=False`) clicked the same element fine.

## Root cause

The humanize layer resolved every selector against the **main frame**, never the owning sub-frame. Two independent misroutes in `cloakbrowser/human/__init__.py`:

1. **Locator wrapper** — `_humanized_click` etc. called `self.page.click(self._impl_obj._selector, …)`. A frame locator's `.page` is the *main* Page, so `#btn` was searched on the top document.
2. **Frame wrapper** — `_frame_click(sel)` → `page.click(sel)`, discarding the frame identity.

The mouse half was already cross-frame-correct (`bounding_box()` on a frame locator returns page/viewport-space coords), so only *element resolution* was wrong.

## Fix (keeps humanization inside iframes)

Mirrors the design already shipping in the JS wrapper:

- **Frame wrapper** now resolves through `frame.locator(selector)`, does a native `scroll_into_view_if_needed`, reads the page-space `bounding_box`, detects input type in the frame's own context, then runs the **humanized** Bézier mouse-move + human click on the page-level mouse (native-frame fallback if the box can't be read).
- **Locator wrapper** routes a sub-frame locator to its owning frame's now-humanized method; main-frame locators are unchanged (still go through the Page — byte-for-byte the same path). Unknown/detached frames fall back to native Playwright (frame-correct).

Sync **and** async. No changes to the page-level primitives, so the main-frame path carries zero regression risk.

The JS and .NET wrappers were already frame-correct — this is a **Python-only** change (verified by running a real same-origin iframe through all three wrappers).

## Testing

- **New unit tests** (mocked, no binary): sub-frame Locator routing (sub-frame → owning frame, main-frame → page, unpatched → native), frame-humanized resolution + native fallback, sync + async.
- **New integration tests** (`@pytest.mark.slow`, real binary, local same-origin iframe over HTTP): humanized click + fill inside an iframe, async click, and a `humanize=False` parity control.
- Existing humanize unit suite: **71 passed** (no main-frame regression).
- On the v148 Pro binary in Docker: the 4 new iframe integration tests pass; pre-existing humanize browser tests pass; matrix **group 9 (Humanize)** and groups **1/2/3/5** = **57/57 passed, 0 failed**.

## Ask

@evelaa123 — as the humanize layer's main author, could you review this and re-run the humanize tests on your side (especially the new iframe integration tests, and any humanize flows you rely on)? Would like a second pair of eyes on the frame-routing before it merges.

title: [Bug] Locator click/fill/etc inside subframes (iframes) fails with ElementNotAttachedError when humanize=True
body:
## Description
When `humanize=True` is enabled, all `Locator` interaction methods (such as `click()`, `fill()`, `hover()`, etc.) fail with an `ElementNotAttachedError` (or `TimeoutError`) if the element is located inside a subframe (iframe).

This occurs because `cloakbrowser`'s class-level patching on `Locator` redirects the interaction to the main `Page` object (e.g. `self.page.click(selector)`), which evaluates the selector on the top-level document rather than within the iframe context.

## Steps to Reproduce

Create a simple page with an iframe and attempt to click a button inside it:

```python
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
from cloakbrowser import launch_context

with sync_playwright() as p:
    # 1. Start context with humanize=True
    context = launch_context(headless=True, humanize=True)
    page = context.new_page()

    # 2. Set page content with an iframe containing a button
    html_content = "<html><body><iframe name='myframe' srcdoc='<html><body><button id=\"btn\">Click Me</button></body></html>'></iframe></body></html>"
    page.goto(f"data:text/html,{html_content}")
    page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded")

    # 3. Locate the button inside the iframe
    frame = page.frame(name="myframe")
    button_locator = frame.locator("#btn")

    # 4. Attempt to click
    print("Clicking button in iframe...")
    try:
        button_locator.click(timeout=3000)
        print("Success!")
    except Exception as e:
        print("Failed with exception:")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()

    context.close()
```

### Expected Behavior
The button inside the iframe should be clicked successfully.

### Actual Behavior
The script raises a `cloakbrowser.human.actionability.ElementNotAttachedError` because the click is routed to the main page where the selector `#btn` does not exist:

```text
playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Locator.wait_for: Timeout 2000ms exceeded.
...
cloakbrowser.human.actionability.ElementNotAttachedError: Element "#btn" failed attached check: element not found in DOM
```

---

## Root Cause Analysis

In `cloakbrowser/human/__init__.py`, inside `_patch_locator_class_sync()`:
```python
def _is_humanized(self):
    return hasattr(self.page, '_original')

def _humanized_click(self, **kwargs):
    if _is_humanized(self):
        self.page.click(_get_selector(self), **_forward_kwargs(kwargs))
    else:
        _orig_click(self, **kwargs)
```

1. Even if a locator is created from a subframe (e.g. `frame.locator("#btn")`), its `self.page` property still returns the main `Page` object. Since the main page has `_original` attached, `_is_humanized(self)` evaluates to `True`.
2. As a result, `_humanized_click` delegates the click to `self.page.click(...)`.
3. `self.page.click` runs the check on the main page DOM instead of the frame DOM, failing to find the selector.

The same issue affects all patched locator methods: `fill`, `type`, `hover`, `dblclick`, `check`, `uncheck`, `set_checked`, `select_option`, `press`, `press_sequentially`, and `clear`.

---

## Proposed Fix / Workaround

Before routing the call to the humanized page method, check if the locator belongs to a subframe. If it does, bypass the humanized layer and fallback to the native Playwright method (which supports frame contexts natively), or route it through the correct frame instance:

```python
def create_wrapped_method(name, orig_method):
    def wrapped(self, *args, **kwargs):
        # Check if the locator's frame is different from the main frame
        impl_frame = getattr(self._impl_obj, '_frame', None)
        page_impl = getattr(self.page, '_impl_obj', None)
        main_frame = getattr(page_impl, 'main_frame', None) if page_impl else None
        
        is_subframe = impl_frame and main_frame and (impl_frame != main_frame)
        
        if is_subframe:
            # Temporarily hide '_original' to force fallback to native Playwright click
            page = self.page
            original = getattr(page, '_original', None)
            has_orig = hasattr(page, '_original')
            if has_orig:
                try:
                    delattr(page, '_original')
                except AttributeError:
                    pass
            try:
                return orig_method(self, *args, **kwargs)
            finally:
                if has_orig:
                    setattr(page, '_original', original)
        else:
            return orig_method(self, *args, **kwargs)
    return wrapped
```

title: Do we need pro for bypassing perimeterx?
body:
I was trying to use CloakBrowser to pass a perimeterx (press and hold) captcha. Although, I tried many adjustments, I couldn't pass the captcha. Then, it came to my mind, that maybe this is a problem of tls handshake and chrome version not just adjusting arguments on launch. 

More info of my setup:

* I have only used Windows machine. 

* I have tried to test it with and without proxies. When using proxies geoip was set to true. I have also tried using VPNs that I usually do when logging in manually. 

* The proxies are not premium enough! They are neither residential nor mobile. However, they do the job if I use a proxy extension and pass the captcha from my chrome. 

* Humanize is typically true.

Arguments in the tests without proxies or with VPN:

'--fingerprint-noise' **(both false and true)**
'--fingerprint-windows-font-metrics'
'--fingerprint-platform=windows'
'--fingerprint-brand=Chrome'
'--fingerprint-brand-version=146'
'--fingerprint-timezone' **(both the true timezone of my machine and the VPN ip address)**
'--fingerprint-locale=en-US',
'--fingerprint-location' **(both the location of real ip and the VPN ip address)**
'--fingerprint-webrtc-ip', **(tried to hardcode it in some sessions)**
'--fingerprint-gpu-vendor=Intel Inc.'
'--fingerprint-gpu-renderer=Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620'

How I do it manually:

* I use a VPN with IKEV2 as selected protocol. When I check my manual setup, I can see webtrc ip leak, different timezone from ip address and geolocation access is blocked. I still manage to pass the verification easily.

The Catch:

* Maybe the latest or at least newer Chrome version is needed for this task and this is not an issue that could be fixed with additional arguments. If so, please inform me on this issue page so I can proceed with the pro version.

title: appreciation post - cloakbrowser just works!
body:
hey team, just wanted to drop a quick appreciation post because this tool genuinely saved me hours of frustration.

i have been fighting with anti-bot detection for hours trying to get a simple scraping flow working. i tried literally everything under the sun.

first i tried camoufox by daijro, spent time setting it up, tweaking configs, adjusting fingerprints. the repo itself warns it is under development and may not be suitable for stable production use. there are hundreds of open issues about google search detecting it every time, cloudflare catching it in docker, gmail registration failing, and twitter blocking due to version blacklisting. the maintainer even stepped down and the latest releases are highly experimental. still got flagged everywhere that mattered.

then i moved to playwright with stealth plugins. i tried playwright-stealth, which literally says on pypi do not expect this to bypass anything but the simplest of bot detection methods. it is basically a proof of concept. i also tried other stealth plugins and they all failed pixelscan and browserscan bot detection tests. playwright even has extra cdp leaks that puppeteer stealth passes, so it fails cloudflare challenges that other tools pass. the most popular playwright extra stealth plugin has not had a meaningful commit since 2023, which is three years of cloudflare updates ago.

puppeteer stealth was next. same story. it is effectively unmaintained for years. it patches navigator.webdriver and window.chrome but it cannot fix the runtime.enable cdp leak, which is the main detection signal now. there are open issues about it failing on cloudflare, imperva, dexscreener, and accounts dot x dot ai.

i was about to give up and write my own custom browser automation stack from scratch. then i found cloakbrowser on github and figured i would give it one last shot.

i ran pip install cloakbrowser and on literally the second try with a proxy everything just worked. no signup needed, no fingerprint tweaks, no endless config rabbit holes, no random blocking on target sites. the pre-patched chromium binary just dropped in and worked seamlessly with my existing playwright code. it was honestly the most seamless experience i have had with any automation tool.

if you are on the fence, just try it. the team has done an amazing job building something that actually works out of the box with real native proxy support and proper patches for canvas, webgl, audio, fonts, webrtc, gpu, and cdp input events.

great work and thank you for building this!

title: --idle-timeout=300
body:
Description:

When using cloakserve with --idle-timeout=300, the idle cleanup sometimes doesn't trigger. The root cause is that proxy_cdp_websocket and WebSocketResponse in bin/cloakserve are created without WebSocket heartbeat/ping, so disconnected clients (e.g. script crash, network drop, process kill) are not detected by cloakserve. The connection refcount stays > 0, preventing disconnect() from being called, which means _schedule_idle_cleanup() is never triggered.

What happened: Chrome processes stay alive indefinitely after client disconnects abnormally, consuming 350MB+ each, eventually causing OOM — the exact problem --idle-timeout was meant to fix (per #346).

What did you expect: cloakserve should detect dead WebSocket connections within a reasonable timeframe and trigger idle cleanup.

CloakBrowser version: 0.4.7

Wrapper: Python (cloakserve / Docker)

Environment: Docker, cloakhq/cloakbrowser:0.4.7, Linux x86-64 (Debian 13 trixie host)

Launch options:

复制
# docker-compose.yml
services:
  cloak-engine:
    image: cloakhq/cloakbrowser:0.4.7
    container_name: server
    command: cloakserve --idle-timeout=300
    ports:
      - "9222:9222"
    restart: unless-stopped
Tested with a different IP or proxy? N/A (not proxy-related)

Works outside Docker / on host machine? Not using outside Docker

Steps to reproduce:

Start cloakserve with --idle-timeout=300
Connect via Playwright connect_over_cdp("http://host:9222")
Open a page, do some work
Kill the Playwright process without calling browser.close() (simulate crash / SIGKILL)
Check GET / — the process shows connections: 1 (or > 0) and idle_cleanup_pending: false
Wait 5+ minutes — idle cleanup never triggers because refcount never reaches 0
Chrome process stays alive indefinitely, consuming ~350MB+
Error output / screenshots:

Root cause in bin/cloakserve:

复制
# Line ~650: cloakserve → Chrome connection (no ping)
async with websockets.connect(
    target_url, max_size=None, ping_interval=None, ping_timeout=None,
) as cdp_ws:

# Line ~700, ~724: Playwright → cloakserve connection (no heartbeat)
ws = web.WebSocketResponse()
Both WebSocket connections have no heartbeat/ping mechanism. When a client disconnects abnormally (crash, SIGKILL, network drop), the server has no way to detect the dead connection until the OS TCP timeout (~15 min on Linux). During this time, pool.disconnect() is never called, refcount stays > 0, and _schedule_idle_cleanup() never runs.

Suggested fix:

复制
# cloakserve → Chrome: add ping
async with websockets.connect(
    target_url, max_size=None, ping_interval=30, ping_timeout=10,
) as cdp_ws:

# Playwright → cloakserve: add aiohttp heartbeat
ws = web.WebSocketResponse(heartbeat=30)
This would detect dead connections within ~40 seconds instead of waiting for TCP timeout, allowing --idle-timeout to work reliably in all scenarios.

Additional notes:

This is the same class of problem as #346 (OOM from non-cleanup), but from a different angle — #346 was about missing cleanup mechanism, this is about the cleanup mechanism not triggering when clients disconnect abnormally.
With heartbeat=30 on WebSocketResponse, aiohttp will send WebSocket pings every 30s and close the connection if no pong is received within 30s, triggering the finally block → pool.disconnect() → idle cleanup countdown.
The ping_interval=30, ping_timeout=10 on the cloakserve→Chrome connection also helps detect Chrome process hangs.
Tested the patch locally (via Docker volume mount) — connections are correctly cleaned up within ~40 seconds after client crash, and idle cleanup triggers as expected.

title: VK ID iframe auth flow restarts indefinitely on mail.ru — postMessage/iframe communication appears broken, persiq.vk.com polling never sustains
body:
**## Summary**
When logging into mail.ru (which uses VK ID as its auth provider), the `id.vk.ru/auth` iframe loads successfully (all network requests return 200), but the authentication flow never completes. Instead, it restarts in a loop with a new `code_challenge` every ~10-15 seconds, and the login form on mail.ru hangs indefinitely with a loading spinner. This does not happen with stock Playwright using the same Chromium version/profile approach.

**## Environment**
- CloakBrowser version: 0.4.5 (also reproduced on 0.4.3 before upgrading)
- OS: Windows 10/11 x64
- Chromium version: 146.0.7680.177 (visible in UA string in logs)
- Python wrapper (`launch_persistent_context_async`)
- Target site: https://mail.ru (login flow via VK ID / `auth.mail.ru/api/v1/vkid_auth/start`)

**## Steps to Reproduce**
1. Launch a persistent context with CloakBrowser:
```python
ctx = await launch_persistent_context_async(
    user_data_dir="profiles/test_profile",
    headless=False,
    no_viewport=True,
    humanize=True,
    ignore_https_errors=True,
    args=["--window-size=1600,900"],
)
page = await ctx.new_page()
await page.goto("https://mail.ru", wait_until="networkidle", timeout=60000)
```
2. Click "Войти" (Login) on the mail.ru homepage.
3. Observe the modal opens with an infinite loading spinner and never resolves.

**## Expected Behavior**
The VK ID auth iframe should complete its handshake with the parent window (mail.ru) and either show the login form or restore an existing session, exactly as it does in stock Playwright.

## Actual Behavior
The iframe (`id.vk.ru/auth?...`) reloads repeatedly with a freshly generated `code_challenge` parameter each time, roughly every 10-15 seconds, and the loading spinner on the parent page never disappears.

## Comparison: Playwright vs CloakBrowser (same machine, same network conditions)

**Stock Playwright** — auth flow completes, VK ID polling sustains:

[PW][302] https://account.mail.ru/login/
[PW][302] https://auth.mail.ru/api/v1/vkid_auth/start
[PW][200] https://id.vk.ru/auth
[PW][200] https://static.vk.ru/vkid/1.1.1368/auth.js
[PW][200] https://persiq.vk.com/vkid/getEvents/auth_common_9068800865393890659
[PW][200] https://persiq.vk.com/vkid/getEvents/auth_common_9068800865393890659

`persiq.vk.com/vkid/getEvents` is called repeatedly — this is the polling endpoint that confirms the iframe is alive and the parent is listening. The login form renders correctly.

**CloakBrowser** — auth flow restarts in a loop:

[CB][302] https://account.mail.ru/login/
[CB][302] https://auth.mail.ru/api/v1/vkid_auth/start
[CB][200] https://id.vk.ru/auth
[frame_navigated] https://id.vk.ru/auth?...code_challenge=WQbYedjQePdyzGPa0ILo2bM18NbnDLaoQV6Hdk8UyJg...
[CB][200] https://static.vk.ru/vkid/1.1.1368/auth.js
[CB][200] https://persiq.vk.com/vkid/getEvents/auth_common_9000000001165586455   <- appears ONCE
[CB][302] https://account.mail.ru/login/        <- restarts
[CB][302] https://auth.mail.ru/api/v1/vkid_auth/start
[CB][200] https://id.vk.ru/auth
[frame_navigated] https://id.vk.ru/auth?...code_challenge=KwJuABsyd77KIzdeLrvjXENCVO2a9oYOMLkDryVsALc...   <- DIFFERENT code_challenge, full restart
[CB][302] https://account.mail.ru/login/        <- restarts again
[CB][302] https://auth.mail.ru/api/v1/vkid_auth/start
[CB][200] https://id.vk.ru/auth
[frame_navigated] https://id.vk.ru/auth?...code_challenge=9RXHF1hNlPaobbi_Tr8JnZbWGelcCqsa5iRnS5InN-Y...   <- restarts a third time

`persiq.vk.com/vkid/getEvents` fires exactly once across the whole session and is never called again, even though the iframe keeps reloading with new challenge parameters. This pattern (one-shot getEvents call followed by full iframe restart) strongly suggests the iframe never receives a confirmation `postMessage` from the parent window — so VK ID's internal logic assumes the parent isn't listening and tears down/restarts the flow.

## What I've already ruled out
I went through the following diagnostic steps before concluding this is likely an iframe/postMessage issue rather than a network/proxy/CORS issue:

1. **ORB (Opaque Response Blocking)** — initially `media-trend.mail.ru/challenge.html` was failing with `net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB`. Adding `--disable-features=OpaqueResponseBlockingV01,OpaqueResponseBlocking` resolved this specific failure (challenge.html now returns 200), but the core spinner issue persisted.
2. **HTTP/2** — `pms.mail.ru` (push/realtime server) was failing with `net::ERR_HTTP2_SERVER_REFUSED_STREAM` on an early test. Adding `--disable-http2` resolved this, but again, the spinner issue persisted.
3. **CORS** — added `--disable-web-security` to rule out cross-origin fetch blocking on `media-trend.mail.ru/api/...`. No change to the core issue.
4. **Proxy/SSL** — not in use for this specific test; reproduced with no proxy configured at all.
5. **Network-level comparison** — ran a side-by-side test with stock Playwright (`playwright.chromium.launch_persistent_context`) and CloakBrowser against the same site in the same session. Network responses are nearly identical (same 200s, same redirect chains) — the only meaningful divergence is the absence of sustained `persiq.vk.com/vkid/getEvents` polling and the repeated `code_challenge` regeneration in CloakBrowser.
6. **postMessage listener** — injected a `window.addEventListener('message', ...)` into every frame via `frameattached`/`framenavigated` events to log any cross-frame messages. No `[postMessage]` log lines were ever captured during the CloakBrowser run, despite the iframe being confirmed present and active (`frame_navigated` events fire correctly for `id.vk.ru/auth`).
7. **stealth_args=False** — disabled all default stealth arguments to isolate whether the issue originates in the wrapper's flag composition or the binary itself. The loop behavior was identical: `persiq.vk.com/vkid/getEvents` fired once, followed by the same `code_challenge` regeneration pattern. This points to the binary-level patches as the likely source rather than anything controlled by launch-time flags.

## Suspected Root Cause
Given that:
- The iframe is created and loaded successfully (network-wise)
- VK ID's polling endpoint (`persiq.vk.com/vkid/getEvents`) is hit exactly once instead of continuously
- No `postMessage` events are observed between the iframe and parent frame
- The flow keeps regenerating `code_challenge` and restarting, consistent with VK ID's client-side logic timing out while waiting for a parent acknowledgment
- The behavior is identical with `stealth_args=False`, ruling out wrapper-level flags as the cause

...this looks like it could be related to one of CloakBrowser's source-level (C++) patches affecting cross-frame communication (`postMessage`, `window.parent` access, or iframe sandboxing behavior) — possibly connected to the sandbox-related warnings also seen in the console during this flow:

_An iframe which has both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin for its sandbox attribute can escape its sandboxing._

This warning appears repeatedly throughout the session on various ad/tracking iframes as well, suggesting the patched binary may be handling sandboxed iframe behavior differently than stock Chromium in a way that could plausibly interfere with legitimate cross-frame messaging used by VK ID's auth widget.

## Questions for maintainers
1. Are there any known patches affecting `postMessage`, `window.parent`/`window.opener` access, or iframe sandbox attribute handling?
2. Is there a way to verify/inspect whether `postMessage` calls are being silently dropped or intercepted by the stealth layer?
3. I tested with `stealth_args=False` to rule out the JS/flag-level stealth layer as the cause — the issue persisted identically (same one-shot `getEvents` call followed by `code_challenge` regeneration loop). This suggests the relevant behavior is baked into the patched binary itself rather than controlled by wrapper-level flags. Can you confirm whether any of the 49/57 source-level patches touch cross-frame messaging or sandboxed iframe behavior?

title: CloakBrowser Pro 148.0.7778.215.3 crashes with SIGSEGV on Linux Docker
body:
```md
Description:

I am using CloakBrowser Pro Chromium `148.0.7778.215.3` and it crashes immediately on my Linux Docker runtime.

The crash happens when calling `launchPersistentContext()`. It also happens with a minimal `about:blank` test and no proxy, so this does not appear to be proxy-related.

Expected:
`launchPersistentContext()` should start Chromium and create the persistent context successfully.

Actual:
Chromium launches, then immediately exits with `SIGSEGV`.

CloakBrowser version:
- npm wrapper: `cloakbrowser@0.4.4`
- Pro binary: `148.0.7778.215.3`

Wrapper:
JavaScript / Node.js

Environment:
- Linux VPS
- Docker: yes
- Node: v22.23.1 inside container
- Platform: linux-x64
- DISPLAY: Xvfb on `:99`
- Windows fonts mounted at `/usr/share/fonts/windows`
- Widevine mounted, but not required to reproduce

Launch options:

```js
import { launchPersistentContext, binaryInfo } from "cloakbrowser";

console.log(await binaryInfo());

const ctx = await launchPersistentContext({
  userDataDir: `/tmp/cb-smoke-${Date.now()}`,
  headless: false,
  geoip: false,
  args: [
    "--fingerprint=12345",
    "--fingerprint-noise=false",
  ],
});

const page = ctx.pages()[0] || await ctx.newPage();
await page.goto("about:blank");
console.log("launch-ok");
await ctx.close();
```

Tested with a different IP or proxy?
Yes. It fails with no proxy at all.

Works outside Docker / on host machine?
Not tested outside Docker.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Install wrapper:
   ```bash
   npm install cloakbrowser@0.4.4
   ```

2. Use Pro binary `148.0.7778.215.3`:
   ```env
   CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=148.0.7778.215.3
   ```

3. Run the minimal script above inside Docker.

4. Chromium crashes immediately.

Error output:

```text
binaryInfo {
  version: '148.0.7778.215.3',
  bundledVersion: '146.0.7680.177.5',
  tier: 'pro',
  platform: 'linux-x64',
  binaryPath: '/root/.cloakbrowser/chromium-148.0.7778.215.3-pro/chrome',
  installed: true,
  cacheDir: '/root/.cloakbrowser/chromium-148.0.7778.215.3-pro'
}

browserType.launchPersistentContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed
Browser logs:

<launching> /root/.cloakbrowser/chromium-148.0.7778.215.3-pro/chrome ...
<launched> pid=56

Call log:
  - <launched> pid=56
  - [pid=56] <gracefully close start>
  - [pid=56] <kill>
  - [pid=56] <will force kill>
  - [pid=56] exception while trying to kill process: Error: kill ESRCH
  - [pid=56] <process did exit: exitCode=null, signal=SIGSEGV>
  - [pid=56] starting temporary directories cleanup
  - [pid=56] finished temporary directories cleanup
```

Additional notes:

I tested rollback with the new wrapper version pinning:

```env
CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=148.0.7778.215.2
```

The exact same script works with `148.0.7778.215.2`:

```text
rollback-launch-ok
```

So the regression appears specific to the Linux x64 Pro binary `148.0.7778.215.3`.
```

title: fix: resolve timezoneId in standalone builders so --fingerprint-timezone is not dropped
body:
Follow-up to #265 (closed in favor of #262). You flagged that standalone callers passing `timezoneId` instead of `timezone` miss `--fingerprint-timezone`. The code has since been refactored, so I traced the gap to where it actually lives now:

- `buildLaunchOptions()` (Playwright) is exported and used standalone but didn't call `resolveTimezone`, so `buildLaunchOptions({ timezoneId })` silently dropped the flag.
- The puppeteer adapter's `resolveArgs()` — shared by `launch`/`launchContext`/`launchPersistentContext` — never resolved `timezoneId` at all, so the entire puppeteer surface dropped it (broader than the Playwright side, where the launch wrappers already resolve it).

`resolveTimezone()` added at the top of both. Tests cover `timezoneId` on the Playwright standalone builder and the puppeteer launch path. Full suite green locally (422 passed).

title: [Bug]: 100% CAPTCHA/Bot Detection Rate on Google SERP despite Mobile Proxies (Free Version)
body:
Hello team,

We are currently running a high-concurrency SERP telemetry worker pool (our Harvester module built on Golang) connected to CloakBrowser via Playwright. Over the last few days, we have experienced a complete halt in our scraping pipeline. Every single Google SERP iteration is immediately flagged by bot detection (CAPTCHA), making it impossible to complete any workflow.

title: Sudden CAPTCHA spike on Google SERP with default settings (free macOS binary, Chromium 145) — regression or IP-reputation / Google-side?
body:
### Summary

Using CloakBrowser with **default settings** to fetch Google SERP results, my CAPTCHA
("sorry"/unusual-traffic interstitial) rate jumped from a historical **~2–5%** to:

- **Residential proxies: >70%** CAPTCHA on fresh sessions
- **Mobile proxies: ~40%** CAPTCHA on fresh sessions

I changed **nothing** on my side — same code, same proxy providers, same launch
options. A few days ago the exact same setup ran essentially flawlessly; now a brand-new
session gets walled almost immediately. I'd appreciate guidance on whether this is a
CloakBrowser-side regression (i.e. should I buy/switch to the Pro binary), or a
Google/proxy-reputation–side change.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| OS | macOS 26.1 (build 25B78), **Apple Silicon / arm64** |
| CloakBrowser wrapper | **0.4.3** (pip) |
| Bundled Chromium (free, `darwin-arm64`) | **145.0.7632.109.2** (from `config.py` `CHROMIUM_VERSIONS`) |
| License | Free (no `license_key` / `CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY` set) → running the free v145 macOS binary |
| Playwright | 1.58.0 |
| Launch config | Defaults (headless, no custom fingerprint flags beyond defaults) |
| Use case | Google SERP scraping (`google.com/search`), one fresh context per request |
| Proxies | Reputable residential + mobile pools (rotating) |

I note from the package METADATA that the green test results are *"Last tested: Jun 2026
(Chromium 148)"* against the **Pro** binary, and that the free binary *"goes stale within
weeks as detection evolves."* My macOS free binary is **Chromium 145**, so I want to
understand whether I'm simply on a binary that detection has caught up with.

### What changed / timeline

- Onset: ~2 days ago, abrupt (not a gradual drift).
- No CloakBrowser upgrade, no code change, no proxy provider change on my side coincided
  with the onset.

### Isolation tests I ran (to separate CloakBrowser vs Google/proxy)

To avoid the "something changed on your side" dead end, I tried to isolate the layer:

1. **Same binary, only Playwright driver version changed (A/B):**
   - Playwright **1.60.0** (Chromium 148 driver): SERP → CAPTCHA
   - Playwright **1.58.0** (Chromium 145/146 driver): SERP → clean
   - Same proxy, same machine, same target. Pinning to 1.58.0 measurably helped, which
     suggests at least part of the signal is **browser/driver-fingerprint** related, not
     purely IP reputation.

2. **Browserless control (plain HTTP through the same proxy pool):**
   - Issuing a plain HTTP GET to Google through the *same* residential IP pool (no browser,
     no CloakBrowser) returned a block/"sorry" response on roughly **27–40%** of TR exit
     IPs at the very first request.
   - This indicates a real **IP-reputation / Google-side** component as well.

**Interpretation I can't resolve on my own:** the browser CAPTCHA rate (>70%) is far higher
than the browserless block rate (27–40%) on the same IPs, which implies an *additional*
browser-detectable signal on top of IP reputation — i.e. the fresh-session browser
fingerprint is now being flagged where it wasn't a few days ago.

### Questions

1. Is the free **macOS Chromium 145** binary now known to be detected on Google
   specifically (a stale-binary regression), and is **Pro (Chromium 148)** expected to
   restore the previous low CAPTCHA rate for Google SERP?
2. Are there recommended default-deviating settings for Google SERP at scale (persistent
   profile / `launch_persistent_context`, `geoip`, timezone/locale alignment to the proxy
   exit, etc.) that the free binary needs but Pro handles automatically?
3. Is there anything in the recent Google detection wave (May–Jun 2026) that you've already
   characterized and patched in 148 but not in 145/146?

I'm happy to run any controlled A/B you suggest (e.g. specific flags, a Pro trial key, or a
nodriver/stock-Chromium comparison on the identical IP pool) and report exact numbers.
Thanks for the great tool.
