# ========================================================
# Stage 1: Build
# ========================================================
FROM cloakhq/cloakbrowser AS build
WORKDIR /app

# Install build tools
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    g++ make python3 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY ./backend-worker/package*.json ./
COPY ./backend-worker/package-lock.json ./
COPY ./backend-worker/tsconfig.json ./
COPY ./backend-lib/sitefontcheck-backend-lib-1.0.0.tgz ./ 
COPY ./backend-lib/package ./package
COPY ./backend-worker .

RUN npm install
RUN npm run build


# ========================================================
# Stage 2: Runtime
# ========================================================
FROM cloakhq/cloakbrowser

# 1. Create a non-root user 'node' and give them audio/video groups for Chromium
RUN groupadd -r node && useradd -r -g node -G audio,video node \
    && mkdir -p /home/node/.cloakbrowser/logs \
    && chown -R node:node /home/node \
    # The cloakhq/cloakbrowser base image pre-bakes Chromium at /root/.cloakbrowser/
    # but /root/ is 700 by default, blocking the node user from traversing it.
    # Making it o+x allows the node user to access the pre-baked Chromium binary
    # without needing to re-download it.
    && chmod o+x /root

RUN cd /root/.cloakbrowser/chromium-*/ && \
    mv chrome_crashpad_handler chrome_crashpad_handler.bak && \
    echo '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0' > chrome_crashpad_handler && \
    chmod +x chrome_crashpad_handler

WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV CLOAKBROWSER_AUTO_UPDATE=false
# 2. Point to the pre-baked Chromium binary at /root/.cloakbrowser
#    The cloakhq/cloakbrowser base image ships Chromium at /root/.cloakbrowser/
#    instead of re-downloading on every container start.
#    Write attempts (update markers) fail silently — fine since AUTO_UPDATE=false.
ENV CLOAKBROWSER_CACHE_DIR=/root/.cloakbrowser

# 3. Copy files and explicitly grant ownership to the non-root user
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/node_modules/sitefontcheck-backend-lib/package/ /app/package/

EXPOSE 3002

# 4. Create the symlink to stdout inside the non-root user's directory
RUN ln -sf /dev/stdout /home/node/.cloakbrowser/logs/server.log

# 5: Create the X11 directory with sticky bit permissions while still root
RUN mkdir -p /tmp/.X11-unix && chmod 1777 /tmp/.X11-unix

HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=5s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -f http://localhost:3002/health || exit 1

# 6. Drop root privileges right before execution
USER node

CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]
```

I assume this is some permissions issue, but I'm not sure what exactly it is. I was looking through the docs to see if anyone has run into this. Can run on AWS fine with playwright.  Not sure if headless on or off matters. I'd like headless off, but tried a bunch of settings/args and nothing's seemed to work. I tried it with the playwright image originally and get the same errors.

title: Chromium always navigates to http://[keyword] instead of searching when typing in the omnibox
body: Description: Chromium always navigates to http://[keyword] instead of searching when typing in the omnibox CloakBrowser has no default search engine configured. When a user types any text into the address bar (omnibox) and presses Enter, Chrome treats the input as a URL and navigates to http://[typed text], resulting in a DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN error instead of performing a web search. CloakBrowser version: 146.0.7680.177.5 Wrapper: JavaScript (Node.js — launchPersistentContext via playwright-core) Environment: Windows 11, localhost test, fresh profile (new userDataDir) Launch options: ```javascript launchPersistentContext({ userDataDir: './profiles/test', headless: false, stealthArgs: false, args: [ '--fingerprint=', '--no-first-run', '--no-default-browser-check', ], }) ``` Tested with a different IP or proxy? No Works outside Docker / on host machine? Yes (running on host machine directly) Steps to reproduce: 1. Launch a CloakBrowser instance using launchPersistentContext with a fresh userDataDir 2. Wait for browser window to open 3. Click on the address bar (omnibox) 4. Type any search keyword (e.g. hello, fggg, or any word without dots) 5. Press Enter Expected: Browser navigates to https://www.google.com/search?q=hello (or uses configured default search engine) Actual: Browser navigates to http://hello → DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN Error output / screenshots: Root cause analysis: Standard Chromium ships with Google (and others) as built-in prepopulated search engines. CloakBrowser appears to have removed these built-in engines (likely to avoid search-engine fingerprinting). As a result, a fresh profile has no default search engine, so Chrome's omnibox navigation falls back to treating all input as a bare hostname. Attempts to work around via Default/Preferences (default_search_provider_data.template_url_data) were ignored by Chrome, likely due to MAC checksum validation on the Preferences file. Current workaround (via playwright-core): ```javascript // ctx.route() does NOT intercept omnibox navigations (Chrome UI level) // Must use framenavigated to catch and redirect after URL commits ctx.on('page', (page) => { page.on('framenavigated', async (frame) => { if (frame !== page.mainFrame()) return const url = frame.url() if (!url.startsWith('http://')) return try { const host = new URL(url).hostname if (!host.includes('.') && host !== 'localhost') { await page.goto(`https://www.google.com/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(host)}`) .catch(() => {}) } } catch {} }) }) ``` Feature request / fix suggestion: Please either: Re-include Google (or a neutral default) as a built-in prepopulated search engine in the omnibox, OR Provide a launch option/API to specify the default search engine URL template (e.g. defaultSearchUrl: 'https://www.google.com/search?q={searchTerms}') Dockerfile (if applicable): No Additional notes: The workaround above works but introduces a brief flash of the DNS error page before the redirect fires. A native fix at the browser level would provide a seamless experience.

title: reCAPTCHA v3 reslove problem
body:
Description:
CloakBrowser advertises a "0.9 human score" for reCAPTCHA v3. I can reproduce that 0.9 on a
score-detector page (antcpt), but on a **real production site** protected by reCAPTCHA v3
(`https://www.olejsilnikowyvw.pl/`) the generated token is **rejected** by the site's server-side
verification as too low ("reCAPTCHA verification failed").

A valid token is generated (length ~2233), and bot signals look clean (`navigator.webdriver=false`,
real GPU, proper UA), yet the production site-key consistently rejects it. The same launch options
score 0.9 on `https://antcpt.com/score_detector/`. I tried headless and headed, `humanize=True`
with `human_preset="careful"`, a persistent profile, and even a profile logged into a Google account
— always rejected on the production site.

Expected: the advertised ~0.9 score should translate to passing real-world reCAPTCHA v3 site-keys
(score above common thresholds). Actual: passes only on the lenient score-detector key, not on a real
production key.

CloakBrowser version: 0.4.2 (stealth Chromium 146.0.7680.177.5, windows-x64)

Wrapper: Python (sync API)

Environment: Windows 11 Pro (build 10.0.26200), x86_64, Python 3.13.2, no Docker (running on host)

Launch options:

python
from cloakbrowser import launch_persistent_context

ctx = launch_persistent_context(
    "profile",
    headless=True,              # also reproduced with headless=False
    humanize=True,
    human_preset="careful",
    locale="pl-PL",
    timezone="Europe/Warsaw",
    viewport={"width": 1366, "height": 768},
)
page = ctx.pages[0]


Tested with a different IP or proxy? No (not tested with a different IP/proxy). Note: the same
residential IP scores 0.9 on antcpt, so the IP itself is not globally flagged.

Works outside Docker / on host machine? Not using Docker (this is the host machine).

Steps to reproduce:

1. `pip install cloakbrowser==0.4.2` and `python -m cloakbrowser fetch` (Chromium 146).
2. Launch with the options above.
3. `page.goto("https://www.olejsilnikowyvw.pl/")` and accept the cookie consent (button `#c-p-bn` / `#s-all-bn`).
4. Stay on the page ~15 s (native `time.sleep`, a little scrolling).
5. Fill the VIN field `#vinInput` with a valid 17-char VW/Audi VIN and click submit `#button-addon2`.
   The site's own JS calls `grecaptcha.execute(siteKey, {action: 'search'})` (site-key
   `6LdeigMsAAAAAHqpnNRwpnhSi-FdktfsaWkg1rKT`) and POSTs the token to `/wyszukiwarka`.
6. Inspect the `/wyszukiwarka` JSON response.
7. For comparison, load `https://antcpt.com/score_detector/` with the identical launch options and read
   the reported score.

Error output / screenshots:

Production site `/wyszukiwarka` response (HTTP 200):

json
{"norm":null,"status":false,"errors":{"vin":"reCAPTCHA verification failed. Please try again."}}


- `#recaptchaToken` value length: ~2233 (token is generated).
- `https://antcpt.com/score_detector/` with the same launch options: score = 0.9.
- Bot signals (headless): `navigator.webdriver = false`; UA
  `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/146.0.0.0 Safari/537.36`;

title: SOCKS5 proxy stalls in CloakBrowser 0.4.0 while the same proxy works perfectly in stock Chrome with Chromium proxy flags
body:
## Summary

I am seeing a reproducible SOCKS5 proxy/network failure in CloakBrowser on Windows. The same SOCKS5 endpoint works perfectly in stock Chrome launched manually with Chromium proxy flags, and it also passes a raw SOCKS5/TLS stress test. However, in CloakBrowser, the first website only loads partially, and after that the browser network becomes unusable: any subsequent page hangs indefinitely until the browser is restarted.

This still happens after upgrading from `cloakbrowser 0.3.31` to `cloakbrowser 0.4.0`.

The issue is important because CloakBrowser 0.4.0 advertises native SOCKS5 proxy support, but in this environment the native SOCKS5 path appears to stall under normal interactive browsing.

## Environment

* OS: Windows
* Python: running from a venv at `O:/programas/venv/Scripts/python.exe`
* CloakBrowser versions tested:

  * `0.3.31`
  * `0.4.0`
* Proxy type: local SOCKS5 endpoint
* Proxy URL: `socks5://127.0.0.1:10010`
* Proxy authentication: none
* Browser mode: headed
* Main API tested: `launch_persistent_context()`
* Persistent profile path: fresh profile directory for every test
* Example sites where the failure is visible:

  * `https://www.youtube.com/`
  * `https://www.facebook.com/`
  * `https://www.google.com/`
  * `https://www.whatismyip.com/`

## Actual behavior

When launching CloakBrowser with the SOCKS5 proxy:

1. Browser opens normally.
2. The first website starts loading but only partially completes.
3. Shortly after that, network activity appears to stall.
4. Any new page or navigation hangs indefinitely.
5. Restarting the browser is required to get any network activity again.
6. The same behavior occurs with both CloakBrowser `0.3.31` and `0.4.0`.

## Expected behavior

CloakBrowser should handle the SOCKS5 proxy like stock Chrome does:

* The proxy should remain usable across multiple navigations.
* The first page should fully load.
* Subsequent pages should continue to load normally.
* The network should not stall after the first partially loaded page.

## Minimal reproduction tested with CloakBrowser 0.4.0

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.metadata
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

PROFILE_DIR = Path("M:/navegadores/cloakbrowser/cloak_040_socks5_final_test")
DOWNLOADS_DIR = Path("M:/dados/downloads/cloak_040_socks5_final_test")

PROXY = "socks5://127.0.0.1:10010"
FRESH_PROFILE = True

def main() -> int:
    from cloakbrowser import launch_persistent_context

    try:
        version = importlib.metadata.version("cloakbrowser")
    except Exception:
        version = "unknown"

    print(f"cloakbrowser version={version}", flush=True)
    print(f"profile={PROFILE_DIR}", flush=True)
    print(f"proxy={PROXY}", flush=True)

    if FRESH_PROFILE:
        shutil.rmtree(PROFILE_DIR, ignore_errors=True)

    PROFILE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    DOWNLOADS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    context = launch_persistent_context(
        str(PROFILE_DIR),
        headless=False,
        proxy=PROXY,
        accept_downloads=True,
        downloads_path=str(DOWNLOADS_DIR),
        viewport={
            "width": 1366,
            "height": 768,
        },
        locale="pt-BR",
        timezone="America/Sao_Paulo",
        humanize=False,
        geoip=False,
    )

    try:
        pages = list(context.pages)
        page = pages[0] if pages else context.new_page()

        try:
            page.goto("about:blank", wait_until="commit", timeout=30000)
        except Exception:
            pass

        try:
            page.bring_to_front()
        except Exception:
            pass

        print("CloakBrowser 0.4.0 opened with native SOCKS5 proxy.")
        print("Manual test: open whatismyip.com, YouTube, Facebook, Google.")

        while True:
            time.sleep(1)

    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 0

    finally:
        try:
            context.close()
        except Exception:
            pass

    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

## Control test 1: raw SOCKS5/TLS probe succeeds

I tested the same SOCKS5 endpoint outside any browser with a raw Python SOCKS5 client. It repeatedly opened TCP/TLS connections through the proxy to multiple HTTPS targets.

Result:

```text
proxy=socks5://127.0.0.1:10010
OK round=1 host=example.com status=200 bytes=868 elapsed_ms=1928
OK round=1 host=www.google.com status=204 bytes=203 elapsed_ms=1858
OK round=1 host=www.youtube.com status=200 bytes=377505 elapsed_ms=3238
OK round=1 host=www.facebook.com status=200 bytes=383482 elapsed_ms=3258
...
OK round=20 host=example.com status=200 bytes=868 elapsed_ms=1857
OK round=20 host=www.google.com status=204 bytes=203 elapsed_ms=1938
OK round=20 host=www.youtube.com status=200 bytes=524703 elapsed_ms=3418
OK round=20 host=www.facebook.com status=200 bytes=382352 elapsed_ms=3339
summary ok=80 fail=0
```

This suggests that the local SOCKS5 endpoint itself is stable and does not die after the first connection.

## Control test 2: stock Chrome with Chromium proxy flags works perfectly

The same proxy works correctly in stock Chrome when launched manually with Chromium proxy flags:

```powershell
$ProxyServer = "socks5://127.0.0.1:10010"
$UserDataDir = "M:/navegadores/cloakbrowser/chrome_socks5_manual"

& "C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe" `
    --user-data-dir="$UserDataDir" `
    --no-first-run `
    --no-default-browser-check `
    --proxy-server="$ProxyServer" `
    --host-resolver-rules="MAP * ~NOTFOUND , EXCLUDE 127.0.0.1" `
    --disable-quic `
    --disable-ipv6 `
    --disable-features="AsyncDns,DnsOverHttps,UseDnsHttpsSvcbAlpn,HappyEyeballsV3" `
    --dns-prefetch-disable `
    --disable-domain-reliability `
    --disable-component-update `
    --disable-client-side-phishing-detection `
    --disable-sync `
    --disable-default-apps `
    about:blank
```

Result:

* `whatismyip.com` confirms the proxy IP is used.
* YouTube loads normally.
* Facebook loads normally.
* Google loads normally.
* No connection stalls.
* No partial first-page load.
* No need to restart the browser.

## Additional isolation tests

I also tested several paths to isolate where the failure begins.

### Works

1. Raw SOCKS5/TLS client:

   * 80 successful HTTPS requests through the same SOCKS5 proxy.
   * No failures.

2. Stock Chrome launched manually with:

   * `--proxy-server=socks5://127.0.0.1:10010`
   * `--host-resolver-rules=MAP * ~NOTFOUND , EXCLUDE 127.0.0.1`
   * Result: stable browsing, no failures.

3. Stock Chrome launched through Python `subprocess.Popen()` with the same flags and no Playwright/CDP attach:

   * Result: stable browsing, no failures.

4. Stock Chrome launched with `--remote-debugging-port`, but without Playwright attaching:

   * Result: stable browsing, no failures.

### Fails

1. CloakBrowser `0.3.31` using `launch_persistent_context()` with SOCKS5 proxy:

   * First page partially loads.
   * Then network stalls.

2. CloakBrowser `0.4.0` using `launch_persistent_context()` with native SOCKS5 proxy string:

   * Same failure.

3. Playwright controlling Chrome via `channel="chrome"` with the same proxy flags:

   * Same failure symptom.

4. Chrome launched with remote debugging, then Playwright attaches using `connect_over_cdp()`:

   * Same failure symptom, even when attempting to avoid defaults.

## Things already tried

* Fresh user data directory for each test.
* `proxy="socks5://127.0.0.1:10010"` as a string.
* Proxy dictionary form in earlier tests.
* No local proxy bridge.
* No bootstrap URLs.
* No navigation guard.
* No extensions.
* No automated browsing loop.
* No `page.goto()` to a real website before manual testing; browser starts on `about:blank`.
* `humanize=False`.
* `geoip=False`.
* Disabling QUIC.
* Disabling IPv6.
* Disabling async DNS / DNS-over-HTTPS related features.
* Using Chromium’s `--host-resolver-rules`.
* Testing stock Chrome manually as a control.

## Why this looks like a CloakBrowser / controlled-browser network issue

The SOCKS5 proxy itself is stable. Stock Chrome with the same proxy is stable. The failure appears only when the browser is controlled through CloakBrowser/Playwright/CDP-like paths, or when using CloakBrowser’s own stealth Chromium.

The most useful comparison is:

* Stock Chrome + `--proxy-server=socks5://127.0.0.1:10010` + `--host-resolver-rules=...` = works perfectly.
* CloakBrowser 0.4.0 + `proxy="socks5://127.0.0.1:10010"` = first page partially loads, then all networking stalls.

## Request

Could you please investigate whether CloakBrowser’s SOCKS5 proxy handling, network-layer patches, Playwright/CDP integration, or stealth Chromium build changes something that can cause SOCKS5 connections to stall after the first partially loaded page?

It would also help to know:

1. Is `proxy="socks5://127.0.0.1:10010"` the intended correct way to use an unauthenticated local SOCKS5 proxy in `launch_persistent_context()`?
2. Does CloakBrowser 0.4.0 internally add Chromium proxy flags, use its own proxy stack, or use network-layer patches for SOCKS5?
3. Is there a way to force CloakBrowser to use the exact Chromium behavior equivalent to:

   * `--proxy-server=socks5://127.0.0.1:10010`
   * `--host-resolver-rules=MAP * ~NOTFOUND , EXCLUDE 127.0.0.1`
4. Are there known conflicts between native SOCKS5 proxy support and the stealth/network timing/proxy signal removal patches?
5. Is there any debug logging or netlog mode you recommend to capture the failure?

I can provide logs or run additional debug builds/tests if needed.

title: Add first-party .NET 8 / C# client
body:
## First-party .NET 8 / C# client

As discussed in the issue, this adds the .NET client in-repo under `dotnet/`, following the conventions you laid out. It's a complete, faithful port of the CloakBrowser wrapper built on `Microsoft.Playwright`, mirroring the Python and JS clients module-for-module.

### Conventions followed

- **Layout:** `dotnet/` at the repo root, alongside `cloakbrowser/` (Python) and `js/`. Self-contained — its own `CloakBrowser.sln`, `src/` (library + CLI + Roslyn generator), `tests/`, `examples/`. Nothing outside `dotnet/` is touched.
- **Namespacing:** top-level `CloakBrowser` namespace mirroring the Python/JS public surface.
- **Versioning:** tracks the wrapper version — this is `0.4.0`, matching upstream. (Happy to let you drive version sync across the three wrappers.)
- **CI / publishing / main README:** untouched — those are yours. The only readme here is `dotnet/README.md`, which feeds the NuGet package page; structure and content are a proposal, polish away.

### What's ported

- **Binary lifecycle:** download / cache / auto-update with the pinned Ed25519 signature verification (`SHA256SUMS.sig`, anti-downgrade), archive extraction with a zip-slip guard.
- **Launch:** stealth args, proxy (HTTP/HTTPS + SOCKS5 with inline credentials), GeoIP timezone/locale from the proxy exit IP (MaxMind GeoLite2), WebRTC IP spoofing, Widevine seeding, persistent contexts, and real window geometry on headed launches (no fixed emulated viewport over the real window) applied on every page/context path.
- **CloakBrowser Pro (`license_key`):** a `LicenseKey` launch option resolved from param → `CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY` → `~/.cloakbrowser/license.key`, with 24h cached validation, the Pro binary gated by the same pinned signature as the free binary, and a clear error rather than a silent downgrade when a valid key's Pro download/signature check fails. Mirrors `validate_license` / `LicenseInfo` / `tier`.
- **Transparent `Humanize = true`:** Bézier mouse motion, human typing, scrolling, and actionability checks — standard Playwright call sites are humanized with no code changes, exactly like the Python/JS `humanize=True` flag.
- **CLI:** `install` / `info` / `update` / `clear-cache`.

### Note on the source generator (per your request)

.NET's Playwright exposes its surface as **sealed interfaces** implemented by internal sealed classes, so the runtime monkey-patching the Python/JS clients use to make humanize transparent isn't available. The .NET client uses a **decorator** instead: each Playwright object is wrapped in a class that implements the same interface, intercepts only the handful of interaction methods, and forwards everything else verbatim.

Hand-writing the "forward to `_inner`" boilerplate for hundreds of members across 8 interfaces would be unmaintainable, so a Roslyn `IIncrementalGenerator` emits it at compile time: annotate a partial decorator with `[GenerateInterfaceDelegation(typeof(IPage))]`, and the generator emits a public forwarding member for every interface member the class doesn't already declare.

It's fully statically typed with **no reflection on the hot path** (`DispatchProxy` is used only in test fakes), and it faithfully reproduces async signatures, generics + constraints, `ref`/`out`/`in`/`params`, optional/default values, properties, indexers and events. A signature-based "already declared" check is what leaves the hand-written humanized methods untouched.

> Full write-up: [`dotnet/DESIGN-SOURCE-GENERATOR.md`](dotnet/DESIGN-SOURCE-GENERATOR.md).

### Tests

**242 total (241 passing / 1 skipped)**, all browser-free (production wrappers exercised through DispatchProxy-backed Playwright fakes; `InternalsVisibleTo` for internal seams). The single skipped test is an end-to-end click-timing check that requires a real browser — verified manually instead.

Coverage includes version/checksum parsing, zip-slip, Ed25519 signature (valid / tampered / bad-sig / downgrade / missing-entry / transient-fetch, free + Pro), license key resolution + cache TTL/expiry, Bézier math, non-ASCII keyboard routing, pointer-events fail-open, the shared timeout budget, focus-aware press/clear, the transparent-wrapper delegate-vs-humanize behavior, and config merge immutability. License/signature tests are ported from `tests/test_license.py`, `js/tests/license.test.ts`, and the signature suites. Build is clean: **0 warnings**.

I'll maintain the .NET client going forward, same as the humanize layer. Anything here you'd like adjusted, just say and I'll turn it around.

Looking forward to your review — happy to adjust, re-test, or rework anything you'd like before merge. Just point me at it.

### Build & test locally

```bash
cd dotnet
dotnet build CloakBrowser.sln -c Release   # 0 warnings
dotnet test  CloakBrowser.sln -c Release   # 242 total (241 passed / 1 skipped)

title: Feature: native omnibar profile identity chip (CLI switches)
body:
## Summary

Anti-detect launchers (GPM Login, Stealth Browser Console) need a **native** profile label inside the omnibar so operators can tell windows apart when 20–30 profiles are open.

MV3 extensions are a poor fit (detectable, slow, require `--disable-extensions` off). GPM solves this with a **Chromium UI patch** — grey pill `GPM | 0003` inside the location bar.

Stealth Browser Console (consumer of `cloakbrowser`) already passes these switches on every headed launch:

```
--stealth-profile-label=Stealth | 0003
--stealth-profile-code=0003
--stealth-profile-id=<uuid>
--stealth-profile-group=<optional>
--stealth-profile-tooltip=[0003] · <group>
```

**Request:** parse switches in the CloakBrowser binary and render a small `ProfileIdentityChipView` in `LocationBarView` (left of the lock icon). Hide chip when `--stealth-profile-label` is empty.

## Motivation

- Zero extension subsystem overhead
- Not visible to page JavaScript (browser chrome only)
- Matches industry UX (GPM / AdsPower / GoLogin)
- P0003 launcher is ready — only binary support is missing

## Proposed implementation

See attached spec from P0003 (full detail):

- Register switches in `chrome_switches.cc`
- `ProfileIdentityChipController` reads command line at startup
- `LocationBarView` hosts pill + optional gear popup (native bubble, not extension)
- Windows first; macOS/Linux follow

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Chip renders when `--stealth-profile-label` is set
- [ ] No chip when switches omitted
- [ ] No new web-exposed APIs
- [ ] Tooltip from `--stealth-profile-tooltip`
- [ ] Manual test: 3 parallel profiles show unique labels

## Reference

- GPM Login omnibar chip (screenshot available on request)
- P0003 spec: https://github.com/tuanhoangfx/Stealth-Browser-Console/blob/main/docs/OMNIBAR-PROFILE-CHIP-SPEC.md
- Launcher code: `buildOmnibarChipChromeArgs()` in Stealth Browser Console

## Non-goals

- Extension-based toolbar badges
- In-page DOM injection
- Changing fingerprint / automation detection behavior

title: fix: validate fingerprint seed to prevent path traversal (CVE-2026-45727)
body:
## Summary

Fixes CVE-2026-45727 — path traversal via crafted fingerprint seed values.

The `fingerprint` parameter is used as a filesystem path component to isolate per-seed Chrome profiles. A malicious value like `../../etc/passwd` could escape the intended directory. This PR validates the seed at **all 4 entry points** with a strict regex:

```
^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$
```

### Entry points hardened
1. **Query param** (`parse_connection_params`) — `?fingerprint=...`
2. **WS path** (`handle_ws_seed`) — `/fingerprint/{seed}/devtools/...`
3. **CLI arg** (`parse_cli_args`) — `--fingerprint=...`
4. **HTTP handlers** (`handle_json_version`, `handle_json_list`) — return `400` on invalid seed

### Tests
10 new tests covering traversal attempts (`../../`, `.`, `..`, `/`, `\\`, spaces) and valid inputs (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores).

```
python3 -m pytest tests/test_cloakserve.py -v
# 40 passed, 1 warning in 0.10s

🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials, lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.
await context.credentials.create('example.com', {
id: credentialId,
userHandle,
privateKey,
publicKey,
});
await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com/login');
// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

🗃️ Web Storage

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

New APIs

title: Implement ability to override functions
body:
Hello,

It would be a very nice feature for CloakBrowser to introduce a simple API that allows functions to be overridden without leaving any traces. Currently, when overriding a function, there are many ways to check if someone has overridden the native code. From the simple comparison of toString to many others. It’s a race, and even if we manage to bypass it on one site, another one that’s more advanced will always detect it. puppeteer-extra has advanced utilities that do this, but they are also already outdated. I suggest adding some kind of API to the browser that would allow this. I know it’s difficult, but it’s really the only and final option that CloakBrowser is missing.

title: Python launch_context: macOS profile triggers Browser Tampering / Virtual Machine signals; Windows profile triggers unusual activity
body:
**Description:**

I am using CloakBrowser (Python wrapper) while trying to create an account on Amazon.co.jp. I need to use macOS platform spoofing to avoid "unusual activity detected" during the signup process, specifically when reaching the password setting step.

**What I expected:**
I was hoping for one of these two clean outcomes:

- Either: use a Windows platform spoof and still be able to create an account on Amazon.co.jp without triggering "unusual activity detected" during the signup process (particularly at the password setting step).

- Or: use macOS platform spoofing (`--fingerprint-platform=macos`) to successfully create the account, while having clean Fingerprint.com smart signals with **no** "Browser Tampering", **no** "Virtual Machine", and fonts matching exactly what a real Mac reports on the playground (only "Arial Unicode MS", "Gill Sans", "Helvetica Neue", "Menlo" — observed on both M2 and Intel Macs).

**What actually happens:**
- Using `--fingerprint-platform=macos` is required to pass the password setting step on amazon.co.jp without "unusual activity detected".
- However, on `https://demo.fingerprint.com/playground` I consistently see:
  - "Browser Tampering: Yes" (high confidence, `anti_detect_browser: true`)
  - "Virtual Machine: Yes"
  - "Incognito: true"
  - The fonts list is dominated by Windows fonts (e.g. "Century Gothic", "Segoe UI Light", etc.) instead of expected macOS fonts.
- The `raw_device_attributes.fonts` and JS font detection probes do not reflect the macOS fonts, even when providing a full set of real macOS font files.

When using a Windows platform spoof or very minimal fingerprint flags, creating the account fails with "unusual activity detected" exactly at the password definition screen (after entering the email). Passing that specific step is the main blocker.

I have tested many configurations on both native Windows and WSL2.

---

**CloakBrowser version:**
Version: 0.3.31

Wrapper: **Python**

---

**Environment:**
- Primary: Windows 10 host (native Python 3.12)
- Secondary (recommended for virtual display): WSL2 Ubuntu (with xvfb + pyvirtualdisplay)
- Not using Docker
- Architecture: x64
- Proxies: <REDACTED_PROXY_PROVIDER> residential JP rotating SOCKS5 (socks5://<REDACTED_PROXY_CREDENTIALS>@<REDACTED_PROXY_HOST>:1080)
- No Docker

---

**Launch options:**
```python
from cloakbrowser import launch_context

browser_args = [
    f"--fingerprint={seed}",
    "--fingerprint-platform=macos",
    "--fingerprint-noise=false",
    "--fingerprint-webrtc-ip=auto",
    # Previously also tried (and removed per latest iteration):
    # f"--fingerprint-screen-width=...",
    # f"--fingerprint-screen-height=...",
    # "--fingerprint-fonts-dir=..."
]

ctx = launch_context(
    headless=False,                    # + virtual display in WSL
    geoip=True,
    proxy="socks5://<REDACTED_PROXY_CREDENTIALS>@<REDACTED_PROXY_HOST>:1080",
    # viewport deliberately omitted in latest version (let seed decide)
    humanize=True,
    extension_paths=[...],             # custom extension sometimes loaded, but results never changed whether I loaded or not an extension
    args=browser_args,
)
```

Other constants used:
- Non-persistent (`launch_context`, no userDataDir, no --fingerprint-storage-quota)
- `headless=False` on virtual Xvfb (via pyvirtualdisplay + `xvfb-run -a` in WSL) or real visible window on native Windows
- Using a random <TEST_EMAIL> address for the signup attempt

---

**Tested with a different IP or proxy?**  
Yes (same result). Multiple JP residential rotating proxies. The "unusual activity on Windows spoof with no flags from FPJS other than incognito" and "tampering/VM on mac spoof" are consistent across IPs.

---

**Works outside Docker / on host machine?**  
Yes (we are not using Docker). Tested directly on Windows 10 host (real visible window) and inside WSL2 Ubuntu.

---

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Launch CloakBrowser using the options shown above (non-persistent `launch_context`, `headless=False` + virtual display when in WSL, or real visible window on native Windows, `platform=macos`, `noise=false`, `geoip=True` + a JP residential SOCKS5 proxy).

2. Go to the Amazon.co.jp account registration page.

3. Attempt to create a new account using a random <TEST_EMAIL> address + name. (e.g. example@icloud.com addresses are never flagged by Amazon in this context)

4. **Critical point**: When you reach the screen to set the password, Amazon always shows "unusual activity detected" unless the macOS platform spoof is active. With Windows with only icognito flag, the block appears reliably at this step.

5. When using the macOS spoof, it is possible to continue past the password step and complete the signup process (reaching the OTP verification page).

6. Separately, open `https://demo.fingerprint.com/playground`, let the signals render, and inspect the smart signals + raw device attributes. A diagnostic JS font probe (classic span offsetWidth test) can also be used to check which fonts the page considers available.

On real Macs (tested on both M2 and Intel), Fingerprint playground only detects these fonts:
fonts: [
0: "Arial Unicode MS"
1: "Gill Sans"
2: "Helvetica Neue"
3: "Menlo"
]

I extracted the complete set of fonts from my real Macs (M2 and Intel, including the Supplemental/ folder) and copied everything into fonts_macos/. Despite providing the full extraction via --fingerprint-fonts-dir, Fingerprint playground still only reported "Century Gothic" as the visible/detected font.

---

**Error output / screenshots:**

**From demo.fingerprint.com/playground (macOS platform spoof, seed-driven, latest minimal args, WSL virtual or Windows host):**

(Full JSON attached in the original report — key excerpt below)

```json
{
  "os": "Mac OS X",
  "os_version": "10.15.7",
  "browser_details": {
    "browser_name": "Chromium-Based Browser",
    "os": "Mac OS X",
    "os_version": "10.15.7"
  },
  "incognito": true,
  "tampering": true,
  "tampering_confidence": "high",
  "tampering_details": {
    "anomaly_score": 1,
    "anti_detect_browser": true
  },
  "virtual_machine": true,
  "virtual_machine_ml_score": 0.109,
  "raw_device_attributes": {
    "fonts": [
      "Agency FB",
      "Century",
      "Century Gothic",
      "Franklin Gothic",
      "Haettenschweiler",
      "Lucida Bright",
      "Lucida Sans",
      "MS Outlook",
      "MS Reference Specialty",
      "MS UI Gothic",
      "Monotype Corsiva",
      "Pristina",
      "Segoe UI Light",
      "ZWAdobeF"
    ],
    "font_preferences": { ... },
    "emoji": { "font": "\"Yu Gothic\"", ... },
    "webgl_basics": {
      "renderer_unmasked": "ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M3 Pro, Unspecified Version)"
    },
    "screen_resolution": [900, 1440],
    "platform": "MacIntel",
    ...
  }
}
```

**Additional observations from runs:**
- "Browser Tampering: Yes" + "Virtual Machine: Yes" appear reliably when using the macOS platform spoof needed to complete signup.
- The fonts array and JS font probe never reflect the macOS fonts. I extracted the complete font set from my real Macs (M2 and Intel, including Supplemental/) into fonts_macos/ and fed it via --fingerprint-fonts-dir, but Fingerprint playground still only saw "Century Gothic".
- On a native Windows host, even with macOS spoof, Windows host fonts (e.g. "Century Gothic") leak to the JS font probe.
- "You are incognito" is reported (expected with non-persistent launch_context).
- With Windows platform spoof with only FPJS Incognito flag the signup on amazon.co.jp hits "unusual activity detected" exactly at the password setting step.

Screenshots available (from diagnostic runs):
- `fingerprint_playground_full_*.png` (showing the tampering/VM tables and signals)
- Screenshots of the Amazon signup flow at the point where "unusual activity" appears
- Manual screenshots taken during testing (using 's' key in console)

---

**Dockerfile (if applicable):**
Not applicable (native Windows + WSL2).

---

**Additional notes:**

**Everything that has been tried (detailed):**
- `launch_persistent_context` vs `launch_context` (non-persistent) — non-persistent mode was used to avoid storage-based signals.
- `headless=True` vs `headless=False` — `headless=True` triggers "verdict detects the headless". `headless=False` is used together with pyvirtualdisplay/Xvfb (in WSL) or a real visible window (on Windows host).
- Forcing viewport + `--fingerprint-screen-width/height` to match the display size (real screen via ctypes on Windows and user-chosen values such as 1920x1080 or 1440x900).
- Providing a full extracted real macOS fonts tree via `--fingerprint-fonts-dir` (hundreds of .ttc/.ttf files + Supplemental/ subdir from a real Mac, with fc-cache on WSL). Recursive scanning and posix path handling were also tested.
- `--fingerprint-noise=false`, `geoip=True` (automatic locale/timezone from the JP proxy), `--fingerprint-webrtc-ip=auto`.
- Removing all manual screen and fonts overrides completely and letting the random `--fingerprint=seed` decide those values (current test configuration).
- Testing on native Windows 10 (real visible window) AND alsos WSL2 Ubuntu using `xvfb-run -a` (virtual headed display).
- Using different JP residential rotating proxies and different  providers.
- Testing signup with other reputable mail providers
- Both manual form filling and assisted flows.
- Both Windows platform spoof (minimal flags) and macOS platform spoof configurations.

**Summary of the core tradeoff:**
- Windows spoof with only FPJS incognito red flags→ "unusual activity detected" appears when trying to create the account, specifically at the password setting step.
- macOS platform spoof (required to complete the signup without the block) → persistent "Browser Tampering: true" (`anti_detect_browser`) + "Virtual Machine: true" on Fingerprint.com, and the fonts list / raw attributes still contain many Windows fonts and trigger tampering detection.

The attached sample `raw_device_attributes` is revealing: it reports a Mac platform + Apple M3 renderer + Japanese locale, but contains a Windows-heavy fonts list ("Century Gothic", "Segoe UI Light", etc.) and has tampering flagged as anti-detect.

We would really appreciate any guidance on:
- Whether `--fingerprint-fonts-dir` is intended to influence the JS-visible fonts list returned in `raw_device_attributes.fonts` (and detected by offsetWidth-style probes) or if it only affects internal canvas / text metrics.
- What the recommended minimal launch options + flags are for obtaining a clean macOS profile that does not trigger tampering or virtual machine signals.
- Known interactions between `launch_context` (non-persistent), virtual display / Xvfb, `geoip=True`, and the tampering / virtual_machine signals.
- How to make the reported font list (and overall profile) more consistent with a real Mac when using the Python wrapper on Windows or WSL.

I am happy to provide the current test script, more raw JSON outputs from the playground, additional screenshots, or run further experiments with specific flag combinations.

---

**Related context:**
This was discovered while trying to signup on Amazon.co.jp using CloakBrowser with different platform spoofs and virtual display setups. The goal is to be able to complete the signup process while keeping the Fingerprint smart signals as clean as possible.

title: Twitch login — CloakBrowser 0.3.31 fails at /protected_login with error_code 5025 while other browsers log in fine (possible regression of #67)
body: Description: Logging into https://www.twitch.tv/login with CloakBrowser 0.3.31 reproducibly fails with Twitch's "Your browser is not currently supported" page. **Other browsers log in to Twitch fine — only CloakBrowser hits this.** That is the end-user observation that prompted this report. The Kasada pipeline mints a `x-kpsdk-ct` token and `/integrity` returns a PASETO token, but the protected business endpoint `POST https://passport.twitch.tv/protected_login` returns: ```json {"request_id":"01KTZP7EZZ61NGPCM85KW8KJAY","has_existing_account":false,"error_code":5025} ``` This looks like a regression of #67 (closed 2026-04-16). Twitch's `5025` is the Kasada "IntegrityFailed" path. The Kasada VM also actively self-reports the environment as suspicious during `ips.js` execution: ``` POST https://reporting.cdndex.io/error → 200 (fires once per run, every run) ``` Per public reverse-engineering notes, any `cdndex.io/error` upload during the challenge means the resulting ct is flagged at Kasada's backend and will be rejected by the protected endpoint regardless of whether the cheap token-mint endpoint accepts it. Observed timeline: ``` /tl (Kasada telemetry, with x-kpsdk-ct) → 200 /integrity (token-mint, with x-kpsdk-ct + x-kpsdk-cd) → 200, PASETO v4.local token /protected_login (real business endpoint) → 400, error_code 5025 ``` This is the two-stage Kasada validation pattern (cheap endpoint stamps; protected endpoint re-validates the environment fingerprint embedded in the ct against a real-browser whitelist). CloakBrowser's source-level patches survive stage one but not stage two on this target. **Expected:** CloakBrowser passes `/protected_login` like other browsers do on the same target, or at least does not trigger the `cdndex.io/error` self-report during `ips.js` execution. **Actual:** `cdndex.io/error` uploaded, `/protected_login` returns `error_code 5025`, page displays "Your browser is not currently supported." CloakBrowser version: 0.3.31 (Chromium binary 146.0.7680.177.5, linux-x64). Also reproduced on 0.3.29 / 146.0.7680.177.3 — upgrading did not change behavior. Wrapper: Python (`cloakbrowser.launch_persistent_context`, sync API). Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8.0), x86_64. No Docker, bare host. Display: tested both `headless=True` and `headless=False` under `xvfb-run`. Proxy: tested both direct and via a residential HTTP proxy. Launch options: ```python ctx = launch_persistent_context( user_data_dir="./twitch-profile", headless=True, # also reproduced with False + xvfb humanize=False, # also reproduced with True geoip=False, # also reproduced with True viewport={"width": 1920, "height": 1080}, args=[ "--fingerprint=42069", "--fingerprint-noise=true", "--fingerprint-screen-width=1920", "--fingerprint-screen-height=1080", ], ) ``` `stealth_args=True` (default). Variables I ruled out: | Variable | Result | | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | CloakBrowser 0.3.29 vs 0.3.31 | Both 5025 | | `headless=True` vs `headless=False` (+ xvfb) | Both 5025 | | `fingerprint=42069` vs `99887` vs `314159` | All three seeds 5025 | | `humanize=True` vs `False` | Both 5025 | | Fresh `user_data_dir` vs reused | Both 5025 | | Direct connection vs residential proxy | Both 5025 | | Username `twitch` (real account) + wrong pw | Still 5025 with `has_existing_account: false` — Kasada rejects the env *before* Twitch even looks up the account, so this is not a credential / account-history issue | | **Other browsers on the same machine/network** | **Log in to Twitch fine — only CloakBrowser fails. This is the observation that prompted filing.** | Tested with a different IP or proxy? Yes (same result) — repeated direct and via a residential proxy with a different exit IP. Same 5025 in both cases. Works outside Docker / on host machine? Not using Docker (bare host). Steps to reproduce: ```python import time from pathlib import Path from cloakbrowser import launch_persistent_context ctx = launch_persistent_context( str(Path("./twitch-profile-repro")), headless=True, humanize=False, geoip=False, viewport={"width": 1920, "height": 1080}, args=["--fingerprint=42069", "--fingerprint-noise=true"], ) page = ctx.new_page() page.goto("https://www.twitch.tv/login", wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=60_000) time.sleep(13) # let p.js → ips.js run page.fill('input[autocomplete="username"]', "any_user_12345") page.fill('input[autocomplete="current-password"]', "AnyWrongPw_99!") page.click('button[data-a-target="passport-login-button"]') time.sleep(15) # Observe: # POST passport.twitch.tv/protected_login → 400 # body: {"request_id":"...","has_existing_account":false,"error_code":5025} # page text: "Your browser is not currently supported." ``` Error output / screenshots: Full network timeline (Playwright `request`/`response` listeners): ``` → GET /fp?x-kpsdk-v=j-1.2.470 ← 429 (initial rate-limit nibble) → GET /mfc ✗ ERR_ABORTED → GET /ips.js?KP_UIDz=... ← 200 (Kasada VM loads + runs) → POST https://reporting.cdndex.io/error ← 200 ❗ self-reported env anomaly → POST /tl (x-kpsdk-ct len=175) ← 200 → POST https://gql.twitch.tv/integrity ← 200 (PASETO v4.local minted) headers: x-kpsdk-ct: 0P1oUlsu4GKFpOfbFuMVLtnGxX2xPZDc... (172 chars) x-kpsdk-v: j-1.2.470 x-kpsdk-cd: {"workTime":...,"id":"d3bce6e4...","answers":[5,4]} client-id: kimne78kx3ncx6brgo4mv6wki5h1ko → POST https://passport.twitch.tv/protected_login ← 400 ❌ environment rejected body: {"request_id":"...","has_existing_account":false,"error_code":5025} ``` Browser console signals under `headless=True`: ``` [error] Failed to load resource: status 429 (https://...kpsdk-v=j-1.2.470) [warning] Automatic fallback to software WebGL has been deprecated. (×3 — Linux headless without GPU falls back to SwiftShader) [error] Failed to load resource: status 400 (.../protected_login) ``` Under `headless=False` + `xvfb-run`: ``` [error] Failed to load resource: status 429 (kpsdk-v=j-1.2.470) [error] Failed to load resource: status 400 (.../protected_login) (no SwiftShader warnings — GL stack works under xvfb, but the protected_login failure is unchanged) ``` So the SwiftShader fallback under headless is at most an aggravating factor, not the root cause — the same 5025 happens even with a real GL stack. Dockerfile (if applicable): N/A — bare host. Additional notes: - 100% reproducible across 8+ runs, multiple days, multiple seeds. - Reproduced with both fresh and existing `user_data_dir`. - Reproduced with both throwaway usernames and a real existing Twitch username (`twitch`) — the `has_existing_account: false` field in the 5025 body confirms Twitch rejects on environment integrity before it ever looks up the username, so this is not a credential / account-history issue. Suggested investigation paths: 1. **What changed since #67's closing fix in April 2026?** Kasada has shipped multiple `j-1.2.x` builds since; we are now on `j-1.2.470`. Re-running the original fix's verification against current Twitch production would surface the regression. 2. **Decoded payload of `reporting.cdndex.io/error`** — Kasada base64 + custom encoding. If CloakHQ has decoded a sample, the body should name which specific environment check failed (Canvas / WebGL renderer / hardware / screen / etc.), pointing directly at the leaking patch. 3. **Two-stage validation pattern** — the cheap `/integrity` endpoint accepting the token does not mean the environment is clean. Internal tests on Twitch should specifically check `/protected_login` (or `/protected_register`) response codes, not just `/integrity` 200. Worth adding to the test matrix if it isn't already. 4. **WebGL renderer under `headless=True`** — Chromium falls back to SwiftShader on Linux hosts without GPU. Does CloakBrowser's patch override `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` strings on the SwiftShader path? ```js const gl = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('webgl'); const ext = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info'); console.log(gl.getParameter(ext.UNMASKED_VENDOR_WEBGL), gl.getParameter(ext.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL)); ``` Note: failure persists under `headless=False + xvfb` where this warning doesn't fire, so SwiftShader isn't the whole story. Happy to share the full network JSON (~40 KB) and page screenshot, and to retest any prerelease build against this exact harness.

title: security: fail-closed binary checksum verification + version-tag validation
body:
## Summary

Two small, self-contained, backward-compatible hardening changes to the binary supply chain (Python + TS clients), with new tests.

### 1. Checksum verification fails closed (was fail-open)
`_verify_download_checksum` / `verifyDownloadChecksum` previously **logged a warning and used the binary** when `SHA256SUMS` could not be fetched, or had no entry for the platform archive. Since every release publishes `SHA256SUMS` (and there's a build-provenance attestation), the client should enforce it:
- Missing checksums / missing entry now **raise** instead of proceeding.
- The existing `CLOAKBROWSER_SKIP_CHECKSUM=true` escape hatch is preserved (custom mirrors / offline builds).
- `_fetch_checksums` now skips an empty parse (e.g. a redirect to an HTML 404 page) and falls through to the next mirror, so a misbehaving primary can't shadow a good fallback or satisfy the check with junk. `_parse_checksums` requires a valid 64‑hex digest per line (the TS regex already did).

I verified that the live release `SHA256SUMS` is reachable and contains each platform's entry, so this does **not** break installs.

### 2. Version‑tag validation
The Chromium version comes from the GitHub release **tag name** and flows into cache paths, download URLs, and (Windows, TS client) the PowerShell zip‑extraction command. Added `is_safe_version_tag` / `isSafeVersionTag` (`^\d+(\.\d+){0,9}$`):
- `_get_latest_chromium_version` / `getLatestChromiumVersion` skip any release whose version isn't plain dotted‑numeric.
- Cache‑marker versions are validated before use in `get_effective_version`.
- TS zip extraction passes the archive/destination paths to PowerShell via **environment variables** instead of interpolating them into the `-Command` string, so a path/version containing a quote can't be parsed as code.

## Tests
- New `tests/test_supplychain_hardening.py` (fail‑closed, mirror fall‑through, version validation) — passing.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean. (Pre‑existing Windows‑only failures in `test_update`/`test_config`/`test_extract` are unrelated — they hard‑code `.tar.gz`/POSIX paths.)

## Deliberately NOT included here (to avoid duplicating existing open PRs)
- Opt‑in `cloakserve` authentication — already proposed in #248.
- Archive‑extraction path‑ancestry hardening — already proposed in #227 (Python side); the TS `extractTar` guard could get the same treatment as a follow‑up.

Happy to adjust scope, split, or rename anything if preferred.

title: fix: auto-add --disable-extensions-except for --load-extension in args
body:
## Problem

When Chrome extensions are loaded via `--load-extension` in `args`/`extra_args` (e.g., through CloakBrowser-Managers `launch_args`), extensions fail to load because Playwrights default `--disable-extensions` flag blocks all extensions.

The `extension_paths` parameter (added in #210) already handles this correctly by injecting both `--load-extension` and `--disable-extensions-except`. However, when `--load-extension` is passed via `args` directly (as CloakBrowser-Manager does), the companion `--disable-extensions-except` flag is **not** automatically injected, leaving extensions broken.

This affects all CloakBrowser-Manager users who try to load extensions via `launch_args`. Related issues:
- CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager#30
- CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager#37

## Fix

In `build_args()`, after processing `extension_paths`, check if `--load-extension` exists in the `seen` dict (from `extra_args`) but `--disable-extensions-except` does not. If so, automatically inject the companion flag with the same paths.

This makes extension loading work seamlessly via either:
1. `extension_paths=["/path/to/ext"]` — existing, unchanged behavior
2. `args=["--load-extension=/path/to/ext"]` — now auto-fixed

**Files changed:**
- `cloakbrowser/browser.py` — Python `build_args()` — auto-inject companion flag
- `js/src/args.ts` — JS `buildArgs()` — same logic
- `tests/test_build_args.py` — 5 new Python tests
- `js/tests/extension-loading.test.ts` — 4 new JS tests

## Testing

All 43 Python tests pass, all 5 JS tests pass:

```
tests/test_build_args.py::test_load_extension_auto_adds_companion PASSED
tests/test_build_args.py::test_load_extension_multi_path_auto_adds_companion PASSED
tests/test_build_args.py::test_load_extension_no_duplicate_companion PASSED
tests/test_build_args.py::test_no_companion_without_load_extension PASSED
tests/test_build_args.py::test_extension_paths_still_works PASSED

js/tests/extension-loading.test.ts (5 tests) PASSED
```

## Backward Compatibility

- Existing `extension_paths` parameter behavior is unchanged (the `elif` only fires when `extension_paths` is falsy)
- If users already manually include `--disable-extensions-except` in their args, no duplication occurs (checked via `seen` dict)
- No API changes, no new parameters

title: fix(humanize): share timeout budget in select_option (follow-up to #307)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #307.

`58ccdb6` fixed the multi-wait timeout bug (a 5s timeout waiting ~15s) for
`click` / `dblclick` / `hover` / `dragAndDrop` on frame and ElementHandle by
sharing a single `deadline` + `remainingMs()` budget. The **`select_option`**
paths were missed and still have the same class of bug.

Each `select_option` helper computes a shared deadline for the actionability +
hover steps, but then calls the **native** `select_option` with the *original
full* `timeout` instead of the remaining budget — so the native call restarts the
clock. A slow `<select>` can therefore wait up to **~2× the requested timeout**.
The frame-level wrapper didn't even compute a deadline (full timeout to both the
hover and the native select).

## Changes

Thread the remaining budget into the native call across every variant:

- **page** `_human_select_option` (sync + async)
- **ElementHandle** `_human_el_select_option` (sync + async) — both the
  move-failed early-return and the normal path
- **frame** `_frame_select_option` (sync + async) — add a shared deadline
- **Locator** `_humanized_select_option` (sync + async) now delegates to
  `page.select_option` (like `click`/`hover`/`fill` already do), so there's a
  single source of truth for the budget instead of a second hover + native wait

## Testing

```
python -m pytest tests/test_humanize_unit.py -k TestSelectOptionTimeoutBudget
# 3 passed
```

New `TestSelectOptionTimeoutBudget`:
- page native `select_option` receives the **remaining** budget (`< 5000`), not the full timeout
- `Locator.select_option` delegates to `page.select_option` with the forwarded timeout
- frame `select_option` shares one deadline across hover + native select

Each test fails against the pre-fix behaviour. Full `tests/test_humanize_unit.py`
run: **76 passed**; the only failures are 5 async tests that also fail on a clean
`main` here (the env has no `pytest-asyncio` configured) — unrelated to this change.

title: Export Browser Session Diagnostics for Easier Bug Reporting
body:
## Problem

When users encounter issues such as browser crashes, download failures, profile corruption, memory leaks, proxy configuration problems, or unexpected behavior, it is often difficult to provide maintainers with enough diagnostic information to reproduce the issue.

Currently, users need to manually collect environment details, browser version information, operating system data, configuration settings, and logs. This slows down troubleshooting and increases back-and-forth communication in GitHub issues.

## Proposed Solution

Add a built-in **Export Diagnostics** feature that generates a sanitized diagnostic bundle containing:

* CloakBrowser version
* Operating system and architecture
* Browser engine version
* Enabled configuration options
* Installed extensions (optional)
* Memory and performance statistics
* Recent application logs
* Crash reports (if available)

The export should automatically remove sensitive information such as:

* Cookies
* Authentication tokens
* Saved passwords
* Personal browsing history
* Proxy credentials
* API keys

Example workflow:

1. User encounters a problem.
2. User clicks **Help → Export Diagnostics**.
3. CloakBrowser generates a ZIP or JSON diagnostic package.
4. User attaches the package to a GitHub issue.

## Use Case

This would significantly improve bug reporting and issue triage.

Examples:

* Download failures
* Browser startup crashes
* Persistent profile issues
* Proxy configuration errors
* Platform-specific compatibility bugs

Instead of manually gathering logs and configuration details, users can provide a standardized diagnostic package in seconds.

## Alternatives Considered

* Manually collecting logs from various directories.
* Copying configuration files by hand.
* Creating custom scripts to gather environment information.

These approaches are error-prone and often result in incomplete bug reports.

## Impact

* Faster issue resolution.
* Better reproducibility for maintainers.
* Reduced support burden.
* More consistent bug reports across platforms.

This feature would likely be used whenever users submit bug reports, improving the overall debugging workflow for both users and maintainers.

title: Widevine CDM not registering on Linux ARM64
body:
**Description:**
Widevine CDM doesn't register on Linux ARM64. Same CDM works with system Chromium (apt install chromium).

**CloakBrowser version**: 0.3.31

**Wrapper**: Python

**Environment**: Debian ARM64 (aarch64), glibc 2.41

**Launch options:**
launch_persistent_context(user_data_dir, headless=False)

Also tried: CLOAKBROWSER_WIDEVINE_CDM=/path/to/WidevineCdm - didn't help

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Install Widevine via AsahiLinux widevine-installer
2. Copy WidevineCdm next to chrome binary (per docs)
3. Create hint file in profile: WidevineCdm/latest-component-updated-widevine-cdm
4. Launch with persistent context
5. Widevine not working:
     chrome://components - Widevine not listed
     chrome://media-internals → CDMs - empty
     https://bitmovin.com/demos/drm - no DRM

**Error output:**

System Chromium has CDM registration code:
```
$ strings /usr/lib/chromium/chromium | grep -I widevine
.local/lib/libwidevinecdm.so
../../chrome/browser/component_updater/widevine_cdm_component_installer.cc
Choosing hinted Widevine
Registering hinted Widevine
Registering bundled Widevine
Widevine Content Decryption Module
...
```

CloakBrowser ARM64 missing CDM registration:
```
$ strings chrome | grep -i widevine
Widevine enabled but no library found
Widevine CDM v1.0
com.widevine.alpha
```
No component_installer, no "Registering" strings

**Root cause:** ARM64 build is missing widevine_cdm_component_installer.cc — CDM registration code not compiled in.

**Additional notes:**

1. System Chromium with same CDM → works
2. CloakBrowser x64 with Widevine → works (per issue #96)
3. ARM64 build has Widevine strings in binary, but CDM never registers
4. CloakBrowser macOS (ARM64 & x64) → works

title: WebGL readPixels output appears stable across --fingerprint seeds (per-GPU clustering risk)
body:
Hi CloakBrowser team,

We found a fingerprint stability issue while using CloakBrowser with Playwright persistent contexts.

CloakBrowser correctly randomizes several fingerprint surfaces through the auto-added `--fingerprint=<seed>` argument, but WebGL pixel readback appears to remain stable across launches on the same physical GPU/driver.

## Environment

- Package: `cloakbrowser@0.3.31`
- Chromium: `146.0.7680.177.5`
- Runtime: Node.js 22+
- OS: Windows
- Launch method: Playwright persistent context through `launchCloakPersistentContext`
- Default CloakBrowser stealth args include:
  - `--fingerprint=<random seed>`
  - `--fingerprint-platform=windows`

## Observed behavior

Across multiple launches with different CloakBrowser fingerprint seeds, these values are randomized or normalized as expected:

- Canvas hash
- WebGL renderer string
- `hardwareConcurrency`
- screen properties
- user agent / platform
- fonts
- audio fingerprint

However, actual WebGL pixel readback via `gl.readPixels(...)` stays stable per machine/GPU/driver.

Example diagnostic:

```js
const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
canvas.width = 256;
canvas.height = 128;

const gl = canvas.getContext('webgl') || canvas.getContext('experimental-webgl');

if (!gl) throw new Error('WebGL unavailable');

gl.clearColor(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 1.0);
gl.clear(gl.COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);

gl.enable(gl.SCISSOR_TEST);
gl.scissor(10, 10, 100, 60);
gl.clearColor(0.9, 0.3, 0.1, 1.0);
gl.clear(gl.COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);

const px = new Uint8Array(256 * 128 * 4);
gl.readPixels(0, 0, 256, 128, gl.RGBA, gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE, px);

let h = 0;
const s = Array.from(px.slice(0, 4096)).join(',');
for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
  h = (Math.imul(31, h) + s.charCodeAt(i)) | 0;
}
console.log((h >>> 0).toString(16));
```

Result pattern:

- Same machine + different CloakBrowser seeds -> same `readPixels` hash
- Different machine/GPU/driver -> different `readPixels` hash
- Renderer string may change/spoof, but pixel readback remains tied to actual GPU/driver behavior

## Why this matters

This creates an internally inconsistent fingerprint:

- WebGL renderer string is randomized/spoofed
- Other browser surfaces are randomized/spoofed
- But WebGL pixel raster/readback stays physically stable

This can make sessions from the same host clusterable even when the CloakBrowser seed changes.

In F5 Shape-style protected environments, this appears to be a strong clustering signal. Userland JavaScript patching is not a safe workaround because prototype and native-code integrity checks can detect it.

## Attempted workaround

We tested a page-level `addInitScript` workaround that patched:

- `WebGLRenderingContext.prototype.readPixels`
- `WebGL2RenderingContext.prototype.readPixels`
- `CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype.getImageData`
- `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.toDataURL`
- `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.toBlob`
- `Function.prototype.toString` spoofing for patched functions

The workaround successfully changed the hash per session and kept it deterministic within the same session.

However, this kind of userland prototype patching is detectable by F5 Shape-style integrity checks and caused immediate blocking in real protected environments.

So this does not seem safely fixable from page JavaScript. It likely needs a native/source-level patch inside CloakBrowser, consistent with CloakBrowser's existing design.

## Expected behavior

When `--fingerprint=<seed>` changes, WebGL pixel readback should also vary consistently with that seed.

Suggested properties:

1. `gl.readPixels(...)` output should be deterministic within one browser/session.
2. It should vary across different `--fingerprint` seeds.
3. It should stay internally consistent with other WebGL/canvas spoofed surfaces.
4. It should be implemented natively, not via page-level JS prototype patching.

## Suggested fix direction

Add native seed-based perturbation or normalization for WebGL readback paths, especially:

- WebGL1 `readPixels`
- WebGL2 `readPixels`
- possible canvas-backed GPU raster paths if they share physical readback behavior

The important part is that returned pixel buffers should not expose stable GPU/driver-specific rasterization or float-to-byte differences across different fingerprint seeds.

## Additional note

This is not about WebGL parameter strings only. Those already appear spoofed. The issue is actual pixel data returned by rendering + `readPixels`.

Thanks.

title: Some suggestions
body:
CloakBrowser’s native fingerprinting works well, but in high-risk flows such as DataDome we found that the default seeded randomness is too broad.

The main issues we observed:

1. Default UA may expose Chrome/146.0.0.0. Vinted worked much better when using the full bundled Chromium version, e.g. Chrome/146.0.7680.177, and matching --fingerprint-brand-version.

2. Default GPU randomization can select high-end NVIDIA/AMD discrete GPUs. In our tests, Intel integrated GPUs consistently passed, while NVIDIA RTX / AMD Radeon profiles triggered DataDome captcha.

3. Screen/window values need coherent presets. A case like screen=1920x1080 with outer=1052x830 looked risky. --start-maximized helps, but a built-in coherent random screen/window preset pool would be better.

4. get_default_stealth_args includes --no-sandbox. To remove it, we had to disable stealth_args entirely and manually re-add fingerprint args. More granular default arg control would help.

Feature requests:
- Full bundled-Chromium UA generation and automatic UA/UA-CH/brand-version sync.
- GPU family constraints, e.g. integrated Intel only.
- Exposed GPU profile database or safe preset pools.
- Coherent screen/window randomization.
- Granular default stealth arg overrides.
- GeoIP/WebRTC diagnostics after launch.
- High-level presets such as residential_windows_laptop / conservative.

title: FPJS detects VPN (`os_mismatch` / `timezone_mismatch`) and Virtual Machine when running CloakBrowser in Docker Desktop on macOS
body: ## FPJS detects VPN (`os_mismatch` / `timezone_mismatch`) and Virtual Machine when running CloakBrowser in Docker Desktop on macOS ### Environment - Host OS: macOS - Runtime: Docker Desktop on macOS - Docker platform: `linux/amd64` - CloakBrowser binary: `146.0.7680.177.5` - CloakBrowser image: custom image based on `cloakhq/cloakbrowser:latest` - Browser mode: headed, running through `Xvfb` + `x11vnc` + `noVNC` - Proxy: `http://host.docker.internal:10808` - Target: `https://demo.fingerprint.com/playground` - Launch API: `launchPersistentContext` - Minimal Windows fonts mounted into Docker: - `calibri.ttf` - `framd.ttf` - `marlett.ttf` - `msgothic.ttc` - `segoeui.ttf` - `segoeuil.ttf` The font mount follows the recommendation from issue #193. I am not using `--fingerprint-fonts-dir`. ### Launch code ```js import { launchPersistentContext } from "/app/js/dist/index.js"; import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, rmSync } from "node:fs"; const profileDir = process.env.CLOAK_PROFILE_DIR || "/profiles/fingerprint"; const targetUrl = "https://demo.fingerprint.com/playground"; const proxy = process.env.CLOAK_PROXY || "http://host.docker.internal:10808"; const fontsDir = process.env.CLOAK_FONTS_DIR || "/usr/share/fonts/windows"; const browserLaunchArgs = [ "--fingerprint-platform=windows", "--fingerprint-noise=false", "--fingerprint-storage-quota=500", "--fingerprint-screen-width=1920", "--fingerprint-screen-height=1080", ]; mkdirSync(profileDir, { recursive: true }); for (const name of readdirSync(profileDir)) { rmSync(`${profileDir}/${name}`, { recursive: true, force: true }); } const context = await launchPersistentContext({ userDataDir: profileDir, proxy, geoip: true, headless: false, humanize: true, humanPreset: "careful", viewport: { width: 1920, height: 1080 }, args: browserLaunchArgs, }); const page = context.pages()[0] || await context.newPage(); await page.goto(targetUrl, { waitUntil: "domcontentloaded" }); ``` ```bash docker run --platform linux/amd64 -d --name cloak-fingerprint --shm-size=1g \ -p 127.0.0.1:5900:5900 \ -p 127.0.0.1:6080:6080 \ -e CLOAK_PROXY=http://host.docker.internal:10808 \ -e CLOAK_PROFILE_DIR=/profiles/fingerprint \ -e CLOAK_FONTS_DIR=/usr/share/fonts/windows \ -e CLOAK_CLEAR_PROFILE=1 \ -v /path/to/profile:/profiles/fingerprint \ -v /path/to/windows-fonts:/usr/share/fonts/windows:ro \ cloakbrowser-vnc:146-amd64-minfonts ``` ```text --fingerprint-platform=windows --fingerprint-noise=false --fingerprint-storage-quota=500 --fingerprint-screen-width=1920 --fingerprint-screen-height=1080 --fingerprint-webrtc-ip= --fingerprint-timezone=America/Chicago --lang=en-US --fingerprint-locale=en-US ``` So geoip: true appears to be working. Timezone, locale, and WebRTC IP are injected. FPJS result On https://demo.fingerprint.com/playground, I get: ```json { "bot": "not_detected", "incognito": true, "tampering": false, "virtual_machine": true, "virtual_machine_ml_score": 0.144, "vpn": true, "vpn_confidence": "high", "vpn_origin_timezone": "America/Chicago", "vpn_methods": { "timezone_mismatch": true, "public_vpn": false, "auxiliary_mobile": false, "os_mismatch": true, "relay": false }, "raw_device_attributes": { "timezone": "America/Chicago", "date_time_locale": "en-US", "screen_resolution": [1920, 1080], "platform": "Win32", "fonts": [ "Calibri", "Franklin Gothic", "MS UI Gothic", "Marlett", "Segoe UI Light" ], "webgl_basics": { "vendor_unmasked": "Google Inc. (NVIDIA)", "renderer_unmasked": "ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (0x00002489) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)" } } } ``` What works bot is not_detected tampering is false Minimal 6-font Windows mount works correctly geoip: true injects timezone / locale / WebRTC IP --fingerprint-storage-quota=500 avoids nodriver Problems FPJS still detects VPN: vpn: true vpn_methods.timezone_mismatch: true vpn_methods.os_mismatch: true FPJS still detects Virtual Machine: virtual_machine: true virtual_machine_ml_score around 0.14-0.20 Additional tests I tried removing Xvfb / noVNC. Test: official image, no Xvfb/noVNC, headless: true Result got worse: ```json { "bot": "not_detected", "incognito": true, "virtual_machine": true, "virtual_machine_ml_score": 0.56, "tampering": true, "tampering_ml_score": 0.8068, "vpn": true, "vpn_methods": { "timezone_mismatch": true, "os_mismatch": true } } ``` Missing X server or $DISPLAY Looks like you launched a headed browser without having a XServer running. So removing Xvfb/noVNC does not help. Headless mode is worse, and headed mode requires an X server inside Docker. Question Is this expected when using Docker Desktop on macOS with --fingerprint-platform=windows? My guess is that FPJS may be detecting a mismatch between: browser fingerprint: Windows Docker Desktop / Linux VM network stack proxy network signature Xvfb virtual display environment Is there any recommended configuration for Docker Desktop on macOS to avoid: vpn_methods.os_mismatch vpn_methods.timezone_mismatch virtual_machine: true while keeping: launchPersistentContext headless: false geoip: true Windows fingerprint minimal 6-font mount bot: not_detected tampering: false

title: Support CommonJS in the JS package
body:
## Summary

This PR adds CommonJS support for the `js` package while keeping the existing ESM exports.

## Changes

- Build both ESM and CommonJS outputs with `tsup`
- Add `require` entries to `exports` for:
  - `cloakbrowser`
  - `cloakbrowser/puppeteer`
  - `cloakbrowser/human`
- Set `main` to the CommonJS entrypoint
- Keep `module` pointing to the ESM entrypoint

## Why

The package already exposed ESM entrypoints, but it did not provide official CommonJS entrypoints through `exports`.

This change allows usage like:

```js
const { launch } = require('cloakbrowser');

I'm using cloakbrowser manager to launch the browsers, and to reproduce this issue we can just launch cloakbrowser manager using the simple docker run command, launch the test browser profile and navigate to https://recaptcha-demo.appspot.com/recaptcha-v2-checkbox.php to solve the captcha. 

In my own browser it solves almost immediately with no image selection challenge. In incognito a simple challenge will be presented (select all traffic lights) and once selected it is considered solved.

From cloakbrowser however, we get the "verify once there are none left" type of challenge which take significantly longer to solve, and it does not even clear after the first one, it asks the user to try again and again. title: Request a macOS Apple Silicon binary build alongside Linux x64 and Windows x64
body:
## Summary

The latest release (chromium-v146.0.7680.177.5) ships `cloakbrowser-linux-x64.tar.gz` and `cloakbrowser-windows-x64.zip`. There is no macOS binary, neither Intel nor Apple Silicon. Mac users currently have to either build from source (long), run via Docker (no GUI / window-creation friction), or skip CloakBrowser entirely. This locks Mac developers out of the simplest install path.

## Evidence

Latest release assets, verified 2026-05-26.
- https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/releases/tag/chromium-v146.0.7680.177.5 lists `cloakbrowser-linux-x64.tar.gz`, `cloakbrowser-windows-x64.zip`, `SHA256SUMS`. No `cloakbrowser-macos-arm64.tar.gz` or `cloakbrowser-macos-x64.tar.gz`.

Mac users are already on the platform and testing. Open issues confirm active macOS usage with no native binary path.
- #273 "Incorrect window sizes and viewport parameters on macOS" (bug, May 2026)
- #246 "How to open browser with a specific profile on macOS?" (May 2026)
- #181 "Canvas and Audio fingerprint unchanged across different --fingerprint seeds on macOS Apple Silicon (M4)" (April 2026)
- #236 "On Apple Silicon Macs, the auto-spoof default sets UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL to ... regardless of the real chip" (bug, May 2026)
- #82 "--fingerprint-locale does not override Intl API default locale on macOS" (March 2026)

Past attempts to ship Mac-adjacent builds.
- #51 "Docker image not available for arm64" (closed March 2026) confirms ARM64 demand existed before. Docker arm64 ships now but the host integration friction on macOS is real (no native window, no system fingerprint inheritance).
- #72 "Latest Cloakbrowser Chromium Download URL Not Found - 404" (closed) shows the download infrastructure is the bottleneck for asset variety.

## Expected behavior

Each Chromium release ships at least one of.
- `cloakbrowser-macos-arm64.tar.gz` for Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4)
- `cloakbrowser-macos-x64.tar.gz` for Intel Macs

Distributed via the same release page as Linux and Windows, with matching SHA256SUMS coverage. Installation flow should match the Linux pattern (download tarball, extract, run binary).

## Actual behavior

No macOS binary in any release in the chromium-v146.x release line. Mac developers must compile Chromium from source (3 to 6 hour build on M-series, longer on Intel), which defeats the value of a curated stealth build.

## Why existing issues do not cover this

Searched the repo for "macos", "darwin", and "mac binary". The matches above are all bug reports about specific macOS runtime behaviors. No existing open or closed issue requests a macOS binary build directly. Closest is #51 about Docker arm64 which was resolved by shipping ARM64 Docker, not a native macOS binary.

## Request

1. Add a macOS Apple Silicon binary (`cloakbrowser-macos-arm64.tar.gz`) to the standard release flow.
2. Optionally add a macOS Intel binary (`cloakbrowser-macos-x64.tar.gz`). Lower priority given Apple Silicon market share but useful for legacy hardware.
3. Include both in `SHA256SUMS`.
4. Document the install flow in the README for macOS users (download, xattr -d com.apple.quarantine if needed, run).

Happy to test pre-release builds on a real M-series Mac if useful (Darwin 25.5.0, Apple Silicon).

## Use case context

I am trying to use CloakBrowser to run an authenticated browser automation flow for legitimate research on dummy freelancer account on Upwork. The standard Playwright fingerprint is detected by Cloudflare and returns 403 even with valid session cookies imported. CloakBrowser's stealth patches would resolve this on Linux and Windows, but there is no path on macOS without compiling from source. A native macOS binary would unlock the documented use case for the Mac developer audience.

---

**Suggested labels**: `enhancement`, `help wanted`
