title: Feature Request: Isolated World Evaluation (Undetectable DOM Access)
body:
# Problem

`page.evaluate()` runs in the main world, making all automation-initiated DOM access detectable by anti-bot systems.

### Verified Detection Vectors (tested on CloakBrowser v0.3.19)

**1. Error.stack trace leaks**
```
Error: test
    at eval (eval at evaluate (:302:30), <anonymous>:3:13)
    at Object.evaluate (<anonymous>:304:16)
```
The `eval at evaluate (:302:30)` frame reveals CDP-initiated code execution. Anti-bot systems checking `Error.stack` patterns detect this.

**2. DOM mutations triggered**
`MutationObserver` on the page fires when evaluate modifies the DOM. Confirmed: `DOM mutations detected: true` after evaluate.

**3. Performance entries**
`performance.getEntries()` shows evaluate-related entries visible to page JS.

**4. addInitScript visibility**
Variables set via `page.addInitScript()` are visible to page JS in the main world.

**5. locator.toString`. native functions still report `[native code]`

## Proposed Solution

An isolated execution context for DOM reads that:
1. Can query the DOM (querySelector, getBoundingClientRect, elementFromPoint)
2. 2. Produces clean Error.stack traces (no `eval at evaluate` frames)
3. 3. Doesn't trigger MutationObservers for read-only operations
4. 4. Variables set in isolated context are NOT visible to main world JS
5. 5. No performance timeline artifacts
### API

```typescript
// Isolated. undetectable DOM read
const rect = await page.evaluateIsolated(() => {
  return document.querySelector('#btn').getBoundingClientRect();
});

// Main world. existing behavior (for when you need to modify the page)
await page.evaluate(() => { ... });
```

### Reference: Camoufox

[Camoufox](https://camoufox.com/python/main-world-eval/) (Firefox/Gecko) provides this. their `page.evaluate()` runs in an isolated world by default. Main world access requires explicit `mw:` prefix and is documented as detectable. This is the model to follow.

## Implementation

Chromium's `blink::DOMWrapperWorld` already supports multiple isolated worlds (used by Chrome extensions). A new world type for automation. separate from extension worlds to avoid extension-detection heuristics. could provide DOM access with clean execution traces.

## Environment

- CloakBrowser v0.3.19
- Chromium 145
 -  macOS arm64

title: fix: allow null viewport to disable viewport emulation
body:
## Problem

Passing `viewport: null` to `launchPersistentContext()` has no effect — the browser always launches with `DEFAULT_VIEWPORT` (1920×947) because the `??` operator treats `null` the same as `undefined`.

## Root cause

```ts
viewport: options.viewport ?? DEFAULT_VIEWPORT
```

`??` coalesces both `null` and `undefined`, so an explicit `null` (which in Playwright means "disable viewport emulation and let the OS window control the size") is silently replaced by `DEFAULT_VIEWPORT`.

## Fix

Use a strict `undefined` check so `null` is passed through to Playwright:

```ts
viewport: options.viewport === undefined ? DEFAULT_VIEWPORT : options.viewport,
```

Also update the `viewport` type in `LaunchContextOptions` to accept `null`:

```ts
viewport?: { width: number; height: number } | null;
```

## Why it matters

Desktop apps (e.g. Electron) need the browser content to resize with the window. With `viewport: null`, Playwright/Chromium uses the actual window dimensions and responds to resize events. Without this fix there is no way to opt out of the fixed 1920×947 default.

title: Chrome always launches to same position in xvfb
body:
Unless some sort of window manager overrides this behaviour Chrome will always initialise browser window to 10, 10 by default.

`console.log(window.screenX, window.screenY)`

Subsequent chrome windows if more than one gets opened will also be offset by some amount from the last opened window. Users will also often move and re-arrange window. A screenX=10, screenY=10 is therefore an indicator of automation. 

Introducing some noise into the initialised position would help prevent fingerprinting.

WebRTC detection
body:
Currently, the browser appears to hide the IP address for WebRTC, preventing leakage. While this solution works in most cases, many anti-bot systems actually flag the absence of an IP address, which can lead to failures or blocking.

(I manually tested a couple of PX captchas and was unable to solve them without a leaked WebRTC IP while using a mobile proxy. However, when I switched to a hotspot (which allowed IP leakage), the captchas were solved successfully.

I further confirmed this by creating a simple spoofing extension that replaces the WebRTC IP. Even though the extension was rudimentary and likely detectable, I was still able to solve captchas again.)

Feature suggestions:

1. Camoufox: Implements WebRTC IP spoofing at the protocol level by modifying ICE candidates and SDP before they are sent.
2. Google forwarding: I’m not entirely certain how this works, but it likely involves forwarding requests through Google’s public STUN servers and forcing TCP instead of UDP. This could allow Google to reflect the proxy’s IP address without requiring direct modifications, potentially improving the chances of remaining undetected.

title: --fingerprint-locale does not override Intl API default locale on macOS
body:
## Summary

On macOS, the `--fingerprint-locale` flag successfully overrides `navigator.language` and `navigator.languages`, but does **not** override the Intl API default locale (`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale`). This creates a detectable mismatch between the navigator locale and the Intl locale.

**Environment:**
- CloakBrowser `v145.0.7632.109.2` on macOS (darwin-arm64)
- macOS system language: `zh-CN` (Simplified Chinese)
- Launched with `locale="en-US"` which sets `--lang=en-US` and `--fingerprint-locale=en-US`

## Current behavior

```js
navigator.language          // "en-US" ✅ (patched by --fingerprint-locale)
navigator.languages         // ["en-US", "en"] ✅ (after fixing Preferences + --accept-lang)

Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale  // "zh-CN" ❌ (reads from macOS system)
new Intl.NumberFormat().resolvedOptions().locale // "zh-CN" ❌
new Intl.Collator().resolvedOptions().locale     // "zh-CN" ❌
```

Bot detection tools like CreepJS and BrowserLeaks flag this inconsistency: `navigator.language` says `en-US` but the Intl API says `zh-CN`.

## Expected behavior

When `--fingerprint-locale=en-US` is set, **all** locale-related APIs should return `en-US`:
- `navigator.language` ✅ (already works)
- `navigator.languages` ✅ (already works)
- `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale` ❌ (should be `en-US`)
- All other `Intl.*` constructors' default locale ❌ (should be `en-US`)

## Root cause

On macOS, the Intl API's default locale comes from ICU's `icu::Locale::getDefault()`, which reads from Cocoa's `NSLocale` / `AppleLanguages` NSUserDefaults — not from `--lang` or any Chromium command-line flag.

The standard macOS workaround is passing `-AppleLanguages "(en-US)"` as a process argument to override NSUserDefaults. However, this is **not compatible with Playwright** — Playwright's argument parser rejects `-AppleLanguages` (single dash, no `--` prefix) and treats the value `(en-US)` as a page URL, throwing:

```
Error: BrowserType.launch_persistent_context: Arguments can not specify page to be opened
```

This means there is no way for users to fix the Intl locale externally. It needs to be patched at the source level inside CloakBrowser.

## Suggested fix

When `--fingerprint-locale` is set, override `v8::Intl::DefaultLocale()` (or the underlying `icu::Locale::setDefault()`) at startup to match the specified locale. This would make the Intl API consistent with `navigator.language` without relying on macOS system preferences.

This is similar to how `--fingerprint-timezone` overrides the timezone at the binary level rather than relying on `TZ` environment variables.

## Workaround (fragile)

Currently the only workaround is injecting JavaScript via `context.add_init_script()` to proxy all `Intl.*` constructors:

```js
const LOCALE = 'en-US';
for (const name of ['Collator','DateTimeFormat','DisplayNames','ListFormat',
    'NumberFormat','PluralRules','RelativeTimeFormat','Segmenter']) {
    const Orig = Intl[name];
    if (!Orig) continue;
    Intl[name] = function(locales, ...rest) {
        if (locales === undefined) locales = LOCALE;
        return new Orig(locales, ...rest);
    };
    Intl[name].prototype = Orig.prototype;
    if (Orig.supportedLocalesOf)
        Intl[name].supportedLocalesOf = Orig.supportedLocalesOf.bind(Orig);
}
```

This runs in the main world and is itself detectable by bot detection tools (modified constructor `toString()`, main-world script injection, etc.).

## Reproduction

```python
from cloakbrowser import launch_persistent_context

ctx = launch_persistent_context(
    "./test-profile",
    headless=False,
    locale="en-US",  # Sets --lang=en-US and --fingerprint-locale=en-US
)
page = ctx.new_page()
result = page.evaluate("""() => ({
    navigatorLang: navigator.language,
    intlLang: Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale,
})""")
print(result)
# On macOS with system language zh-CN:
# {'navigatorLang': 'en-US', 'intlLang': 'zh-CN'}  ← mismatch
```

Tested on macOS system language `zh-CN`. The issue does not occur on Linux where `--lang` correctly sets the ICU locale.

title: CreepJS Audio trap detects binary-level WebAudio pipeline modification
body:
## Summary

CreepJS (https://abrahamjuliot.github.io/creepjs/) flags the **Audio** fingerprint as tampered (`lies hash` class) on macOS. This occurs both **with and without** `--fingerprint` seed — the patched binary itself produces a detectable audio processing difference.

**Environment:**
- CloakBrowser `v145.0.7632.109.2` on macOS (darwin-arm64, Apple M3)
- Tested on two instances:
  - Instance A: `stealth_args=False`, no `--fingerprint` flag (clean launch)
  - Instance B: `stealth_args=True`, `--fingerprint=53552` with full fingerprint args (screen, GPU, etc.)
- Both instances produce the same Audio detection result

**Note:** Screen fingerprint passes CreepJS with proper `--fingerprint-screen-width/height` args — this issue is Audio-only.

---

## Audio trap detection

CreepJS runs a "trap" audio pipeline specifically designed to detect modifications to the WebAudio processing chain. The trap value is **unstable across page loads and instances**:

### Instance A (no `--fingerprint`, clean launch)

| Run | trap value |
|-----|-----------|
| 1 | `1016.4283441503703` |
| 2 | `999.1696287449392` |
| 3 | `1003.9878614289453` |

### Instance B (with `--fingerprint=53552`, full stealth args)

| Run | trap value |
|-----|-----------|
| 1 | `1008.9074133125515` |

On stock Chrome, this trap value should be **deterministic** — same value every time for the same hardware. The variation across loads strongly suggests the binary's source-level audio patches introduce per-context jitter regardless of whether `--fingerprint` is set.

### Stable values (not affected)

These audio fingerprint values remain consistent across all runs and both instances:
```
sum:    124.04348155876505  (consistent)
gain:   -20.538288116455078 (consistent)
freq:   164524.5661239624   (consistent)
time:   502.599934064001    (consistent)
data:   14b6ef01            (consistent)
copy:   14b6ef01            (consistent)
values: dfc44fc6            (consistent)
```

Only the `trap` value varies, which is what CreepJS uses to detect tampering.

## How CreepJS detects this

CreepJS's trap test creates a specific OfflineAudioContext pipeline (oscillator → compressor → destination) and renders a single sample. On an unmodified Chrome binary, this produces a deterministic value. CloakBrowser's source-level patches to the WebAudio pipeline (noise injection, fingerprint randomization) alter the output even when `--fingerprint` is not passed.

The `trap` value fluctuating between ~999 and ~1016 across page loads is the smoking gun — it proves the audio pipeline is being modified at the binary level, not just through the `--fingerprint` flag.

## CreepJS result

The Audio section is marked with CSS class `lies hash`:
- Audio hash `33619edf` (instance B) → flagged
- Audio hash `b528e02f` (instance A) → flagged

No "Lies" detail section is generated (individual API tampering is not detected), confirming this is a binary-level issue, not a JavaScript-level override.

## Expected behavior

When no `--fingerprint` flag is passed, the WebAudio pipeline should be **completely stock** — no jitter, no noise, no patching. The trap value should be deterministic and identical to stock Chrome.

When `--fingerprint` is passed, the intentional noise should be applied in a way that doesn't cause the trap value to fluctuate between page loads (deterministic per seed).

## Reproduction

```python
from cloakbrowser import launch_persistent_context

# Both of these produce the same Audio detection:

# Clean launch (no fingerprint)
ctx = launch_persistent_context(
    "./test-profile",
    headless=False,
    stealth_args=False,
    args=["--no-sandbox", "--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled"],
)

# With fingerprint
ctx = launch_persistent_context(
    "./test-profile",
    headless=False,
    args=["--fingerprint=53552", "--fingerprint-platform=windows",
          "--fingerprint-gpu-vendor=Google Inc. (NVIDIA)",
          "--fingerprint-gpu-renderer=ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 ...)"],
)

page = ctx.new_page()
page.goto("https://abrahamjuliot.github.io/creepjs/")
# Wait for results → Audio section shows "lies hash"
```

title: CloakBrowser fails to bootstrap Airbnb embedded payment iframe while stock Chromium works
body:
## Summary

We are seeing a CloakBrowser-specific compatibility issue on Airbnb checkout.

On the Airbnb payment step, the embedded payment iframe from `iframes.airbnbpayments.com` loads but never boots correctly in CloakBrowser. The same flow works in stock Chromium.

## Impact

This breaks Airbnb checkout/payment flows in CloakBrowser and forces us to fall back to stock Chromium for this site/flow.

## What we ruled out

We reproduced the failure in pure browser-only mode.

That means:

- no page instrumentation from our side
- no extra capture/debug logic
- no additional runtime hooks from our stack

We also stripped the exposed CloakBrowser launcher settings down to effectively:

- `args: []`
- `ignore_default_args: []`

and explicitly disabled the obvious suspects we could control from the launcher:

- `--no-sandbox`
- `AutomationControlled` masking
- fingerprint args
- ignored Playwright default args

The failure still reproduced.

## Observed behavior

On Airbnb checkout, the parent page creates the payment iframe:

- `https://iframes.airbnbpayments.com/.../iframe_v2.html?...`

But the iframe remains blank and the payment UI never appears correctly.

Inside the failing iframe we observed:

- `document.readyState === "complete"`
- correct `document.referrer` (`https://www.airbnb.com/`)
- empty `#iframe_v2_root`
- no visible rendered content
- `sessionStorage` throws `SecurityError`
- `localStorage` throws `SecurityError`
- `document.cookie === ""`
- no successful ready/resize handshake back to the parent

So the iframe document loads, but its app never mounts.

## Expected behavior

The embedded payment iframe should bootstrap normally and render the card form, as it does in stock Chromium.

## Comparison

- CloakBrowser: fails
- Stock Chromium: works

This strongly suggests a CloakBrowser runtime compatibility issue around third-party iframe storage/bootstrap behavior.

## Repro notes

Environment:

- CloakBrowser Chromium binary: `145.0.7632.109.2`
- Reproduced via Playwright connection path
- Reproduced in headed interactive mode
- Reproduced with launcher-level custom args effectively stripped

High-level repro:

1. Launch CloakBrowser
2. Open Airbnb checkout payment flow
3. Navigate to the "Add a payment method" step
4. Observe that the embedded Airbnb payment iframe never renders its contents

## Likely area

Current best guess is a deeper CloakBrowser issue involving third-party iframe storage/privacy/bootstrap behavior.

Because the iframe loads but storage is denied and the app never mounts, the issue appears to be around embedded payment iframe environment compatibility rather than basic navigation or network reachability.

## 🎯 Implements Issue #62 - SOCKS5 UDP Support ($2000 Bounty)

This PR implements full SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE support (RFC 1928) for tunneling QUIC and WebRTC traffic through SOCKS5 proxies.

## 🚀 Features

### Core Implementation
- ✅ **SOCKS5 UDP Protocol** (`cloakbrowser/socks5udp/protocol.py`)
  - RFC 1928 compliant UDP ASSOCIATE implementation
  - Support for IPv4, IPv6, and domain name addresses
  - 10-byte UDP datagram header packing/unpacking
  - SOCKS5 authentication (username/password)

- ✅ **Async UDP Client** (`cloakbrowser/socks5udp/client.py`)
  - Local UDP relay server (default port 10800)
  - Transparent tunneling of UDP packets
  - Connection management and error handling
  - Integration with asyncio event loop

- ✅ **Browser Integration** (`cloakbrowser/browser.py`)
  - New `socks5_udp` parameter in `launch()`

title: Tip: Use page-level methods instead of ElementHandle to keep humanize patches active
body:
## Context

When using `launch_persistent_context()` with `human_preset="default"`, CloakBrowser patches `page.click()`, `page.type()`, `page.mouse.move()` etc. with Bézier curves and realistic timing. However, these patches only apply at the **page level** — not on ElementHandle objects.

## The Problem

```python
# ❌ Bypasses humanize patch — direct ElementHandle interaction
el = page.query_selector("input#solution")
el.fill("")
el.click()
```

These calls go straight to the underlying Playwright methods, skipping all Bézier movement, timing randomization, and CoalescedEvents injection.

## The Fix

```python
# ✅ Goes through humanize patch — Bézier move + realistic timing
page.click("input#solution")       # scroll to element → Bézier move → human click
page.keyboard.press("Control+a")   # select all
page.keyboard.press("Delete")      # clear field
page.type("input#solution", text)  # human_type with per-key timing
```

## Why It Matters

Anti-bot systems can distinguish between:
- A mouse that teleports instantly to an element (ElementHandle)
- A mouse that curves naturally from its last position (page.click via humanize)

The same applies to keyboard input — `el.fill()` sets the value directly without dispatching any keyboard events, which is a detectable signal.

## Summary

| Method | Humanized | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `page.click(sel)` | ✅ Yes | Use this |
| `page.type(sel, text)` | ✅ Yes | Use this |
| `page.mouse.move(x, y)` | ✅ Yes | Use this |
| `el = page.query_selector(sel); el.click()` | ❌ No | Avoid |
| `el.fill(value)` | ❌ No | Avoid |
| `page.fill(sel, value)` | ❌ No (no keyboard events) | Prefer page.type() |

This applies to any custom plugin or automation code running alongside CloakBrowser.

title: fix: ensure pw.stop() runs even if browser.close() raises or is cancelled
body:
Greetings from https://github.com/dgtlmoon/changedetection.io <3

**Problem - Session cleanups can be improved**

All four launch functions patch browser.close() / context.close() to also call pw.stop(), which is the right approach. However the patched functions have no error handling:

```
  async def _close_with_cleanup() -> None:
      await _original_close()   # if this raises or is CancelledError...
      await pw.stop()           # ...this line is never reached
```

This means the Playwright Node.js subprocess can be left running if:

- The Chromium process hangs and the caller uses asyncio.wait_for(browser.close(), timeout=N)  the timeout cancels the coroutine with CancelledError before pw.stop() runs
- _original_close() raises any exception (renderer crash, already-closed browser, etc.)

The result is an orphaned playwright Node process, open DevTools sockets, and /tmp/playwright-* profile directories that are only cleaned up when that process eventually dies on its own.

**Fix**

Wrap each patched cleanup function in try/finally so pw.stop() is guaranteed to run regardless of what _original_close() does:

```
  # Before
  async def _close_with_cleanup() -> None:
      await _original_close()
      await pw.stop()

  # After
  async def _close_with_cleanup() -> None:
      try:
          await _original_close()
      finally:
          await pw.stop()
```

Same one-line change applies to the sync variants (launch, launch_persistent_context, launch_persistent_context_async, launch_context).

Why this matters in practice

Callers that defensively wrap browser.close() with a timeout — which is the correct thing to do for a hung page — currently get a resource leak as a side-effect of doing the right thing:

```
  # Caller does the right thing...
  try:
      await asyncio.wait_for(browser.close(), timeout=5.0)
  except asyncio.TimeoutError:
      pass
  # ...but pw.stop() was never called, playwright process stays alive
```
After this fix, pw.stop() runs in all cases.

title: Feature request: spoof navigator.plugins (Plugins Length = 0 detected by bot detectors)
body:
## Problem

Bot detection sites like [bot.sannysoft.com](https://bot.sannysoft.com) flag CloakBrowser sessions because `navigator.plugins.length === 0`. Two checks fail:

1. **Plugins Length (Old)**: Fails when `navigator.plugins.length === 0`
2. **Plugins is of type PluginArray**: Fails if `navigator.plugins` is not `instanceof PluginArray`, length is 0, or `navigator.plugins[0].toString() !== '[object Plugin]'`

### Detection code (from bot.sannysoft.com)

```javascript
// Plugins Length check
if (navigator.plugins.length === 0) {
  // FAIL - flagged as bot
}

// Plugins type check
if (!(navigator.plugins instanceof PluginArray) || 
    navigator.plugins.length === 0 || 
    window.navigator.plugins[0].toString() !== '[object Plugin]') {
  // FAIL - flagged as bot
}
```

## Root cause

In containerized/headless Chrome, the built-in plugins (PDF Viewer, Chrome PDF Plugin, Chromium PDF Plugin, etc.) are not available because the component extensions that provide them aren't installed. A real desktop Chrome always has these plugins.

A typical real Chrome reports 5 plugins:
- PDF Viewer
- Chrome PDF Plugin  
- Chromium PDF Plugin
- Microsoft Edge PDF Plugin (Edge only)
- Native Client

## Requested feature

Add a `--fingerprint-plugins` flag (or include plugin spoofing by default) that injects realistic `Plugin` and `MimeType` objects into `navigator.plugins` at the C++ level, similar to how `--fingerprint-gpu-vendor` and `--fingerprint-gpu-renderer` work for WebGL.

The spoofed plugins should:
- Return correct `length` (e.g., 5 for Chrome)
- Be proper `instanceof PluginArray`
- Have each entry return `[object Plugin]` from `.toString()`
- Include realistic `MimeType` entries (e.g., `application/pdf`)
- Survive prototype chain checks (which is why JS-level spoofing is fragile)

## Environment

- CloakBrowser version: 0.3.15
- Platform: linux-x64 (Docker container)
- Backend: patchright

title: Incognito detection in Docker/Xvfb not fixed in v0.3.14
body:
**Problem**

After updating from v0.3.12 to v0.3.14, BrowserScan.net reports the browser as incognito when running inside Docker with Xvfb, similar to #44.

The only abnormal signal I could identify is the reported storage quota. All three storage quota APIs return unusually low values (~0.45–0.77 GB, persistent = 0 GB), even though the browser is launched with a persistent profile directory.

Observed values:

┌──────────────────────────────┬──────────────┐
│ API │ Observed │
├──────────────────────────────┼──────────────┤
│ navigator.storage.estimate() │ 0.45–0.77 GB │
│ webkitTemporaryStorage │ 0.45–0.77 GB │
│ webkitPersistentStorage │ 0 GB │
└──────────────────────────────┴──────────────┘

All other storage-related signals I tested appear normal and do not suggest incognito mode:

FileSystem API

IndexedDB

Cache API

ServiceWorker

I cannot prove that BrowserScan relies solely on storage quota for its incognito verdict, but among the tested signals this is the only one that remains obviously abnormal.

**Reproduction**

from cloakbrowser import launch_persistent_context

context = launch_persistent_context(
user_data_dir="/app/cloak_profile",
headless=False,
args=["--fingerprint=12345"],
)

page = context.pages[0] if context.pages else context.new_page()
page.goto("https://www.browserscan.net/
", timeout=60000)

result = page.evaluate("""async () => {
const est = await navigator.storage.estimate();
return {
quota: est.quota,
quota_gb: (est.quota / 1024 / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(2)
};
}""")

print(result)

Example output:

{'quota_gb': '0.51'}

**What I tested**

launch(), launch_context(), and launch_persistent_context() → same result

Minimal flags (--fingerprint=<seed> only) → same result

No custom flags at all → same result

tmpfs with 300 GB for the profile directory → no change

body:
[Bug] --fingerprint seed has no effect on Windows x64 — is this expected?

Environment

  • CloakBrowser: v0.3.11 (pip install cloakbrowser)
  • Binary: Chromium 145.0.7632.109 (Windows x64)
    (Windows binary has not been updated since v0.3.3; releases .159, .159.2, .159.3 are Linux-only per release notes)
  • OS: Windows 11 x64 (25H2)
  • Python: 3.10
  • Backend: Playwright (default)

Summary

The --fingerprint seed reaches the binary (confirmed via chrome://version) but has no observable effect on Windows. Canvas, WebGL render, audio, and client rects are bitwise identical across different seeds.

The README describes seed behavior without a platform caveat:

"--fingerprint: Master seed for canvas, WebGL, audio, fonts, client rects"
"Every launch produces a fresh, coherent identity."
"Run multiple instances with different fingerprint seeds on different ports — each gets unique canvas noise, client rects, and other browser signals."

Is this a known limitation of the Windows binary, or a bug?

Confirmed: seed reaches the binary

chrome://version command line shows:

--fingerprint=11111
--fingerprint-platform=windows
--fingerprint-gpu-vendor="Google Inc. (NVIDIA)"
--fingerprint-gpu-renderer="ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce
  RTX 3070 (0x00002484) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)"

The wrapper passes the flag. The binary receives it.

Reproduction

3 separate Chromium processes (launch → extract → close):

  1. launch(args=["--fingerprint=11111"])
  2. launch(args=["--fingerprint=99999"])
  3. launch(args=["--fingerprint=11111"]) — repeat

Extracted canvas toDataURL on http://example.com.

Results

seed=11111:         length=4218  last40=...yHvcsLvTE6kAAAAASUVORK5CYII=
seed=99999:         length=4218  last40=...yHvcsLvTE6kAAAAASUVORK5CYII=
seed=11111 (again): length=4218  last40=...yHvcsLvTE6kAAAAASUVORK5CYII=

seed=11111 == seed=99999: canvas is bitwise identical.

Full audit (4 launches including default/no seed) — all values identical:

Parameter seed=11111 seed=99999 11111 repeat no seed
Canvas toDataURL length 4218 identical identical identical
WebGL render toDataURL length 4462 identical identical identical
Audio sum (4500-5000) 124.04347527516074 identical identical identical
Audio sample 4500 -0.10808052122592926 identical identical identical
Client rect Arial width 327.140625 identical identical identical
Client rect Times width 302.171875 identical identical identical
GPU renderer RTX 3070 (0x00002484) identical identical identical
Screen 1920×1080 identical identical identical
HW concurrency 8 identical identical identical
deviceMemory 8 identical identical identical

Seed changes: nothing.

Context from releases

All binary releases since v0.3.3 ship Linux x64 only:

v145.0.7632.159.3: "macOS and Windows remain on v145.0.7632.109.2"
v145.0.7632.159.2: "macOS and Windows remain on v145.0.7632.109.2"
v145.0.7632.159:   "macOS and Windows remain on v145.0.7632.109.2"

Linux is now on .159.3 with 31 patches. Windows is on .109.2. CHANGELOG v0.3.10 mentions "Fix fingerprint consistency in offline audio rendering" which shipped only in the Linux build.

title: feat(proxy): add ProxyRotator with multi-strategy rotation, health tracking, and auto-failover
body:
## Summary

Adds `ProxyRotator` — a thread-safe proxy pool with automatic rotation, health tracking, and failover for both Python and JavaScript/TypeScript.

## Background

The design was inspired by [Scrapling's ProxyRotator](https://github.com/D4Vinci/Scrapling), which provides cyclic proxy rotation with custom strategy callbacks for its spider framework. CloakBrowser's implementation is written from scratch and differs significantly:

- **Built-in strategies** instead of callback-based: four strategies are built in (round-robin, random, least-used, least-failures) rather than requiring the user to write a strategy function.
- **Health tracking with automatic cooldown:** Scrapling's rotator is stateless — it just cycles through a list. Ours tracks per-proxy failure counts, consecutive failures, and automatically sidelines broken proxies for a configurable cooldown period, then recovers them.
- **Sticky sessions:** Scrapling has no concept of reusing the same proxy for N consecutive requests. Ours supports `sticky_count` to keep the same proxy for a batch of requests (useful for session-based websites).
- **Dynamic pool management:** proxies can be added/removed at runtime without restarting. Scrapling's list is static.
- **Thread safety:** all operations are protected by `threading.Lock` (Python). Scrapling's rotator is not thread-safe.
- **Credential masking:** `stats()` and all log output automatically mask usernames and passwords. Scrapling does not mask credentials.
- **SOCKS5 validation:** rejects `socks5://user:pass@host:port` at construction time with a clear error message, because Chromium does not support SOCKS5 authentication. This prevents a confusing launch-time crash.
- **Bare proxy format:** accepts `user:pass@host:port` without a scheme prefix, which is common in proxy provider dashboards.
- **Dual implementation:** both Python and TypeScript, matching CloakBrowser's architecture. Scrapling is Python-only.
- **Context manager / withSession:** auto-reports success on normal return, failure on exception. Scrapling relies on the spider framework's retry system instead.

In short: Scrapling's ProxyRotator was the starting inspiration for "a class that rotates proxies," but the actual implementation, API, and feature set are entirely different and written from scratch for CloakBrowser's use case (standalone browser automation, not a spider framework).

## Features

### Rotation Strategies

- **round-robin** (default): cycles through proxies in order, skipping any that are in cooldown
- **random**: picks a random available proxy each time
- **least-used**: picks the proxy with the fewest total uses (distributes load evenly)
- **least-failures**: picks the proxy with the fewest total failures (avoids unreliable proxies)

### Health Tracking

Each proxy tracks: `use_count`, `fail_count`, `consecutive_fails`, `last_used`, `last_failed`, `cooldown_until`.

When a proxy reaches `max_failures` consecutive failures (default: 3), it is automatically placed on cooldown for `cooldown` seconds (default: 300). During cooldown it is skipped by all strategies. When cooldown expires, the proxy becomes available again. Calling `report_success()` immediately resets the consecutive failure counter and removes any cooldown.

If all proxies are in cooldown simultaneously, `next()` raises `RuntimeError` with a clear message.

### Sticky Sessions

Set `sticky_count=N` to reuse the same proxy for N consecutive `next()` calls before rotating. Useful for websites that track sessions by IP. If the sticky proxy fails, rotation is forced immediately.

### Dynamic Pool

- `add(proxy)` — add a proxy to the pool at runtime
- `remove(proxy)` — remove a proxy (raises if not found or would empty the pool)
- Round-robin index is clamped after removal to prevent index errors
- Sticky state is cleared if the sticky proxy is removed

### Context Manager / withSession

Python:
```python
with rotator.session() as proxy:
    browser = launch(proxy=proxy)
    # if this block raises, report_failure() is called automatically
    # if it completes normally, report_success() is called
```

JavaScript:
```typescript
await rotator.withSession(async (proxy) => {
    const browser = await launch({ proxy });
    // same auto-reporting behavior
});
```

### Credential Masking

`stats()` output and all internal logging automatically masks credentials:
- `http://user:pass@host:8080` → `http://***:***@host:8080`
- `user:pass@host:8080` (bare format) → `***:***@host:8080`
- `socks5://host:8080` (no creds) → unchanged
- Dict key format `http://host:8080||username` → `http://host:8080||***`

### SOCKS5 Validation

Chromium does not support SOCKS5 proxy authentication. Rather than failing with a cryptic error at browser launch time, `ProxyRotator` validates proxies at construction and `add()` time:

- `socks5://host:port` — accepted (no auth)
- `socks5://user:pass@host:port` — raises `ValueError` immediately
- `{"server": "socks5://host:port", "username": "u", "password": "p"}` — raises `ValueError` immediately

### Integration with launch()

```python
from cloakbrowser import ProxyRotator, launch

rotator = ProxyRotator([
    "http://user:pass@proxy1:8080",
    "http://user:pass@proxy2:8080",
], strategy="round_robin")

browser = launch(proxy=rotator.next())
page = browser.new_page()
page.goto("https://example.com")
rotator.report_success(rotator.current())
browser.close()
```

The `current()` method returns the proxy that was last selected by `next()`, so you can report success/failure after using it.

## API Reference

### Python (`cloakbrowser.proxy_rotator`)

```python
class ProxyRotator:
    def __init__(self, proxies, strategy="round_robin", cooldown=300.0, max_failures=3, sticky_count=1)
    def next(self) -> str | dict
    def current(self) -> str | dict | None
    def report_success(self, proxy) -> None
    def report_failure(self, proxy) -> None
    def session(self) -> ContextManager[str | dict]
    def stats(self) -> list[dict]
    def reset(self) -> None
    def add(self, proxy) -> None
    def remove(self, proxy) -> None
    @property
    def available_count(self) -> int
```

### JavaScript/TypeScript (`cloakbrowser`)

```typescript
class ProxyRotator {
    constructor(proxies: ProxyValue[], options?: ProxyRotatorOptions)
    next(): ProxyValue
    current(): ProxyValue | null
    reportSuccess(proxy: ProxyValue): void
    reportFailure(proxy: ProxyValue): void
    withSession<T>(fn: (proxy: ProxyValue) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
    stats(): ProxyStats[]
    reset(): void
    add(proxy: ProxyValue): void
    remove(proxy: ProxyValue): void
    get availableCount(): number
    get size(): number
    static proxyKey(proxy: ProxyValue): string
}
```

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| Python unit (pytest) | 49 | ✅ |
| JS unit (vitest) | 45 | ✅ |
| Python real-proxy integration | 7 | ✅ |
| JS real-proxy integration | 9 | ✅ |
| **Total** | **110** | **✅** |

Tests cover: all four strategies, health tracking with cooldown expiration, sticky sessions, context manager success/failure paths, dynamic pool add/remove edge cases, credential masking for all proxy formats, SOCKS5 validation, thread safety (10 threads × 100 calls), bare proxy format handling, round-robin index clamping after removal, and real browser integration (headless Chromium verifying external IP via ipify.org).

## Files

### Added
- `cloakbrowser/proxy_rotator.py` — Python implementation
- `js/src/proxy-rotator.ts` — TypeScript implementation
- `tests/test_proxy_rotator.py` — Python unit tests (49 tests)
- `js/tests/proxy-rotator.test.ts` — JS unit tests (45 tests)
- `tests/test_proxy_real.py` — Python real-proxy integration tests
- `tests/test_proxy_real.mjs` — JS real-proxy integration tests
- `examples/proxy_rotation.py` — Python usage example
- `examples/proxy_verify.py` — Python proxy verification script
- `js/examples/proxy-rotation.ts` — TypeScript usage example

### Modified
- `cloakbrowser/__init__.py` — export ProxyRotator
- `cloakbrowser/browser.py` — integrate rotator with launch()
- `js/src/index.ts` — export ProxyRotator, maskProxy, resolveProxyRotator
- `js/src/proxy.ts` — integrate rotator resolution
- `js/src/types.ts` — add ProxyRotator-related types
- `js/src/playwright.ts` — resolve rotator in Playwright launcher
- `js/src/puppeteer.ts` — resolve rotator in Puppeteer launcher
- `tests/test_proxy.py` — add bare proxy format parsing tests

title: WebGL fingerprint noise detected as spoofed by detection sites
body: ## Problem Detection sites identify CloakBrowser's WebGL noise patch as spoofing. **webbrowsertools.com/webgl-fingerprint/** reports: - `Is browser webgl fingerprint spoofed: true` - `Is fingerprint spoofed by persistent noise: true` **BrowserScan** flags `WebGL exception (-5%)`, likely using a similar technique. ## How detection works The site renders the same scene using different methods and compares hashes: | Method | Hash | | --- | --- | | Red solid box | `7063ee752835a549...` | | Before DOM load (random image with color mixing) | `bb04eae70ea1dc23...` | | After DOM load (random image with color mixing) | `bb04eae70ea1dc23...` | The two "random image" hashes match (persistent noise — same seed), but the "red solid box" hash differs. This means the noise function produces different offsets for different rendering pipelines, which is trivially detected by comparing outputs across methods. ## Expected behavior A normal (non-spoofed) browser produces consistent hashes across all rendering methods for the same canvas context. The noise patch should do the same. ## Suggested fix 1. Make the noise function dependent on the **canvas context + session seed only**, not on the rendering method/call path. This way, all methods that render to the same canvas produce the same noise offset, and cross-method comparison yields identical hashes. 2. Alternatively, apply noise at the **readback stage** (`readPixels`, `toDataURL`, `toBlob`) rather than at the draw stage, so it doesn't matter which draw calls were used — the noise is added once when pixels are read. ## Environment - CloakBrowser v0.3.7 (Windows) - Real GPU: Intel UHD Graphics (0x000046A3) - Tested with `--fingerprint-gpu-vendor` and `--fingerprint-gpu-renderer` set to real GPU values (not spoofed) - Detection persists regardless of GPU string — the issue is the noise patch itself ## Screenshots

title: fix(python): reduce download connect timeout to 10s, read to 60s for …
body:
## Problem

When the primary download server (cloakbrowser.dev) is unreachable, `httpx.stream()` waits the full `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` (600 seconds / 10 minutes) before falling back to GitHub Releases. First-time users on any platform sit staring at a frozen terminal for 10+ minutes.

## Root cause

`DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT = 600.0` is a single float, which httpx applies to **all** phases equally — connect, read, write, pool. A dead server that accepts the TCP connection but never sends data holds the stream open for the full 600s on the read phase.

## Fix

Replace the single float with granular timeouts:

```python
DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT = httpx.Timeout(connect=10.0, read=60.0, write=10.0, pool=10.0)
```

- **connect=10s** — fail fast if server doesn't accept connection
- **read=60s** — if server connects but sends no data, fail after 60s (not 600s)
- **write/pool=10s** — reasonable defaults

Note: `read=60s` is conservative on purpose — slower connections downloading the 526 MB binary won't be interrupted since the read timer resets with each received chunk. This could be reduced further (e.g. `read=30s`) if needed.

## Before / After

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Primary down → fallback → complete | ~692s (11.5 min) | ~170s (2.8 min) |
| Primary works → complete | ~90s | ~90s (unchanged) |

Tested on Windows 11, Python 3.10, cloakbrowser 0.3.8.

## Note

The JS wrapper had a related issue (PR #23 — file handle leak causing extraction failure). The Python wrapper doesn't have the file handle bug (context manager `with open()` closes correctly), but the timeout makes first-run UX equally bad when the primary server is down.

title: [Feature] Companion package for behavioral bot detection: cloakbrowser-human
body:
Hey! This is a **companion package, not a replacement** — CloakBrowser remains the core, this just adds a behavioral layer on top. It's also a **temporary community-built solution** while we wait for native behavioral humanization in CloakBrowser. It works now and passes current detection benchmarks, but the proper long-term fix belongs in the CloakBrowser binary itself — especially for signals like coalesced pointer events that can't be fully addressed from a JS wrapper. ## Problem CloakBrowser handles fingerprint-based detection perfectly — WebDriver, CDP, headless flags, GPU inconsistencies. But some sites now analyze behavioral signals: mouse movement patterns, typing speed, click coordinates, scroll velocity. Plain Playwright calls produce instant, straight-line interactions that get flagged. ## Solution [cloakbrowser-human](https://github.com/evelaa123/cloakbrowser-human) — a drop-in wrapper that replaces Playwright methods with human-like implementations. Change one import line, everything else stays the same. ```javascript // Before import { launch } from 'cloakbrowser'; // After import { launch } from 'cloakbrowser-human'; ``` ## What it does - Mouse: Bezier curves with easing, wobble, burst patterns, 15% overshoot chance - Keyboard: Full keydown/hold/keyup per character, Shift wrapping, random "thinking" pauses - Scroll: mouse.wheel() with accelerate → cruise → decelerate pattern - Clicks: Realistic aim points (left third for inputs, center for buttons), mousedown/hold/mouseup timing - Coalesced events patch (experimental) ## Test results ## Demo
Without wrapper (bot) With wrapper (human)
On [deviceandbrowserinfo.com/are_you_a_bot_interactions](https://deviceandbrowserinfo.com/are_you_a_bot_interactions): Without wrapper: `isBot: true`, `suspiciousClientSideBehavior: true`, `superHumanSpeed: true` With wrapper: `isBot: false` — all 23 detection flags return `false`. ## Install ```bash npm install cloakbrowser-human pip install cloakbrowser-human ``` Works with JS and Python. Two presets: `default` (normal speed) and `careful` (slower, more deliberate). ## What can't be fixed from a wrapper Coalesced pointer events: human average is 2.7 points per event, CDP produces exactly 1. The current JS patch via `page.evaluate()` fabricates fake points but advanced anti-fraud can detect it via `toString()`, cross-origin iframes, or web workers. A real fix requires a Chromium source patch in `pointer_event_manager.cc`. Full docs and demo: https://github.com/evelaa123/cloakbrowser-human Happy to discuss and collaborate!

title: add_init_script() breaks proxy when using patchright (Python only)
body:
## Bug

In the Python package, `page.add_init_script()` causes `net::ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED` when using an HTTP proxy with authentication. This is a patchright bug, not CloakBrowser, but affects all Python users who combine proxy + `add_init_script`.

The **JS/Node.js** package is **not affected** — `addInitScript` + proxy works fine.

## Reproduction

```python
from cloakbrowser import launch

proxy = "http://user:pass@host:port"

# ✅ Works
b1 = launch(headless=True, proxy=proxy)
p1 = b1.new_page()
p1.goto("https://httpbin.org/ip")
print(p1.evaluate("document.body.innerText"))  # proxy IP
b1.close()

# ❌ Fails
b2 = launch(headless=True, proxy=proxy)
p2 = b2.new_page()
p2.add_init_script("window.__test = true;")
p2.goto("https://httpbin.org/ip")  # ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED
b2.close()
```

Confirmed same bug with patchright directly (without CloakBrowser wrapper):

```python
from patchright.sync_api import sync_playwright

proxy = {"server": "http://host:port", "username": "user", "password": "pass"}

with sync_playwright() as pw:
    b = pw.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    ctx = b.new_context(proxy=proxy)
    p = ctx.new_page()
    p.add_init_script("window.__test = true;")
    p.goto("https://httpbin.org/ip")  # ❌ ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED
    b.close()
```

JS equivalent works fine:

```javascript
import { launch } from 'cloakbrowser';

const b = await launch({ headless: true, proxy: 'http://user:pass@host:port' });
const p = await b.newPage();
await p.addInitScript('window.__test = true;');
await p.goto('https://httpbin.org/ip');  // ✅ Works
await b.close();
```

## Root cause

Bug is in **patchright-python**, not in CloakBrowser or the Chromium binary.

## Workaround

Use `page.evaluate()` after `page.goto()` instead of `add_init_script()`:

```python
b = launch(headless=True, proxy="http://user:pass@host:port")
p = b.new_page()
p.goto("https://httpbin.org/ip")  # ✅ works
p.evaluate("window.__test = true;")  # inject after load
```

Limitation: `page.evaluate()` runs after page load, so scripts cannot be injected before the page's own JS executes.

## Environment

- cloakbrowser: 0.3.7
- patchright: latest (pip)
- Python: 3.10
- OS: Windows 11
- Chromium binary: 145.0.7632.109.2
- Proxy: HTTP with username/password auth

title: proxy_bypass option not supported — no way to set Playwright's proxy.bypass field
body:
Playwright's chromium.launch() accepts a proxy dict with a bypass field that allows specifying a comma-separated list of domains that should bypass the proxy:

```python
# Playwright native API

browser = pw.chromium.launch(
    proxy={
        "server": "http://proxy:8080",
        "username": "user",
        "password": "pass",
        "bypass": ".google.com,localhost",
    }
)

# proxy : Union[{server: str, bypass: Union[str, None], username: Union[str, None], password: Union[str, None]}, None]
```
However, cloakbrowser's `launch()` / `launch_async()` / `launch_context()` functions only accept proxy as a plain URL string (str| None). The internal helper _build_proxy_kwargs parses this string into a Playwright proxy dict with server, username, and password, but has no mechanism to include the bypass field.

title: fix(windows): zip extraction fails when primary download server is down
body:
Problem

On Windows, ensureBinary() consistently fails with “file in use by another process” when extracting the downloaded Chromium zip. This happens every time the primary download server (cloakbrowser.dev) is unavailable and the fallback to GitHub Releases is triggered.

The error appears as:

The process cannot access the file
'C:\Users\...\.cloakbrowser\_download_xxx.zip'
because it is being used by another process.

This makes CloakBrowser completely unusable on first install for any Windows user when the primary CDN is down — which currently happens consistently (terminated error on every attempt).

Root cause

The bug is in downloadFile() inside downloadAndExtract(). Here is the exact sequence:

Step 1 — downloadFile(primaryUrl, tmpPath) is called:

  • createWriteStream(tmpPath) opens a file handle (handle #1)
  • fetch(primaryUrl) starts but the server is down
  • The fetch throws terminated
  • The function exits via the thrown error
  • fileStream is never closed or destroyed — handle #1 is leaked

Step 2 — downloadFile(fallbackUrl, tmpPath) is called on the same tmpPath:

  • createWriteStream(tmpPath) opens a NEW file handle (handle #2) on the same file
  • fetch(fallbackUrl) succeeds, 526 MB downloaded
  • fileStream.end(() => resolve()) is called — handle #2 is closed
  • Download completes successfully

Step 3 — extractArchive(tmpPath, ...) is called:

  • extractZip() spawns PowerShell to extract the zip
  • PowerShell tries to open the file but handle #1 from Step 1 is still open
  • Windows returns ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION
  • Extraction fails, chromium-145.0.7632.109.2 directory is empty
  • ensureBinary() throws “binary not found”

Visual flow:

downloadFile(primaryUrl, tmpPath)
  └─ createWriteStream(tmpPath)    → handle #1 OPENED
  └─ fetch(primaryUrl)             → FAILS (terminated)
  └─ throw                         → handle #1 NEVER CLOSED ← BUG

downloadFile(fallbackUrl, tmpPath)
  └─ createWriteStream(tmpPath)    → handle #2 OPENED
  └─ fetch(fallbackUrl)            → OK (526 MB)
  └─ fileStream.end(callback)      → handle #2 CLOSED

extractZip(tmpPath, destDir)
  └─ PowerShell opens tmpPath      → BLOCKED by handle #1
  └─ ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION       → EXTRACTION FAILS

Additional issue

Even when the primary server works (no fallback), there is a secondary problem: downloadFile() waits for the finish event via fileStream.end(() => resolve()). On Windows, finish fires before the OS fully releases the file handle. The close event is the correct signal that the file descriptor is freed.

Fix

Two changes in downloadFile():

1. Destroy fileStream on error (fixes the primary bug):
The createWriteStream is now created before the try block, and the catch handler calls fileStream.destroy() followed by waiting for the close event. This guarantees the OS handle is released even when the download fails.

2. Wait for close instead of finish on success (fixes secondary issue):
Changed from fileStream.end(() => resolve()) (listens for finish) to fileStream.end() + fileStream.on("close", () => resolve()). The close event fires after the file descriptor is fully released by the OS.

3. Safety delay in extractZip() (defense in depth):
Added a 500ms delay before extraction and switched from Expand-Archive to ZipFile.ExtractToDirectory for more predictable behavior on PowerShell 5.1.

Reproduction

Save as test-repro.mjs and run with node test-repro.mjs on Windows:

import fs from 'node:fs';
import { createWriteStream } from 'node:fs';
import { execSync } from 'node:child_process';
import path from 'node:path';

const dir = path.join(process.env.USERPROFILE, '.cloakbrowser');
fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
const zip = path.join(dir, '_download_repro.zip');
const dest = path.join(dir, 'repro-extract');
const GITHUB_URL = 'https://github.com/CloakHQ/cloakbrowser/releases/download/chromium-v145.0.7632.109.2/cloakbrowser-windows-x64.zip';
const DEAD_URL = 'https://cloakbrowser.dev/chromium-v145.0.7632.109.2/cloakbrowser-windows-x64.zip';

async function downloadFile(url, filepath) {
  const fileStream = createWriteStream(filepath);
  const resp = await fetch(url, { redirect: 'follow' });
  if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${resp.status}`);
  const reader = resp.body.getReader();
  while (true) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    fileStream.write(value);
  }
  await new Promise((res, rej) => { fileStream.end(() => res()); fileStream.on('error', rej); });
}

console.log('Step 1: Primary download (will fail)...');
try { await downloadFile(DEAD_URL, zip); }
catch (e) { console.log('  Failed:', e.message); }

console.log('Step 2: Fallback download (same file path)...');
await downloadFile(GITHUB_URL, zip);
console.log('  Done:', Math.round(fs.statSync(zip).size / 1024 / 1024), 'MB');

console.log('Step 3: Extract...');
if (fs.existsSync(dest)) fs.rmSync(dest, { recursive: true, force: true });
fs.mkdirSync(dest, { recursive: true });
try {
  execSync(`powershell -NoProfile -Command "Expand-Archive -Path '${zip}' -DestinationPath '${dest}' -Force"`, { timeout: 120000 });
  console.log('  Result: SUCCESS');
} catch {
  console.log('  Result: FAILED — file locked by leaked handle from Step 1');
}

if (fs.existsSync(dest)) fs.rmSync(dest, { recursive: true, force: true });
try { fs.unlinkSync(zip); } catch {}

Expected output on current version:

Step 1: Primary download (will fail)...
  Failed: terminated
Step 2: Fallback download (same file path)...
  Done: 526 MB
Step 3: Extract...
  Result: FAILED — file locked by leaked handle from Step 1

Actual test logs

Original ensureBinary() from npm — FAIL (ran 3 times, failed every time):

PS> node -e "import('cloakbrowser').then(m => m.ensureBinary()).then(p => console.log('PASS:', p)).catch(e => console.log('FAIL:', e.message.substring(0, 300)))"

title: feat: add launchPersistentContext() to avoid incognito detection
body:
## Summary

Adds `launchPersistentContext()` — a new exported function that wraps Playwright's `chromium.launchPersistentContext()` with the same stealth defaults, geoip resolution, and proxy handling that `launch()` already provides.

## Problem

`launch()` and `launchContext()` both use `browser.launch()` + `browser.newContext()`, which creates incognito/ephemeral contexts. Detection services like BrowserScan flag this as "Incognito mode: Yes" with a -10% penalty, undermining the stealth that CloakBrowser's C++ patches provide.

The only way to get a non-incognito context in Playwright is `chromium.launchPersistentContext()` with a `userDataDir`. Until now, this required importing internal `dist/` modules directly — undocumented and fragile.

## Changes

- **js/src/types.ts** — added `LaunchPersistentContextOptions` interface
- **js/src/playwright.ts** — added `launchPersistentContext()` function
- **js/src/index.ts** — exported the new function and type

## Usage

    import { launchPersistentContext } from 'cloakbrowser';

    const context = await launchPersistentContext({
      userDataDir: './chrome-profile',
      headless: false,
      proxy: 'http://user:pass@host:port',
      geoip: true,
    });

    const page = context.pages()[0] || await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('https://example.com');
    await context.close();

## Test results

Tested on Windows 11, Node.js 18.20.4, cloakbrowser 0.3.4, Chromium 145.0.7632.109.2:

- BrowserScan incognito detection: Yes → No (-10% penalty removed)
- Cookies and localStorage persist across launches
- All existing stealth args, geoip, and proxy handling work unchanged
- TypeScript compiles without errors

Windows x64 binary v145.0.7632.109.2: side-by-side configuration error — missing assembly manifest
body:
## Bug Report

The Windows x64 binary (`cloakbrowser-windows-x64.zip`, v145.0.7632.109.2) cannot launch on Windows 11. It fails immediately with a side-by-side configuration error.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 11 Pro, build 26200
- **CPU**: Intel 12th Gen (Alder Lake), x86_64
- **GPU**: NVIDIA RTX 3050 Ti
- **Node.js**: v18.20.4
- **Python**: 3.10
- **cloakbrowser**: v0.3.4 (tested via both `npm` and `pip`)
- **VC++ Redistributable**: 2015-2022 x64 installed

## Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install cloakbrowser playwright-core`
2. Binary auto-downloads successfully (526 MB, SHA-256 verified)
3. Run:
```js
import { launch } from 'cloakbrowser';
const browser = await launch({ headless: false });
```
4. Error: `browserType.launch: spawn UNKNOWN`

Launching `chrome.exe` directly also fails:
```
chrome.exe --version
→ "The application has failed to start because its side-by-side configuration is incorrect."
```

## Root cause analysis (sxstrace)

Ran `sxstrace` as admin. The embedded manifest in `chrome.exe` references a non-existent assembly:

```
Reference: 145.0.7632.109,language="*",type="win32",version="145.0.7632.109"
```

Windows tries to resolve it and fails:

```
INFO: Resolving reference 145.0.7632.109,language="*",type="win32",version="145.0.7632.109"
  INFO: Assembly not found in WinSxS.
  INFO: Manifest probe: ...\145.0.7632.109.DLL — not found
  INFO: Manifest probe: ...\145.0.7632.109.MANIFEST — not found
  INFO: Manifest probe: ...\145.0.7632.109\145.0.7632.109.DLL — not found
  INFO: Manifest probe: ...\145.0.7632.109\145.0.7632.109.MANIFEST — not found
  ERROR: Cannot resolve reference 145.0.7632.109,language="*",type="win32",version="145.0.7632.109"
INFO: Activation context generation failed.
```

The `Microsoft.Windows.Common-Controls` dependency resolves fine. Only the `145.0.7632.109` assembly reference is broken.

## What I tried

- ✅ VC++ Redistributable 2010, 2012, 2013, 2015-2022 — all installed
- ✅ Windows Defender exclusion added for `~/.cloakbrowser/`
- ✅ Created external `chrome.exe.manifest` without the bad dependency — no effect (embedded manifest takes precedence)
- ✅ Re-downloaded zip from GitHub Releases — same result
- ✅ Verified file integrity — `chrome.exe` is 3,771 KB, SHA-256 checksum matches

## Expected behavior

`chrome.exe` should launch without requiring an external assembly manifest, same as the Linux and macOS builds.

## Suggestion

It looks like the Windows build embeds a manifest with a self-referencing assembly dependency (`145.0.7632.109` referencing itself). This dependency should either be removed from the manifest or the corresponding `.manifest` file should be included in the zip alongside `chrome.exe`.

## Additional context

This is the first Windows x64 release (shipped ~March 3, 2026). Linux x64 and macOS builds work correctly. The issue affects both Node.js and Python wrappers since both use the same binary.

title: fix: include full Chromium runtime in Windows package, remove duplicate test
body:
## Summary

- **Windows packaging**: All 4 packaging locations (`build-deploy.yml`, `build-windows.ps1`, `build-windows.bat`, `WINDOWS_BUILD.md`) were only packaging `chrome.exe`. Chromium requires DLLs, `.bin`, `.pak`, `.dat`, and `locales/` to run. Updated tar command to include all required runtime files.
- **Duplicate test**: `test_windows_binary_path_with_version` was defined twice in `TestGetBinaryPath`. Python silently shadows the first definition, so only the second ran. The first copy was incomplete (missing `assert_called_with`), so it was removed.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_platform.py -v` — no duplicate test warnings, all pass
- [ ] `pytest tests/ -m "not slow" -v` — full suite passes
- [ ] Windows build CI: verify packaged archive contains DLLs and locales

title: Proxy authentication is not supported despite README claiming it is
body: The README states that custom proxies can be used: https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/blob/4e809b96780526f05f2ba520f2fd3b4cd0ed9759/README.md?plain=1#L424-L425 However, the current implementation of https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/blob/4e809b96780526f05f2ba520f2fd3b4cd0ed9759/cloakbrowser/browser.py#L220-L224 wraps the proxy string into Playwright's `{"proxy": {"server": proxy}}` format, which does **not** support authentication credentials embedded in the URL. https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/blob/4e809b96780526f05f2ba520f2fd3b4cd0ed9759/cloakbrowser/browser.py#L122-L130
